summary:
HOW IT WORKS TODAY. Topology: alliance and guild are separate tenants (own Postgres schemas); the control plane holds alliance_memberships (pending/active/left, one alliance per guild), alliance_shares (guild->alliance snapshot map), event_sync_links (canonical event <-> copies, sync_enabled flag), event_fanout_jobs/targets/assets (alliance->guild outbox), event_mirror_requests (guild->alliance retry outbox), event_participant_attributions, alliance_split_distribution_batches/items, alliance_role_grants/revocations. Background workers: ONE global task, events::fanout_worker::spawn (lib.rs:118), ticks every 15s and drains both event_fanout_targets and event_mirror_requests (fanout_worker.rs:32-49). Per-tenant battle_sync and event_sessions workers are NOT started for alliance tenants (tenant.rs:84, lib.rs:119-127). There is no worker for split distribution, share refresh, membership backfill, user/link sync or role reconciliation.
Event sync: (a) alliance-created event -> create_event enqueues a 'publish' job for the active-member snapshot and processes it inline (router.rs:1066-1085); copies are created per guild with comp+builds copied (fanout_worker.rs process_target). Later source mutations (update/start/cancel/uncancel/stop/archive/delete) call sync_source_change -> sync_owner_change_to_copies -> enqueue 'update'/'archive' job (lifecycle.rs:97-174, router.rs:1341-1361). (b) guild-created event with ping_alliance=true -> create_mirror inline (comp+builds+roster-role builds+split are shared via alliance_shares, one mirror event created), failure goes to event_mirror_requests with 12 attempts of backoff (router.rs:1101-1135, mirror_retry.rs). Later guild source mutations converge the mirror inline (lifecycle.rs:169-172, no outbox). Participation join/leave fans out synchronously in the HTTP request via sync_participation with durable guild attribution; there is no outbox for it. Copies reject management (assert_manageable_source_event). Alliance split distribution (alliance_distribution.rs) is a manual, idempotent, batch-tracked projection into guild ledgers, invoked only by POST /splits/{id}/complete. Registering an IGN on a guild or alliance Discord copies the user+link to the paired tenant best-effort and assigns Discord roles (albion/alliance_fanout.rs, errors swallowed).

SYNC MATRIX (A->G = alliance to member guilds, G->A = guild to alliance):
- Events create: A->G yes (outbox, retry, status endpoint); G->A only if ping_alliance=true (inline + mirror outbox, 12 attempts then manual /mirror-retry). Not G->G by design.
- Events update (title/time/caps/status/start/stop/cancel/archive): A->G yes via 'update'/'archive' job (but see alliance-3, alliance-9); G->A yes inline converge, NO retry outbox (error returned to caller). Comp change, roster roles, battles: A->G only on next update job (comp) / never (roster roles added later); G->A never (comp, roster roles, battles).
- Event auto-stop: NOT synced either way, alliance has no worker (alliance-4).
- Signups/roster participation (self join/leave): yes both directions, attribution-filtered, synchronous, no retry. Officer add/set/remove participant: NOT synced. Seat assignments/swaps/auto-fill: NOT synced (copies cannot even manage). Live web roster socket: not notified for peer tenants.
- Builds: G->A only by manual share (or implicitly via comp/event mirror), snapshot, no re-sync on edit/delete, stale reuse; A->G only implicitly as part of event copy (and duplicated, alliance-1); no explicit alliance->guild publish.
- Comps: same as builds. Comp edits in alliance/guild never propagate until manual re-share/next update job.
- Splits: G->A manual snapshot (read-only) or auto-snapshot at event-mirror creation (then writable and diverging); no later propagation of edits/bags/amounts. A->G: only the money projection (split_credit transactions into guild ledgers) on manual complete; no worker retry, no UI/bot surfacing.
- Bank: not synced; alliance reads live aggregates from active guild ledgers and proxies writes (read-through, fine). Alliance split payouts are projected into guild ledgers.
- Regear, warns, XP/progression, ranks, guild settings, roles/permissions, VODs, trials, applications, giveaways, tickets: NO alliance sync at all.
- Members/users: IGN register/link copied to paired tenant on /register|/link only (one-shot, best-effort, no backfill when a guild joins, no reconciliation on guild-membership changes, unlink removes only paired link); Discord roles (alliance hub role, Ally role) granted at register time only, recorded in alliance_role_grants, revoked on guild leave via retry-able revocation rows (only retried inside the leave request).
- Islands/tabs catalog: read live across member guilds for alliance tenants (splits/router.rs:854), no copy; fine.
- Battles: not synced; alliance has no battle sync worker, alliance scope reads live from AlbionBB.
- Membership lifecycle: join/accept performs no backfill (events, shares, users); leave disables event_sync_links, keeps shares and copies; no alliance-side expel endpoint.

The recurring root cause: the system has three distinct mechanisms (snapshot shares, event outbox, event mirror outbox) plus a few one-shot best-effort hooks, instead of one generic entity-sync engine with change triggers, retries and membership reconciliation. Everything not an event or a manual share simply is not synchronized.

findings.title: Every alliance event update/start/cancel job re-copies all comp builds into each guild as NEW build rows
findings.description: process_target runs copy_alliance_comp_to_tenant for every non-terminal operation (publish, update). The previous build mapping comes from load_build_id_map, which filters event_fanout_assets by the CURRENT job_id. Each update/start/cancel/stop creates a new job (idempotency key update:<updated_at>), so previous_build_ids is always empty and copy_build_graph inserts a brand-new build (items+spells) per comp entry per guild every time. The comp row is reused (previous_comp from the event copy) and re-pointed to the new builds, sync_roster_roles deletes and recreates roster roles, but existing event_participations/seat keys keep referencing the old build ids that are no longer in the comp. Result: guild build libraries fill with duplicates on every lifecycle change, participants' builds become orphaned from the comp (roster seat/assigned_build mismatches), and each update does N-guild x M-build x items x spells inserts in the request path (perf). Existing tests only exercise flash events on the update path (lifecycle.rs tests), so this is uncovered.
findings.fix: Make the build/comp mapping stable per (source_tenant, source_event, target_tenant, asset) instead of per job: load mapping across ALL jobs for the target (or key event_fanout_assets by source event + tenant, not job_id), or store source->destination origin ids on builds/comps in the destination (origin_tenant_id/origin_id columns) and upsert by origin. Only re-copy the comp when its version/updated_at changed. Add a test: publish then two updates must leave exactly the same number of builds in the guild.
findings.verify_note: Real. load_build_id_map filters by the current job_id (fanout_worker.rs:431-448). Update jobs use key update:<updated_at> (lifecycle.rs:155-161), and start/stop also go through sync_source_change as an Update operation. previous_builds is therefore empty on every non-publish job, and copy_build_graph inserts a new build with items and spells each time (alliance_share/service.rs:657-659). The comp row is reused and repointed. 'Cancel' is wrong: cancel becomes an Archive job, which returns early at fanout_worker.rs:151-164 before any comp copy. Duplicate build pollution and heavy inline work are real, but 'critical' is inflated because nothing is lost, so I rate it high. The orphaned-participant claim is plausible but not traced to a seat-key level.

findings.title: Alliance events with extra roster roles whose build is outside the comp can never fan out; copy is created but never linked
findings.description: create_event_roster_role accepts any existing build (extra roster role). copy_alliance_comp_to_tenant only returns a mapping for builds that are entries of the comp. sync_roster_roles then fails with Conflict 'source roster build N has no destination mapping' for any role whose build is not in the comp. The error occurs AFTER the destination event was created/converged but BEFORE link_copy_if_membership_active, so the target stays 'failed' (retried hourly forever, there is no max attempts on the fanout outbox) and the destination event is never inserted in event_sync_links. Consequences: participation/lifecycle sync for that guild never works, the guild shows an orphan 'copy' with source identity but no link (so assert_manageable_source_event lets guild officers edit it), and the fanout-status endpoint shows permanent failure. The guild-origin path (create_mirror) does handle extra roster builds via share_build, so the two directions are inconsistent. The test only uses a roster role whose build is also in the comp (fanout_worker.rs ~885-897).
findings.fix: In process_target, copy any roster-role build that is missing from the comp mapping with copy_build_graph (and record it in the asset map) before sync_roster_roles. Link the event first (idempotently) and treat roster-role sync as a retryable step after linking. Add a bounded attempt count / terminal 'failed' state to event_fanout_targets like event_mirror_requests has.
findings.verify_note: The defect is real. create_event_roster_role accepts any build (service.rs:2156-2195) and sync_roster_roles errors when a build has no mapping (fanout_worker.rs:364-390). The 'never linked' impact is overstated. CreateEventRequest has no roster roles, so extra roles are added after creation, usually after the inline publish has already linked the copy. The usual outcome is that every later update job converges content, then fails and retries hourly forever. Link failure only happens if a publish retry runs after a role was added. The extra-role recopy and the unbounded retry (alliance-16) are real. I rate it medium.

findings.title: Auto-stop is never synced and alliance events never auto-stop; next fanout update resurrects stopped guild copies
findings.description: event_sessions (auto-stop + battle linker) is spawned per guild tenant only; starts_sync_workers('alliance') is false. (1) An alliance-origin event that is started is never auto-stopped (no worker on the alliance tenant) and never battle-linked. (2) Each guild copy runs its own auto-stop (status 'live' + deadline copied from source by converge) and stops locally via stop_event_with_xp_policy without calling sync_source_change, so alliance source and sibling guilds stay 'live'. (3) Because converge_copy_to_source overwrites status/started_at/stopped_at/auto_stop_deadline from the source on every update job, the next alliance update (or retry) flips an auto_stopped guild copy back to 'live'. (4) For guild-origin events with ping_alliance, the guild auto-stops the source but the alliance mirror is never converged (also no worker on the alliance), so the mirror and its mirrored split (awaiting_event) stay live/awaiting forever; splits for alliance-owned events cannot be distributed until a human stops the event (alliance_distribution::complete requires event_has_ended).
findings.fix: Run a minimal control-plane/alliance-level lifecycle worker (auto-stop for alliance-owned events, and call sync_owner_change_to_copies after any auto-stop on a canonical event). In auto_stop, skip copies with sync_enabled links (like is_mirror_event) instead of stopping them locally, and after stopping a source call sync_owner_change_to_copies. Make converge never move a copy backwards out of a terminal state unless the source was explicitly uncancelled.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. starts_sync_workers excludes alliance tenants (tenant.rs:84-86) and lib.rs:119-127 skips them. auto_stop_expired_sessions calls stop_event_with_xp_policy locally with no sync_owner_change_to_copies (auto_stop.rs:50-67). converge_copy_to_source then sets status, started_at and auto_stop_deadline from the source (lifecycle.rs:79-84), so the next update flips an auto-stopped copy back to live. Slight overstatement on 'alliance events never auto-stop': the bot poller still stops live events through POST /stop once an occupied voice channel empties, but that depends on a bound voice channel. The deadline-based auto-stop does not run for alliance tenants.

findings.title: Bot mass/start/voice-channel flow on synchronized copies is rejected by the backend and loops every poll tick
findings.description: converge_copy_to_source explicitly says the Discord voice channel is tenant-local, but set_event_voice_channel/clear_event_voice_channel/start_event all call assert_manageable_source_event, which returns 403 for any copy with an enabled sync link. Every tenant poller auto-masses and auto-starts scheduled events at their time (checkEventLifecycle). On a guild copy of an alliance event (and on an alliance mirror of a guild event) massDiscordEvent creates a Discord voice channel, the PUT bind fails with 403, the channel is deleted, the error is swallowed and massedEvents is not updated, so it repeats every poll interval (channel create/delete churn, Discord rate limits, log noise); startDiscordEvent 403s on POST /start each tick. Guild members therefore never get a per-guild voice channel/start notice for alliance events, and the copy only flips to live when the source start propagates via an update job.
findings.fix: Allow the tenant-local operations (voice-channel bind/clear, discord thread/forum ids, vod, alliance_discord_message_id) on copies; keep assert_manageable_source_event only for content/lifecycle fields. In the bot, skip mass/start for events with is_synchronized_copy, and mark failures in massedEvents to avoid retry loops.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. set/clear voice channel and start_event all call assert_manageable_source_event (router.rs:1942, 1985, 2030), which 403s on any copy with an enabled link. checkEventLifecycle (poller.ts:1715-1745) calls massDiscordEvent, which creates the voice channel, fails the PUT, deletes the channel and throws. massedEvents is only pushed after success, so the loop repeats every tick. startDiscordEvent POSTs /start and hits the same 403. The bot only hides the buttons for copies (event.embed.ts:714-719) and does not skip the auto lifecycle.

findings.title: Officer participant management and seat assignments are never synchronized, and officer-added participants have no guild attribution (blocks alliance split payout)
findings.description: sync_participation is only called from the self-service participate/cancel handlers (router.rs:1518,1566) and platform/service.rs tests. add_event_member, set_participant, remove_participant, assign/clear/swap/auto-fill roster seats and roster-role CRUD mutate only the owner tenant and never propagate to copies; guild copies reject these actions outright, so guild officers cannot manage their own copy's roster and guild rosters/Discord cards diverge from the alliance roster. add_event_member/set_participant also never call resolve_join_attribution, so no event_participant_attributions row exists for those users: alliance_distribution::complete then fails the entire split with 'has no guild attribution for this event; remove them manually before retrying' for any officer-added participant. Conversely, remove_participant never deletes the attribution, and attributions are never deleted on leave, so a user who left cannot rejoin attributed to a different eligible guild.
findings.fix: Route officer participant changes through the same propagation + attribution path (resolve the participant's eligible guild from user_tenant_memberships, require explicit choice if ambiguous). Propagate seat assignments/roster-role changes to copies (or declare the alliance roster canonical and make guild copies read-only mirrors of it). Delete the attribution when the participation is removed.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. add_event_member, set_participant, remove_participant and all seat handlers call assert_manageable_source_event, so guild copies are rejected, and none of them call sync_participation or resolve_join_attribution (router.rs:651-760, 1698-1840). Only participate/cancel (router.rs:1507, 1566) resolve attribution. alliance_distribution.rs:221-236 hard-fails on a missing attribution. No code deletes event_participant_attributions (grep for DELETE found nothing). Workaround exists: the officer can manually remove the participant, as the error message says.

findings.title: Cross-tenant participation sync is non-durable and returns an error after the local write already committed
findings.description: participate/cancel_participation commit locally, then call sync_participation(...).await? synchronously against every peer (user upsert, build mapping, participate_with_roster_version, split sync). Any peer failure (tenant unloadable, build not mapped 'selected build is not shared with the linked event', roster version conflict, comp slot taken in the copy) is returned as an HTTP error although the local signup and the control-plane attribution are already persisted, and hub.publish for the local room is skipped. There is no outbox/retry for participation (unlike event create/update), so the peer roster stays permanently out of sync until the user repeats the action. The web client and bot see an error for a successful signup.
findings.fix: Persist the participation intent in a participation outbox (control plane) in the same logical step, apply to peers from the fanout worker with retry, and always return success + publish the local roster notification; expose pending/failed peer state in the roster view.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. participate commits locally, then sync_participation(...).await? (router.rs:1518-1531) propagates any peer failure as an HTTP error, and hub.publish at line 1548 is skipped. The peer path can fail on map_build 'not shared' or participate_with_roster_version conflicts (sync.rs:395-440). Seats and builds are independent per tenant, so a peer slot conflict is realistic. There is no participation outbox, and leave has the same problem.

findings.title: Guild moving to a different alliance reuses stale share and sync-link rows (wrong-tenant writes, mirror silently skipped)
findings.description: alliance_memberships revives the 'left' row by UPDATE-ing alliance_tenant_id (insert_alliance_memberships), but alliance_shares.find_share looks up by (source_tenant_id, artifact_type, source_id) WITHOUT alliance_tenant_id, and upsert_share_row's UPDATE does not set alliance_tenant_id. After a guild joins a different alliance, share_build/share_comp/share_split pass the OLD published_id to copy_build_graph/copy_comp_graph/copy_split_graph against the NEW alliance database: it finds an unrelated build/comp/split with that numeric id and OVERWRITES it (name, items, comp_builds, split bags/participants), then the stale row still names the old alliance, so unshare deletes in the wrong tenant. Likewise create_mirror's early return `SELECT mirror_event_id FROM event_sync_links WHERE source_tenant_id AND source_event_id` ignores mirror_tenant_id and sync_enabled, so for an event already mirrored into the old alliance it returns Ok(Some(old mirror id)) and the retry request is marked 'complete' without ever creating a mirror in the new alliance. Same for rejoining: old links stay disabled forever.
findings.fix: Include alliance_tenant_id in find_share and the upsert (and invalidate shares on leave); in create_mirror filter by mirror_tenant_id = current alliance and sync_enabled, creating a fresh link when none exists. On leave, mark shares and links as detached with explicit semantics.
findings.verify_note: The code is as described. find_share ignores alliance_tenant_id (service.rs:519-552) and the UPDATE branch of upsert_share_row does not set it (561-575). insert_alliance_memberships revives a 'left' row with a new alliance_tenant_id (platform/service.rs:394-450). mark_alliance_left only disables links and does not detach shares. create_mirror's early return (sync.rs:56-72) ignores mirror_tenant_id and sync_enabled, so it returns a stale disabled link. The scenario needs a guild to leave and then join a different alliance, which is rare, so I rate it medium despite the cross-tenant overwrite risk.

findings.title: Duplicate announcement in alliance Discord for guild events with ping_alliance (legacy direct post plus mirror event announcement)
findings.description: When a guild event has ping_alliance, the guild's poller posts directly into the alliance's discord_events_channel_id (postAllianceAnnouncement, plus lifecycle notices), while create_mirror ALSO creates a real mirror event in the alliance tenant which the alliance's own poller announces (own thread, signup card, role ping) in its events channel. The README/plan ('alliance copies use destination delivery settings') made the mirror the intended path but the legacy ping_alliance path was left active. Additionally the mirror is created with discord_delivery copied from the SOURCE event (sync.rs:171) instead of the alliance's local setting (the alliance->guild fanout correctly uses the destination's local setting, fanout_worker.rs:206), so delivery mode depends on the guild's config.
findings.fix: Remove postAllianceAnnouncement/postAllianceLifecycle once a mirror exists (or make ping_alliance purely mean 'create mirror') and have the alliance poller be the only announcer. Use the alliance tenant's own discord_event_delivery for mirrors.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. announceEvent still calls postAllianceAnnouncement (poller.ts:972), which posts to alliance_discord_channel_id taken from the alliance's discord_events_channel_id (service.rs:333-341). create_mirror also creates a real mirror event in the alliance tenant, and nothing in the poller skips synchronized copies. Both announcements go to the same configured channel. The mirror's discord_delivery is copied from the source event (sync.rs:171), unlike fanout_worker.rs:206. This is annoying duplicate notification rather than data loss, so medium.

findings.title: Builds, comps and splits are one-shot snapshots: no update/delete propagation, no refresh of already-shared builds, no alliance->guild publishing
findings.description: alliance_shares is only touched by the share/unshare endpoints and event mirror creation. update_build/delete_build/update_comp/delete_comp/archive_*/update_split/delete_split/archive_split never look at alliance_shares (grep shows no reference outside alliance_share and events). So edits after sharing never reach the alliance, deleting/archiving the source leaves an orphan published copy and a dangling alliance_shares row (get_*_share_status still says shared), and ensure_build_published reuses an existing published build WITHOUT refreshing it, so even re-sharing a comp or creating a mirror event ships stale build contents. There is no alliance->guild path for builds/comps/splits at all (only incidental comp copies for events, see alliance-1), and the web UI only exposes sharing from guild tenants (comp-detail.ts:1560-1563). This contradicts the owner goal 'alliances sync EVERYTHING with member guilds'.
findings.fix: Introduce a generic origin-tracked sync: hook update/delete/archive of build/comp/split services to enqueue an 'artifact sync' job for tenants that have an alliance_shares row (and for alliance-owned artifacts, to all active members), processed by the same outbox worker with retries; make ensure_build_published refresh when the source version changed; add an explicit alliance->guild publish (policy decision, see questions).
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. No file under comps/ or splits/ references alliance_shares (grep). ensure_build_published reuses an existing build as long as the published row exists, with no refresh (service.rs:700-754). The README states these are snapshots, so the no-propagation part is a design choice, but stale-build reuse, dangling share rows and the absence of any alliance-to-guild path are real gaps versus the owner's goal. Missing feature rather than a bug, so medium.

findings.title: Guild-origin mirrors only sync schedule/status; comp changes, roster roles, battles and later-created splits never propagate and updates have no retry
findings.description: converge_copy_to_source copies title/description/flags/cap/times/status/vod flag only, not comp_id, roster roles, event_battles (replace_event_battles has no propagation) or splits. create_mirror short-circuits once a link exists, so update_event with a new comp_id (UpdateEventRequest.comp_id) leaves the mirror on the old comp and alliance signups then fail map_build ('selected build is not shared'). Splits are mirrored only if one exists at mirror-creation time and are never refreshed (and become writable/diverging via attach_shared_split_to_event). Setting ping_alliance back to false does nothing to the mirror (no unshare/withdraw path). Guild->alliance lifecycle convergence runs inline after the source commit and returns the error to the caller (router.rs:1334, lifecycle.rs:169-172) with no outbox, unlike alliance->guild; the documented 'repeat the request' retry does nothing if the user does not know it failed. Mirror split status is not recalculated when the mirror event status is converged (no sync_event_participants call in converge), so mirror splits lag.
findings.fix: Reuse the fanout outbox for guild->alliance too (direction-agnostic jobs), have converge also reconcile comp_id/roster roles/battles/splits, and add ping_alliance=false -> archive mirror + disable link.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. converge_copy_to_source never touches comp_id, roster roles, battles or splits (lifecycle.rs:56-96). create_mirror returns early on an existing link (sync.rs:56-72). The guild-to-alliance converge runs inline and its error is returned by sync_source_change (router.rs:1334-1360, lifecycle.rs:166-172), with no outbox. There is no ping_alliance=false withdrawal path.

findings.title: Joining an alliance performs no backfill: existing events, shares, users and links are not synchronized
findings.description: accept_alliance_membership / register_alliance_tenant / configure_alliance_setup only flip membership status. Slice 4 of alliance-operations.md ('accepting a guild starts initial sync of users/links/islands') is not implemented. A newly active guild receives alliance events only if a later update job runs AND the event already has at least one link (sync_owner_change_to_copies returns early when linked_event_peers is empty), so upcoming alliance events never reach it otherwise; users registered in the guild before joining are not copied into the alliance (only lazily via adopt_existing_member_link when that user opens the alliance page); existing guild comps/events are not mirrored.
findings.fix: On membership activation enqueue a backfill job: (1) publish all non-terminal alliance events to the new guild (targets = new guild), (2) copy registered users/albion links into the alliance schema, (3) refresh Ally/hub roles. Make sync_owner_change_to_copies not depend on pre-existing links.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. accept_alliance_membership only flips status (platform/service.rs:871-905). Slice 4 of plans/alliance-operations.md (lines 116-123) requires an initial sync and nothing implements it. sync_owner_change_to_copies returns early when the event has no links (lifecycle.rs:123-126), so a new guild only gets an existing event if another guild already has a link and the event is later updated.

findings.title: Leaving an alliance leaves live copies, mirrors and shared artifacts in place (ghost events, leaked data), and the alliance cannot remove a guild
findings.description: mark_alliance_left sets status='left' and sync_enabled=false and queues Discord role revocations, but does not archive/cancel the guild's copies of future alliance events (only targets still pending in the outbox are archived), does not hide the alliance's mirrors of the guild's events, and does not unshare alliance_shares rows (published builds/comps/splits of the departed guild stay readable in the alliance, including split financial data). Guild copies become locally manageable but receive no more cancel/time changes, so they stay announced and auto-started by the guild bot as ghost events. Role revocations are retried only inside the leave request (retry_alliance_role_revocations); there is no worker, so a transient Discord failure leaves roles. There is no endpoint for the alliance to expel or suspend a guild (only reset-setup, which marks everyone left).
findings.fix: On departure: archive future linked copies on both sides, mark alliance_shares detached and hide published artifacts, and run revocation retries from a background worker. Add an alliance-side remove-member action with the same cleanup.
findings.verify_note: Behavior is as described: mark_alliance_left only sets status, disables links and queues role revocations. Role retry runs only inside the leave request (service.rs:1038), and there is no alliance-side remove or expel route (public.rs:44-67). However, the doc comment at platform/service.rs:985-990 says history (membership row, published shares, links) is intentionally kept, and the copies become locally managed events. So 'leaked data' and 'ghost events' are mostly design choices. The real gaps are the missing expel action and the missing revocation retry worker. I rate it low.

findings.title: Alliance split distribution has no worker, UI or bot surface; failures need a manual retry of the same endpoint
findings.description: load_or_create_batch/project_one make crediting idempotent, but nothing resumes a 'processing'/'failed' batch (the partial index idx_alliance_split_distribution_pending has no consumer; only fanout_worker is spawned). If the process dies after some guilds were credited the split stays pending until an officer calls POST /splits/{id}/complete again. GET /api/splits/{id}/alliance-distribution is not called by the frontend or the bot, so partially failed payouts are invisible. A single unregistered/unattributed/zero-share participant or a departed guild blocks the whole batch (by design) but the only guidance is an error string. Created guild transactions carry split_id NULL and are pending 'split_credit' rows, so guild officers see credits without a link back to the alliance split.
findings.fix: Add a resume loop in the fanout worker for batches in processing/failed, surface distribution status in split-detail (web) and the split forum thread (bot), and expose the source alliance split id on the guild transaction view.
findings.verify_note: Mostly confirmed. Nothing resumes a processing or failed batch; only fanout_worker is spawned. The status endpoint is GET /api/splits/{id}/distribution-status (splits/router.rs:553), not 'alliance-distribution', and neither frontend nor bot calls it (grep). One sub-claim is refuted: guild transactions do record source_alliance_tenant_id and source_alliance_split_id (alliance_distribution.rs:505), and the transaction view and frontend model expose source_alliance_split_id (bank/models.rs:48, api.models.ts:365). Only split_id is NULL, so the back-link exists.

findings.title: Users/roles sync is a one-shot best-effort hook at /register; no reconciliation of members, Ally roles or hub roles
findings.description: after_successful_link swallows every error (let _ = record_membership, warn-only on link copy failure, Conflict on ensure_user_and_link treated as success) and returns (); the HTTP call succeeds even if the paired tenant never got the user/link/role. Nothing reconciles later: Albion guild membership changes, a user joining a sibling guild's Discord later, new member-guild role configuration, or Ally role for members of sibling guilds (assign_alliance_roles_on_tenant only targets the home guild and the alliance hub, so members of guild B never get guild A's Ally role unless they register inside guild A). Registering on the alliance Discord also creates a user row and user_tenant_memberships entry in the member guild tenant even if the person is not in that guild's Discord, and those memberships drive eligible_participation_guilds attribution. Unlink only deletes the paired albion link, not the paired user or memberships.
findings.fix: Move the fan-out into a durable job (control-plane outbox) with retry and an admin-visible failure list, add a periodic reconcile that diffs Albion guild rosters vs tenant users/links/roles, and gate guild membership on actual Discord guild membership.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. after_successful_link returns () and discards or only warns on every error (alliance_fanout.rs:107-175). There is no reconcile job. record_membership is created for every paired tenant regardless of actual Discord membership. I did not trace the Conflict-as-success and unlink sub-claims line by line, but the core claim is verified.

findings.title: Discord bot cannot do alliance operations the web can (event sharing, shares, retry/status) and neither surface shows sync health
findings.description: The web event form has a ping_alliance checkbox (events.ts:408) but /event-create sends no ping_alliance (no occurrence in the bot outside embed/poller code), so Discord users cannot share an event to the alliance. The bot has no commands for alliance share/unshare of builds/comps/splits (web: comp-detail, comp-build-detail, split-detail). Neither client calls GET /events/{id}/fanout-status, GET /events/{id}/mirror-status, POST /events/{id}/mirror-retry or the split alliance-distribution status (no matches in apps/frontend/src or apps/discord-bot/src), so a failed target, exhausted mirror request (12 attempts) or half-paid split is invisible and unrecoverable for non-API users.
findings.fix: Add ping_alliance option and sync health (fanout/mirror status + retry button/command) to both the web event detail and the bot (embed field + button); add share/unshare commands or buttons; show distribution status in split detail and the forum thread.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. The web has a ping_alliance checkbox (events.ts:409, 919) and the share UI (comp-detail.ts:2550, split-detail.ts:1607). The bot only reads ping_alliance in types and embeds and never sends it. grep finds no bot use of alliance/shares. Neither client calls fanout-status, mirror-status, mirror-retry or distribution-status.

findings.title: Fanout outbox has no terminal state or attempt cap and runs heavy work inline in request handlers
findings.description: event_fanout_targets are claimed while state IN (pending, failed, processing) with no attempts limit, so permanent errors (deleted source event, missing mapping as in alliance-2, unloadable tenant) retry hourly forever with no operator signal beyond fanout-status (which only reports the latest PUBLISH job via status_for_event). By contrast mirror requests cap at 12. process_due_targets is also invoked inline after create_event and after every update/start/cancel/stop/archive (up to 12 targets per call, each recopying comp graph, see alliance-1), so alliance event mutations pay the latency of all guilds; the worker also processes sequentially per tick (MAX_TARGETS_PER_TICK=12) so large alliances backlog. Update/archive job state is not exposed at all (status endpoint reads the publish job only).
findings.fix: Add attempts cap + 'exhausted' state and an operator re-arm endpoint; do not process inline (just notify the worker, e.g. tokio::sync::Notify) or process only the single target set with a timeout; expose latest job of any operation in fanout-status.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. claim_due has no attempts cap (fanout_outbox.rs:131-150), while mirror_retry caps at 12. process_due_targets runs inline after create_event (router.rs:1066-1085) and after every lifecycle sync (lifecycle.rs:158-166). status_for_event reads only the latest publish job (fanout_outbox.rs:340-347). Retry is capped at one attempt per hour, so the cost of retrying forever is low; the inline latency is the more real issue.

findings.title: Live web roster and split status are not refreshed for peer tenants after cross-tenant changes
findings.description: RosterHub.publish is only invoked by handlers for the caller's own tenant/event id. sync_participation and converge_copy_to_source write peer tenants' DBs (participations, status, archive) but never publish for (peer_tenant, peer_event_id), so a web user watching the guild copy's /roster/live only sees changes made elsewhere after a manual refetch; the Discord bot learns via roster_version revision polling. converge also never calls SplitService::sync_event_participants on the peer, so splits linked to a copy keep their awaiting_event/pending status when the source starts/stops.
findings.fix: After peer writes call hub.publish(peer_tenant, peer_event_id, new_version, kind, []) (hand RosterHub to the sync helpers) and call sync_event_participants in converge when status changes.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. sync_participation and converge_copy_to_source write peer DBs without any RosterHub publish. The functions do not receive the hub, and converge never calls sync_event_participants. This is a staleness UX issue, since the web stream and mirror split status lag until a refetch.

findings.title: Entire domains have no alliance sync: regear, warns, XP/progression, ranks, settings, battles, bank history
findings.description: grep for alliance across modules shows no sync logic in regear, warns, progression/XP, giveaways, tickets, applications, trials, vods, ranks, roles or guild settings. Bank is read-through (live aggregation) which is acceptable, but battles are not stored for alliance (no battle_sync worker, scope read live), event completion XP is deliberately skipped for copies (README: mirror events are not award authorities) which means guild members get no XP/stats for alliance events they attended, and guild-level regear/attendance for alliance events rely on the guild's own linker (tenant-local link_status) with no coupling to the alliance source. If the owner wants 'everything' synced, these domains need explicit policies.
findings.fix: Decide per domain (see logic_questions); implement the chosen ones on top of one generic origin-tracked sync engine rather than per-feature code.
findings.verify_note: Informational and policy-dependent, not a traced defect. The events README (line 15) says mirror events are not award authorities, and auto_stop skips XP for copies, so guild members get no event XP for alliance events. Bank is intentionally live-aggregated (bank/alliance.rs:1-8). The rest is a negative claim that those domains have no sync, which cannot be confirmed as a bug without a stated policy.

findings.title: Three overlapping sync mechanisms and cross-DB writes with no common contract
findings.description: There are four independent copy engines (alliance_shares snapshots, event_fanout_* outbox, event_mirror_requests outbox, one-shot register fan-out) plus the distribution batch, each with its own idempotency key, retry/lease code (fanout_outbox and mirror_retry are near-duplicates), direction and failure surface, and each copies assets differently (event_fanout_assets per job vs alliance_shares per artifact). Divergences found above (duplicate builds, stale builds, missing roster-role mapping, delivery setting source, no retry on converge) all stem from this. Business logic also sits in HTTP handlers (create_event decides fanout targets and runs workers inline, router.rs:1020-1135) instead of a service layer.
findings.fix: Create one sync module: origin columns (origin_tenant_id, origin_id, origin_version) on builds/comps/events/splits in destination schemas, a generic control-plane job table with direction, kind and per-target state, one worker, and a single status API consumed by both web and bot. Move handler orchestration into services.
findings.verify_note: The observations are accurate: separate copy engines exist (alliance_shares, fanout outbox, mirror_retry, register fan-out, distribution batch). fanout_outbox and mirror_retry duplicate lease and retry code, and create_event orchestrates fanout in the handler. This is a refactoring recommendation rather than a defect, and the 'divergences stem from this' causality is argued rather than shown.

findings.title: Participant attribution is permanent and mirror requests for flash/ineligible sources fail slowly
findings.description: resolve_join_attribution refuses to ever change a stored guild ('cannot be changed') and nothing deletes rows on leave/removal or when the guild membership ends, so a user leaving an event and rejoining as a different eligible guild is blocked and a user whose guild left the alliance blocks the whole split distribution. Also mirror_retry::attempt returns Ok(None) (inactive) only for cancelled/archived sources; a guild event without an active alliance, or whose comp was deleted, yields Conflict/NotFound and burns all 12 attempts (≈ hours of backoff capped at 3600s) before surfacing as 'failed'.
findings.fix: Delete attributions when participation is removed; classify non-retryable errors (no active alliance, missing comp) as immediate terminal failures.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. resolve_join_attribution refuses to change a stored guild (attribution.rs:99-125) and nothing deletes attribution rows. mirror_retry::attempt returns inactive only for cancelled or archived sources, so 'no active alliance' and 'flash' errors from create_mirror (sync.rs:75-93) burn all 12 attempts with backoff capped at 3600s.

logic_questions: Should a guild-origin event shared with the alliance ALSO appear in the other member guilds (guild->alliance->other guilds), or stay alliance-only as plans/alliance-event-distribution.md states? The owner goal 'alliances sync everything with member guilds' could mean either. Options: (a) keep alliance-only mirror, (b) alliance re-fans-out guild events to all other guilds, (c) per-event opt-in scope (own guild / alliance / all guilds).

Who owns builds and comps: should alliance-created builds/comps automatically (or via an explicit 'publish to guilds' action) propagate to every member guild, and should guild edits of shared builds/comps keep flowing to the alliance copy automatically? Options: (a) keep manual one-shot snapshots, (b) automatic one-way refresh from owner (origin tracking), (c) shared library readable cross-tenant instead of copies.

For alliance-owned events, who manages the roster seats (assign/swap/auto-fill) and extra roster roles: only the alliance (guild copies show a read-only aggregated roster) or each guild for its own members? Today copies cannot manage but also do not receive seat assignments.

Should guild members who attend an alliance event receive guild XP/progression/attendance/regear credit in their own guild (currently mirrors/copies are not award authorities and are not stopped via the XP-awarding path)? Options: no, alliance-level XP only; yes via the guild copy; or yes via a projected ledger like split credits.

When a guild leaves (or is removed) should its published artifacts, mirrored events and split snapshots in the alliance be deleted, archived/hidden but retained for history, or left as-is? Also should the alliance owner be able to expel a guild unilaterally (today impossible except reset-setup)?

Which additional domains must be synced alliance<->guild (warns/blacklist, regear, ranks/roles, guild settings, VODs, trials/applications, giveaways, battles) and in which direction/authority? Today none of these has any alliance logic; each needs an owner decision (shared, alliance-owned broadcast to guilds, or guild-private).

Is the Discord-side behaviour of the legacy ping_alliance direct post to be removed in favour of the mirror event (avoiding duplicate announcements), and should a mirror use the alliance's own delivery mode or the originating guild's?

Should an officer-added participant on an alliance event be attributed automatically to the participant's single eligible guild, require an explicit guild pick, or be allowed without attribution (and then excluded/blocked at split distribution)?

For alliance splits, when a participant has no guild-registered account or their guild left: keep the current 'block the whole batch until a human removes them', or allow partial payout with the unresolved shares held in an alliance suspense balance?

summary: Events are stored per tenant in the backend (event row, participations, roster seats, roster_version). The only live push channel is the in-process RosterHub, a WebSocket broadcast that carries invalidation messages and is published only for roster/participation changes within the same tenant. The web detail page reloads GET /api/events/{id} plus roster, comp and losses on every message. Discord has no push channel at all: a per-guild Poller in the bot (default every 60s) pulls state, and ALL Discord-side bookkeeping lives only in a local JSON file (poller-state-<guild>.json): announcement thread ids, parent and signup-card message ids, calendar message ids, massed/pinged events, pending announces, last-seen revisions. The poller discovers new events by scanning /api/events sorted by created_at against a high-water id, then every cycle diffs /api/events/revisions (roster_version:status:updated_at) to re-render the signup card, starter message and linked split posts. Mass/Start timing, the 1h warning, voice-channel creation, participant pings and alliance lifecycle notices are decided by the bot, not the backend. Lifecycle logic is copy-pasted across poller.ts, handlers/button.ts, services/event-thread-command.ts and commands/event-*.ts. The backend owns start/stop/cancel/uncancel/archive state and a 30s per-guild-tenant worker (event_sessions) for auto-stop at the 3h deadline and the AlbionBB battle linker. Alliances: an alliance-origin event is fanned out through a control-plane outbox (fanout_outbox + fanout_worker, 15s tick, max 12 targets per tick, also run inline in the HTTP request) into tenant-local copies linked in event_sync_links, and lifecycle/content changes are converged to copies by converge_copy_to_source. Copies reject all management calls (assert_manageable_source_event). Participation is mirrored to peers by sync_participation, filtered by guild attribution. A legacy second path remains for guild-origin events: ping_alliance creates a one-shot mirror (create_mirror) in the alliance tenant and the guild bot also posts directly to the alliance Discord channel. Result: web-to-Discord latency is at least one poll (60s) and many web-initiated lifecycle actions have no Discord side effects; Discord-initiated lifecycle changes are invisible to open web pages; several alliance sync paths (officer participant edits, roster seats, roster roles, comp changes, voice binding, auto-stop) are missing or blocked.

findings.title: Poller wipes event->thread mappings for every event not among the last 50 pinged, breaking roster sync, close, calendar links and mass/start posts
findings.description: In checkUpcomingEvents, once pinged1hEvents exceeds 50 entries (after the 51st 1h warning ever sent for the guild) the cleanup slices pinged1hEvents and then REPLACES this.state.eventThreadIds with only the entries whose event id is in that retained pinged list. Every announced event that has not yet received its 1h warning (all future scheduled events) or is otherwise not in the last 50 pings loses its thread id. Consequences: checkEventRosterSync iterates Object.keys(eventThreadIds) so web joins/leaves/edits/seat changes stop re-rendering the signup card; checkClosedEvents stops closing/deleting threads on stop/cancel/archive; Mass/Start notices are skipped (getEventThread returns null so massDiscordEvent/startDiscordEvent get no thread and nothing is posted to participants); buildEventCalendarMessages(..., this.state.eventThreadIds) loses the 'open thread' links; findEventIdForThread breaks thread slash commands. checkNewEvents does not re-announce because lastEventId already passed those ids, so the mapping is never recovered. It triggers on every 1h-warning once a guild has >50 pings, so it affects any long-lived tenant.
findings.fix: Delete the eventThreadIds filtering entirely (prune only pinged1hEvents, or prune thread ids for terminal/archived events using the revisions map). Better, persist thread_id/parent_message_id/signup_message_id in the backend (see events-2) so the bot cannot lose them.
findings.verify_note: poller.ts:2007-2014 replaces eventThreadIds with only the ids still in the last-50 pinged1hEvents once that list exceeds 50. Threads for every other announced event are dropped. checkEventRosterSync, checkClosedEvents, getEventThread, the calendar links and findEventIdForThread all read that map. checkNewEvents uses lastEventId, so it never re-announces and the mapping is not recovered.

findings.title: Discord announcement state (thread, parent message, signup card, calendar message ids) lives only in a bot-local JSON file, not in the backend
findings.description: The backend event entity has no field for the announcement thread id, parent message id, signup card id, or announced status (only vod_forum_thread_id and alliance_discord_message_id exist). PollerState (eventThreadIds, eventParentMessageIds, eventSignupMessageIds, eventSignupRevisions, pendingAnnounces, massedEvents, pinged1hEvents, archivedEventIds, calendar ids) is a per-guild JSON on the bot's disk. Consequences: the web UI cannot show 'open in Discord' or announcement/delivery status; a bot container without a persistent volume (or a wiped file) hits adoptCheckpointBaseline, which silently adopts all existing events as already-announced and forgets all threads, so every existing event permanently loses its Discord card sync; two bot replicas would double-announce; pending/failed announcement state is invisible to admins; and backend-driven behaviours (fanout copies, restore from archive, web cancel) must be guessed from polling.
findings.fix: Add an event_discord_delivery table (event_id, channel_id, parent_message_id, thread_id, signup_message_id, last_rendered_revision, state, attempts, last_error) with bot-authenticated claim/record/list endpoints, mirroring the existing VOD claim/created pattern. The poller then reads 'what needs rendering' from the backend instead of diffing local files, and the web can show delivery status and thread links.
findings.verify_note: The thread, parent, signup-card and calendar ids live only in the bot's PollerState JSON. The backend entity has only vod_forum_thread_id, so the structural claim holds. adoptCheckpointBaseline on an uninitialized state does adopt existing events as already announced. The multi-replica double-announce is speculative. This is an architecture finding rather than a traced defect, so severity is lowered from high.

findings.title: Guild copies of alliance events cannot get a voice channel or be started by the guild bot; the bot creates and deletes a voice channel every minute
findings.description: lifecycle.rs documents that a copy's Discord voice channel stays tenant-local, but set_event_voice_channel (router.rs:1942) and start_event (router.rs:2030) both call assert_manageable_source_event, which returns 403 for any copy whose sync link is enabled. In each guild's poller, checkEventLifecycle runs massDiscordEvent for scheduled copies at mass time: createAndBindVoice creates a Discord voice channel, the PUT /discord-voice-channel returns 403, the catch deletes the new channel and throws. massedEvents is only pushed on success, so this repeats every poll for the whole mass-to-start window; at start time startDiscordEvent also gets 403 on POST /start every poll. The guild bot can therefore never provision voice, mass/start pings, or the voice-empty auto-stop for alliance copies, and it spams Discord audit logs and rate limits with create/delete channel calls. Only status converged from the source flips the copy to live.
findings.fix: Allow tenant-local, non-content mutations on copies for the bot-system principal or any caller: voice binding/clearing, mass/start notification state. Keep content edits and source lifecycle blocked. Alternatively model Discord side effects (voice, mass/start notice) as backend-queued jobs per tenant so the bot only executes them.
findings.verify_note: set_event_voice_channel (router.rs:1942) and start_event (router.rs:2030) both call assert_manageable_source_event. It returns Forbidden for any copy whose event_sync_links row has sync_enabled, with no exemption for the bot principal. The guild poller lists copies and runs massDiscordEvent, which calls createAndBindVoice. That PUT gets 403, the catch deletes the new channel, massedEvents is not pushed, and it repeats every poll. startDiscordEvent also hits 403 on POST /start.

findings.title: Alliance tenants run no event_sessions worker: alliance events never auto-stop, completion XP never retries, and guild copies are resurrected to 'live'
findings.description: starts_sync_workers returns false for kind 'alliance', so ensure_sync_workers and run_server never call event_sessions::spawn for an alliance tenant (this also skips retry_pending_event_completion_xp and giveaway draws). A started alliance-owned event keeps status live and auto_stop_deadline in the past forever unless someone clicks Stop. converge_copy_to_source copies started_at/auto_stop_deadline to guild copies, so each guild's own worker auto-stops its copy at the deadline; the next converge triggered by any source update/fanout retry sets status back to the source's 'live' and stopped_at=None (lifecycle.rs:80-87), after which the guild worker stops it again. The alliance roster, XP, and linked splits stay 'live' indefinitely.
findings.fix: Spawn a reduced worker for alliance tenants (auto-stop + completion XP retry, skip AlbionBB linking) and make auto-stop call sync_owner_change_to_copies so copies follow the source. In converge, never move a terminal copy back to live unless the source's status transition actually happened after the copy's stop.
findings.verify_note: starts_sync_workers returns false for 'alliance' (tenant.rs:84-86), and ensure_sync_workers and lib.rs:120 both skip such tenants. So event_sessions::spawn never runs for an alliance tenant, and auto_stop and retry_pending_event_completion_xp never run there. converge_copy_to_source (lifecycle.rs:80-87) resets a copy's status to the source's 'live' and clears stopped_at after the guild worker auto-stopped it. Impact is bounded because a manual Stop still works, so severity is lowered from high.

findings.title: Join/leave: local change is committed before cross-tenant sync; a peer failure returns an error to the user and skips the live-roster publish
findings.description: participate() commits the local participation via participate_with_roster_version, then calls sync_participation(...).await? and only afterwards hub.publish. sync_participation applies the join in each peer with `?` and no compensation. Failure modes: (a) peer build mapping missing ('selected build is not shared with the linked event'); (b) the peer comp slot is full while the local slot is free; (c) the peer copy is archived/cancelled (apply_participation rejects); (d) on leave with no stored attribution (legacy joins) peers get cancel_participation and the first peer where the user never joined returns NotFound, aborting the loop. In all cases the user already holds a local seat but gets an error toast / Discord 'Selection Failed', the remaining peers are never updated, and hub.publish is skipped so web viewers don't see the change and the Discord card only catches up on the next poll. Participants end up present in one tenant and absent in the other with no retry (unlike fanout which has an outbox).
findings.fix: Make participation propagation an outbox job (same table pattern as fanout_outbox with per-target status and retry) instead of an inline fallible call; publish to the hub unconditionally after the local commit; treat peer NotFound on leave as success; surface per-target sync state in the response/fanout-status.
findings.verify_note: participate() commits locally, then calls sync_participation(...).await? (router.rs:1518-1531), and hub.publish comes only after it. Peer failures from map_build or participate_with_roster_version propagate with ? and nothing compensates or retries. The leave path has the same shape. The user-facing error plus partial state is real, but it needs a failing peer, so severity is lowered from high.

findings.title: Officer add/set/remove participant never syncs to alliance copies/mirrors and never notifies peers' live rosters
findings.description: Only the self-service participate/cancel handlers call sync_participation. add_event_member, set_participant and remove_participant (used by the web 'Add member' and 'remove participant' actions, event-detail.ts:5001 and :5190) only touch the local tenant. An alliance officer adding or removing a member on the canonical alliance event never changes the attributed guild's copy (so the guild's web roster/Discord card stays stale); a guild officer on a guild event with an alliance mirror never updates the mirror. Because copies reject management calls, nobody can fix the copy by hand. Also sync_participation itself calls EventService on the peer DB directly and never publishes to RosterHub for the peer tenant (hub.publish uses only tenant.0 at router.rs:1544/1594), so a live web roster in the other tenant doesn't update until the next manual reload.
findings.fix: Route all participant mutations through one backend 'participation command' that resolves attribution, fans out through the outbox, and publishes RosterHub notifications for every affected (tenant, event) pair; give officer edits an explicit attributed_guild.
findings.verify_note: add_event_member, set_participant and remove_participant (router.rs:1698-1840) only touch the local tenant and publish to the local hub. They never call sync_participation. sync_participation also never publishes to RosterHub for the peer tenant. Copies reject management calls, so nobody can fix them by hand.

findings.title: Web start/stop/cancel have no Discord side effects (voice channel, start notice to participants, alliance lifecycle pings); Discord /event-start also posts nothing in the thread
findings.description: Voice-channel creation/binding, the 'LIVE' mention of linked participants, the 'mass is starting' notice, and alliance 'mass/start/cancel' pings exist only in the bot (startDiscordEvent/massDiscordEvent/postAllianceLifecycle) and only run from (a) Discord button/slash with a thread, or (b) the poller's time-based auto Mass/Start. A web officer clicking Start calls POST /start, which only flips status/started_at/auto_stop_deadline. No voice channel is created, so the poller's voice-based auto-stop never applies (it requires discord_voice_channel_id), nobody is pinged, and the alliance Discord gets no 'is live' notice. /event-start (commands/event-start.ts) calls startDiscordEvent without a thread, so the start announcement is skipped there too. The backend remind endpoint only validates scheduled status ('records the reminder request for the bot' but persists nothing, service.rs:3770-3790), and the frontend has no remind action at all, so Ping is Discord-only.
findings.fix: Have the backend record lifecycle notifications as a durable queue (event_discord_actions: mass/start/stop/cancel/remind, with target tenant) enqueued by start/stop/cancel/remind regardless of caller; the bot consumes the queue and executes voice + messages. Then every initiator (web, slash command, button, auto timer) behaves identically.
findings.verify_note: Web POST /start (router.rs:2030-2036) only flips state and syncs. Voice binding and the mass and start notices exist only in the bot's event-lifecycle.ts. commands/event-start.ts calls startDiscordEvent with no thread, so it posts no start message. prepare_event_reminder (service.rs:3770) only validates and persists nothing, and the frontend has no remind call. The parity gap is real.

findings.title: Stopped and auto-stopped events leave the Discord signup card stale (still 'LIVE' with a Stop button)
findings.description: For terminal status stopped/auto_stopped, checkClosedEvents only calls closeEventThread (lock+archive, then forgetEventThread deletes the mapping), and checkEventRosterSync explicitly `continue`s for stopped/auto_stopped/cancelled. Nothing re-renders the card with the final status. Only the cancelled path refreshes it (closeCancelledEvent). So after a web stop, an auto-stop by the 3h worker, or a Discord /event-stop or thread-command stop (neither refreshes the card), the archived thread's card permanently shows status LIVE and enabled buttons. The final roster snapshot is also never frozen on the card.
findings.fix: Before closing a thread for stopped/auto_stopped, run refreshEventSignupCard with the final detail (like closeCancelledEvent does), and keep the mapping long enough for a final render.
findings.verify_note: checkClosedEvents only calls closeEventThread for stopped and auto_stopped events. checkEventRosterSync skips those statuses. closeEventAnnouncementThread only locks and archives. The Discord stop paths (event-stop.ts, event-thread-command.ts) do not refresh the card either. Only the cancelled path calls refreshEventSignupCard.

findings.title: Discord Stop button archives the thread before editing the card, which will fail in an archived thread
findings.description: The stop button does stopDiscordEvent, then closeEventThread (lockAndArchiveThread -> setArchived(true)), then interaction.message.edit(...) on a message inside the now-archived thread. Elsewhere the codebase uses withReopenedThread/withUnarchivedThread precisely because Discord rejects message edits in archived threads. The edit is likely to throw after the backend stop already succeeded, so the user gets the generic 'Button Action Failed' error even though the event stopped, and the stale card is not updated (compounds events-8). The cancel branch correctly edits first, then closes.
findings.fix: Edit the card first, then close the thread (as the cancel branch does), or use refreshEventSignupCard which reopens safely.
findings.verify_note: button.ts:985-1000 does closeEventThread (lock then archive) and then interaction.message.edit. The code base's own comment says Discord rejects every mutation on an archived thread. The exact behaviour for editing a message cannot be confirmed from the code. If it does throw, the effect is a spurious 'Button Action Failed' after the stop succeeded. Severity is lowered because it is cosmetic.

findings.title: Battle linker polls every 'pending' event every 30s forever, including never-started and cancelled events, and walks up to 100 AlbionBB pages for cancelled live events
findings.description: link_status defaults to 'pending', and refresh_pending_links selects ALL events with link_status in (in_progress, pending) with no filter on archived, status, or kind (flash included). For a scheduled or cancelled-before-start event, link_battles_for_event runs and fails at `started_at.ok_or_else(... has not been started)` with a warn! log every 30s per event, per tenant, forever; the set only grows. For an event that was live and then cancelled, link_status stays 'in_progress' (cancel_event does not touch it) and linker_is_done returns false for status 'cancelled' (only stopped/auto_stopped/completed/failed), so link_battles_for_event keeps paginating AlbionBB (up to MAX_BATTLE_PAGES=100) every 30s indefinitely for a cancelled event, hammering the upstream and writing event rows.
findings.fix: Default link_status to 'idle'; only select events with status in (live, stopped, auto_stopped) and archived_at IS NULL; set link_status='failed'/'completed' in cancel_event; include 'cancelled' in linker_is_done.
findings.verify_note: link_status defaults to 'pending' and refresh_pending_links selects all pending and in_progress rows with no status or archived filter. linker_is_done is false for 'cancelled'. A never-started event fails at the started_at check with a warn log every 30s. That check runs before any AlbionBB call, so the cost is a DB read plus log spam. Upstream paging happens only for events cancelled after starting. cancel_event does not touch link_status. Severity is lowered from high.

findings.title: Linker tick bumps event.updated_at every 30s, so every live event is fully re-rendered on Discord every poll
findings.description: The Discord sync fingerprint is `roster_version:status:updated_at`. link_battles_for_event sets updated_at=now() on each tick (30s) for every live/in-progress event, and bind_event_voice_channel/clear also bump it. While an event is live, the revision differs on every 60s poll, so checkEventRosterSync does for each live event: GET /api/events/{id} (the heavy detail), fetchStarterMessage + edit, possibly thread.setName, edit the signup card, and for each linked split GET discord-sync + forum post sync. That is a continuous stream of Discord edits (rate-limit risk across tenants sharing one bot token) and heavy detail reads for no user-visible change. For 45 minutes after stop the status is terminal so it stops, but throughout the live window it churns.
findings.fix: Do not touch updated_at in the linker (use a separate link_updated_at column) or compute a dedicated `content_revision` bumped only by user-visible changes (title/time/status/roster/comp/roles), and expose that in /events/revisions.
findings.verify_note: link_battles_for_event sets updated_at = now() on every tick (service.rs:4303-4308). list_event_revisions returns updated_at, and checkEventRosterSync builds its fingerprint from it. So every live event is re-fetched and re-rendered on each poll. The mechanism is real.

findings.title: Bot auto Mass/Start and 1h warning read only page 1 of a newest-first event list (limit 50 / 20)
findings.description: GET /api/events with no sort defaults to event_date desc (SortOrder::from_query defaults to Desc). checkEventLifecycle takes page 1 limit 50 and checkUpcomingEvents takes page 1 limit 20, then filters for scheduled events whose mass/start/1h time has arrived. Events due now sort BELOW every later-dated event. A guild with 20 events scheduled further in the future (weekly series, alliance copies) never gets the 1h warning for the event starting in the next hour; with 50 future events, Mass and automatic Start silently stop working for the due event. There is already an unpaginated /api/events/calendar feed for exactly live + upcoming scheduled events, but it is not used here. The poller also never prunes massedEvents (state grows) and never re-arms massedEvents/pinged1hEvents if an event is rescheduled after the notice.
findings.fix: Move the due-event decision into the backend (e.g. GET /api/events/due?kind=mass|start|reminder returning only events whose time passed and which have not been notified, with an ack endpoint), or at minimum switch the bot to /api/events/calendar.
findings.verify_note: The poller reads api/events page 1 with limit 50 (lifecycle) or 20 (1h warning) and no sort. SortOrder defaults to Desc on event_date, so the nearest-due events sort below later-dated ones. The /api/events/calendar feed exists and is not used. This only bites a guild with more than 20 or 50 events dated after the due event.

findings.title: New-event discovery rescans the entire event list every poll; the detail endpoint doing the real work also writes on GET
findings.description: listSinceCheckpoint loads page 1, then every page up to 50 (x50 items) of /api/events?sort=created_at&order=desc on every poll, without stopping once ids drop to or below the checkpoint, and without a server-side `after_id` filter; per tenant, per minute, up to ~2500 EventViews plus a control-plane query per request (hydrate_event_list). In addition, the same poll cycle issues separate list calls for lifecycle, upcoming, calendar, revisions. All card renders call GET /api/events/{id}, which runs ensure_seed_fights_for_event and automatically_group_event_fights (DB writes), applies canonical snapshot metrics, loss estimates, performance stats and split summaries on a read. The web reloads this same endpoint plus roster, comp and battle losses on every realtime message, so one signup triggers the heavy detail query for every open viewer and the bot.
findings.fix: Add `created_after_id`/`updated_after` filters (or a dedicated bot feed returning only changed events) so the poller does an O(changes) query; split a lightweight `EventCardView` from the analytics detail, and move fight seeding/grouping out of the read path (do it in the linker/finalize step).
findings.verify_note: listSinceCheckpoint (poller.ts:751-782) scans every page up to 50 each poll with no early stop. The code comment says this is deliberate because list order is not id order. get_event_detail_scoped calls ensure_seed_fights_for_event and automatically_group_event_fights on a read (service.rs:2911-2912). The cost is real but scales with event count.

findings.title: Alliance-to-guild convergence skips comp, roster roles, Discord roles and officer seat assignment; guild-origin mirrors are one-shot
findings.description: (1) For an existing copy, fanout_worker computes target_comp_id (re-copying the comp and all builds on every update) but converge_copy_to_source never sets comp_id, so changing comp on an alliance event via PATCH leaves guild copies on the old comp; the new comp/builds are copied and mapped but unused. (2) Alliance event discord_role_ids are not copied (`discord_role_ids: Vec::new()` at fanout_worker.rs:225), so guild copies announce with no role ping and no mapping to a guild role exists; player-facing 'call to arms' alliance events don't ping anyone in guild servers. (3) create_event_roster_role / delete_event_roster_role don't call sync_source_change, so extra roster roles only propagate on a later unrelated update (alliance) or never (guild-origin mirror: create_mirror returns early if a link exists, sync.rs:63-72). (4) Roster seat assign/swap/auto-fill/clear are only on the source; seat assignments are never propagated to the guild copy, so guild members' web roster/Discord card (which prefers assigned_build) shows no assignments. (5) ping_alliance=false on update does not retract/archive the existing mirror. (6) update_event cannot change discord_role_ids, player_cap or vod_forum_post_enabled (UpdateEventRequest has none), so those cannot be fixed after creation.
findings.fix: Make converge a full state-sync: map and set comp_id via the stored build/comp mapping, copy player_cap, mirror roster roles and (if the owner wants it) seat assignments; call sync_source_change from roster-role handlers; add discord_role_ids/player_cap/vod flag to UpdateEventRequest; implement mirror retraction.
findings.verify_note: converge_copy_to_source never sets comp_id (lifecycle.rs:56-96), although fanout_worker re-copies the comp. fanout_worker.rs:225 sets discord_role_ids to an empty list. The roster-role create and delete handlers (router.rs:905-966) only notify the hub and do not call sync_source_change. UpdateEventRequest has no discord_role_ids, player_cap or vod flag field. The other sub-claims are plausible but not individually traced.

findings.title: Web live roster only reacts to roster changes; Discord-initiated start/stop/cancel/edit never reach an open web page, and flash masses have no realtime at all
findings.description: RosterHub.publish is called only from roster/participation handlers. start_event, stop_event, cancel_event, uncancel_event, archive, update_event, voice binding and auto-stop (worker) don't publish and don't bump roster_version, so a Discord Stop/Cancel/Start leaves the web detail page showing the old status (and old action buttons) until the user reloads. The notification is process-local (broadcast channel of 128, 'single backend replica'), and carries no lifecycle kind. For flash masses the detail loader returns before realtimeRoster.connect (event-detail.ts:5856), so participant lists on flash pages never update live.
findings.fix: Publish a 'status_changed'/'event_updated' notification from every lifecycle handler and from the worker, and have the frontend reload on it; connect the socket for flash masses too; if multi-replica is ever needed, back the hub with Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY.
findings.verify_note: hub.publish appears only in the roster, participation and role handlers (router.rs:673-1814). start, stop, cancel, uncancel, archive and the auto-stop worker never publish. The flash early return at event-detail.ts:5856 skips realtimeRoster.connect. The hub is a process-local broadcast channel.

findings.title: Feature parity gaps between web and Discord for events
findings.description: Web-only: ping_alliance, Discord role selection, VOD toggle, player cap, regear, split creation, comp edits, battle linking, roster seats, archive/unarchive. Discord-only: flash masses (the web detail page for flash is read-only with 'discord only', no status, no start/stop/cancel/archive, and the web cannot create them), Ping/remind (no web remind exists), voice channel provisioning. /event-create only sends title/date/comp/description/call_to_arms, so Discord-created events have no mass_time (auto start-30m), no roles, no regear, no player cap, no VOD flag decisions (backend default true), and there is no Discord event edit command at all. Rules also differ: the backend only rejects joins to cancelled/archived events (apply_participation) and allows leave in any status, while Discord disables Join/Leave unless scheduled, so the web/API can still mutate the roster of a live or stopped event after completion XP snapshots.
findings.fix: Define one event command contract in the backend (create/edit/lifecycle/remind/participate with allowed-status table) and expose it to both clients; add the missing Discord commands (edit, flash from web via event_kind) and enforce status rules in apply_participation/cancel_participation.
findings.verify_note: The flash detail page is read-only with no status or lifecycle controls and is marked 'discordOnly'. The web has no flash creation path. /event-create sends only title, date, comp, description and call_to_arms. apply_participation rejects only cancelled and archived events. These are real gaps, but several are product-scope choices rather than defects.

findings.title: Event lifecycle orchestration is duplicated in four bot code paths and frontend re-derives authority
findings.description: Cancel (incl. empty-voice cleanup, thread close, mapping retention), stop, start, reopen are implemented separately in button.ts, event-thread-command.ts, commands/event-*.ts and the poller (each with slightly different thread/card/alliance-ping behavior, e.g. only the poller posts alliance notices). The auto Mass/Start schedule and voice-empty auto-stop decisions are bot logic. The frontend computes canEdit/canDelete from permission strings and created_by instead of calling the backend's /api/events/{id}/management-authority endpoint that the bot already uses; events.ts and event-detail.ts duplicate the create/edit form validation (mass<=start) hard-coded in Italian.
findings.fix: Centralize lifecycle in backend commands that return the resulting side-effect list; keep one bot 'apply lifecycle effects' function; use /management-authority in the frontend.
findings.verify_note: Lifecycle orchestration is duplicated across button.ts, event-thread-command.ts, commands/event-*.ts and the poller. The frontend computes canEdit and canDelete from permission strings and created_by (event-detail.ts:3230-3250) and never calls /management-authority. The backend still enforces authorization, so this is a maintainability and consistency issue. Severity is lowered.

findings.title: Two parallel guild-to-alliance mechanisms plus a write-only per-event delivery setting
findings.description: A guild event with ping_alliance both (a) creates a mirror event in the alliance tenant via create_mirror (the alliance poller announces it with its own thread/card in the alliance Discord) and (b) has the guild bot post a direct message into alliance_discord_channel_id (postAllianceAnnouncement) and lifecycle pings, so the alliance Discord can receive two announcements for one event. Idempotency of (b) relies on the bot PATCHing alliance_discord_message_id through the generic event update endpoint as the full-Admin bot_system principal (rbac.rs:282-300), which any user with events.edit can also overwrite. Separately, events.discord_delivery is stored and fanned out per event (and in fanout copies from the destination guild's setting), but the bot ignores it and uses the live tenant setting via this.settings.eventDelivery(), so the per-event column and CreateEventRequest field are dead data. README confirms the legacy path is not on the new outbox.
findings.fix: Retire the direct alliance message path and use mirror events as the single mechanism (route alliance pings from the mirror), or move guild->alliance publication onto the fanout outbox; delete or honor events.discord_delivery; move alliance_discord_message_id into the delivery table from events-2.
findings.verify_note: The guild path creates a mirror (router.rs:1101-1108 and 1319) and the bot also posts postAllianceAnnouncement directly. discord_delivery appears in the bot only as a type field in types.ts:263, so the bot never reads the per-event column and uses the tenant setting. The double announcement in the alliance Discord is plausible and follows from the two code paths.

findings.title: Alliance lifecycle and fanout run synchronously inside the HTTP request, re-copy the comp for every guild each time, and return errors after commit
findings.description: Every start/stop/cancel/uncancel/archive/update on an alliance event enqueues a fanout job and calls process_due_targets inline; each target re-runs copy_alliance_comp_to_tenant for the comp and all builds, rewrites asset maps, and delete+reinserts roster roles, even for a simple Start. MAX_TARGETS_PER_TICK=12 means alliances with >12 guilds are only partly processed in the request; the rest wait up to 15s ticks. The processing also claims any tenant's due targets, not just this job's. For guild-origin events with mirrors, converge errors propagate with `?` after the state change was committed (router.rs:2033/2068/2103/2143), so the UI/bot shows failure for a stop/start that actually happened and repeating it returns 409.
findings.fix: Make lifecycle operations (status-only) skip asset copy and only converge status/timestamps; run the heavy comp sync only on publish/comp changes; return 200 after the local commit with a sync_status field instead of failing.
findings.verify_note: Alliance sources enqueue and process inline. The comp is re-copied for every target on each update, and MAX_TARGETS_PER_TICK is 12. The claim that errors are returned after commit applies only to guild-origin mirrors, where sync_owner_change_to_copies returns the converge error with ?. Alliance-origin failures are deliberately swallowed and logged (lifecycle.rs:140-147). The finding is therefore partly overstated. Severity is lowered.

findings.title: Event edit cannot clear the description; flash page shows no status; web edit always resends comp
