findings.description: The edit form sends `description: undefined` when empty and the backend only applies `Some(description)`, so a description can never be removed once set. The flash-mass detail page renders no status badge, no start/stop/cancel controls and no archive, so web users cannot tell whether a flash mass is live/cancelled. PATCH always carries comp_id, so a stale draft silently re-applies it.
findings.fix: Use null-aware optional semantics in UpdateEventRequest (explicit null clears), render status and lifecycle actions for flash masses, and send only changed fields.
findings.verify_note: The edit form sends description || undefined, and UpdateEventRequest.description is Option<String>, so a description cannot be cleared. The flash detail page shows no status. The remaining claim is trivial.

logic_questions: Should alliance roster seat assignments (roster room), officer add/remove of participants, and extra roster roles propagate to the guild copies (one shared roster) or should each guild copy keep its own independent roster with only signups flowing up? Today signups flow guild->alliance (attributed) and alliance->attributed guild, but seats and officer edits flow nowhere.

Alliance-origin events are copied to guilds with discord_role_ids cleared because role ids belong to the alliance Discord server. Do you want a per-guild default ping role (or a role mapping per alliance event) so guild copies still ping their members, or is no ping on guild copies intended?

Who is allowed to provision voice and run Mass/Start/notifications for a guild copy of an alliance event: the guild bot (tenant-local, as lifecycle.rs documents) or only the alliance? Currently the code blocks the guild bot (403) while the docs say voice stays tenant-local. Options: allow bot-system/tenant-local mutations on copies, or move Discord side effects to a backend queue per tenant.

Should events auto-start at start_time and auto-mass at mass_time without any officer action (current bot behaviour), or should automatic start be an opt-in per event / per guild setting? And should an event that is auto-started with zero participants be allowed?

Should the legacy ping_alliance path (guild event -> mirror event in the alliance tenant plus a direct bot post to the alliance channel) be retired in favour of the alliance-origin fanout, and should a mirrored guild event remain a one-way snapshot or keep converging (comp, roles, roster roles) like fanout copies?

Alliance-owned events: who earns completion XP when a copy completes in a guild? README says mirrors/copies are not award authorities and the alliance tenant has no worker (so even its XP retry never runs). Should guild members receive XP for attending alliance events, and in which tenant ledger?

Flash masses can only be created and joined from Discord and are read-only on the web. Is web create/manage/join for flash masses expected (parity goal), and should flash masses fan out to alliance guilds (ping_alliance and alliance fanout are currently rejected for flash)?

Should joining or leaving an event after it is stopped/auto-stopped (and after the XP participant snapshot) be blocked by the backend, as the Discord UI does, or allowed for late attendance corrections?

Is the per-event discord_delivery column meant to override the guild's discord_event_delivery setting (calendar/message/forum) per event, or should it be removed in favour of the guild-level setting that the bot actually uses?

For alliance events, should a guild copy keep its own linked AlbionBB battles, regear and splits (each guild links its own battles since copies converge started_at/stopped_at), or should only the owning tenant link battles and share results with the copies?

summary:
The money flow works like this. A guild member creates a split. Anyone with `splits.create` can, and the seeded "User" role has it. The split carries estimated value, repair, bags, fee and weighted participants, and starts `pending`, or `awaiting_event` if linked to a live event. Completing it computes `net_value` and writes one `pending` `split_credit` bank row per participant, with the last participant taking the rounding remainder. The complete, not-completed and lost endpoints are allowed for the split's creator or anyone with `splits.edit`. A member then moves credits through `pending` -> `requested` -> `withdrawn` (officer accept) or `rejected`, or donates the share. The balance is derived live from ledger rows, and `consolidate_user_open_credits` runs inside the GET balance and list reads. Completed splits can be amended in place: reconcile rewrites open rows and inserts negative "clawback" rows for amounts already settled. Regear creates a `regear_credit` bank row on officer accept and spends a request credit when the member asks. Giveaways credit a `giveaway_credit` row on draw. Siphoned settlement writes a `donated` ledger row. Event economy and the intel report aggregate these rows.

For alliances, a bank tenant has no ledger of its own. Reads fan out to member guild schemas and mutations proxy into one guild. Alliance-owned event splits use a durable control-plane batch to insert guild-local ledger rows. Guild splits reach an alliance only as a one-shot read-only snapshot when an event is mirrored.

The Discord forum sync works as follows. The bot polls `GET /api/splits/discord-sync`, ordered by `(updated_at, id)`. For each item it fetches `/{id}/discord-sync`, edits the forum summary and tag, and advances a cursor stored in the bot's local state file. Bank mutations bump `splits.updated_at` so the poller sees them. Giveaways are announced by a poller that keeps its own local lists of announced ids, and auto-draw runs inside the event-session worker.

The main defects are:
- **Self-payout path:** the creator of a split can complete it, with a self-chosen fee and value.
- **Event-linked roster rewrites:** event sync rewrites the roster of already-closed splits.
- **Stranded splits:** a cancelled event leaves its splits stuck in `awaiting_event`.
- **One-shot alliance sync:** the split snapshot to the alliance is taken once and never refreshed.
- **Discord net pool:** the bot computes the pending net pool by adding string decimals.
- **Lost updates:** regear credits are spent with a read-modify-write that can be overspent.
- **Bot sync stall:** one failing split blocks the whole split sync.
- **Giveaway draw timing:** auto-draw is coupled to an unrelated worker.
- **Ledger writes on read:** the GET paths rewrite the ledger without a transaction.

findings.title: Any member can create AND complete their own split (self-payout path), with a self-chosen fee and value
findings.description: The seed migration gives the built-in `User` role `splits.create`. `create_split` accepts `fee` (0..100) and `estimated_market_value` from the creator with no further check. `authorize_split_owner_or_global` then lets the creator call `/complete`, `/complete-batch`, `/lost`, `/not-completed` and `/archive` on their own split, even without `splits.edit` or `splits.delete`. The OpenAPI text says 'Requires the Admin or Officer role', but the code does not enforce it. A normal member can create a split with themselves (and alts) as participants, fee 0 and a huge value, complete it, and get `pending` bank credits. The only remaining gate is the officer who later accepts the withdrawal. The web UI mirrors the same rule in `canActOnSplit`.
findings.fix: Make complete, lost, not-completed, archive and unarchive require `splits.edit`/`splits.delete` regardless of ownership. Optionally allow the owner to archive only while the split is still pending with no credits. Restrict `fee` and bag/value overrides on create to users with `splits.edit`; otherwise force the guild default fee. Fix the OpenAPI summaries. Make the frontend's `canActOnSplit` match the backend.
findings.verify_note: Verified. User role is seeded with splits.create (m20260902_000004:42-52). create_split only requires SplitsCreate and accepts fee and value. authorize_split_owner_or_global at router.rs:32-45 lets the creator through. complete_split and the batch route both use it. The batch OpenAPI text at router.rs:~745 documents creator-completes as intended, but the complete_split text says Admin/Officer, so the docs contradict each other. The self-payout is real, but credits are only pending and an officer still has to accept the withdrawal, so this is a privilege and fraud-surface weakness. Severity lowered from high to medium.

findings.title: Discord split summary computes the pending pool by adding decimal STRINGS; net pool, fee line and chart are wrong
findings.description: The backend serialises `Decimal` fields as strings. The utoipa schema for `estimated_market_value`, `fee`, `repair_value`, `bags_value` and `net_value` is `value_type = String`, and the web client wraps everything in `Number()`. The bot types declare `number` and do no normalisation. `pendingSplitPool` runs `split.estimated_market_value - split.repair_value + split.bags_value`. With strings that is `(number) + "50.00"`, i.e. string concatenation, so `"1000.00"-"100.00"+"50.00"` becomes `"90050.00"`. The 'Net Split Pool' on every pending or awaiting forum post is then roughly 10x or more too large. The 'Guild Fee' line and the allocation chart are also wrong, even on completed splits, because `taxAmount` always comes from the broken pool. The unit tests pass because they use JS numbers, so this is invisible in CI. It is also business logic that duplicates `calculate_net_value` outside the backend, and JS `Math.round` rounds half away from zero while `rust_decimal::round_dp` rounds half to even.
findings.fix: Have the backend return the pool preview (`pool_before_fee`, `fee_amount`, `net_preview`) in `SplitDetail`/`SplitSummary`, computed by `calculate_net_value`. Have the bot only render it. As a stop-gap, coerce with `Number()` in the bot API layer, and add a test fixture with string decimals.
findings.verify_note: Verified. Decimal fields are declared value_type=String in models.rs:70-84. bot types.ts:178-185 declares number and the client does only 'as ApiResponse<T>' casts, with no Number() coercion. In split-summary.ts:54, 'est - repair + bags' with string operands gives a number followed by string concatenation. The pending net pool, fee line and chart are wrong on Discord forum posts. Net value for completed splits is also routed through formatting of a string. Real defect that tests miss.

findings.title: Event roster sync rewrites rosters of completed / not_completed / lost splits and overrides officer roster edits
findings.description: `sync_event_participants` loops every split with that `event_id` and calls `sync_participants_from_event` before checking status, so it also runs on `completed`, `not_completed` and `lost` splits. After a split is paid, a late join or a cancel on the event (there is no status guard in `cancel_participation`) deletes or adds rows in `split_participants` without reconciling credits. A later amend (fee change, weight change) then runs `reconcile_completed_split_credits` over the mutated roster. A late signer gets paid a share of a split they did not attend, and someone who cancelled gets a clawback or their credit deleted. Sync is also a full set reconciliation. It deletes participants an officer added manually who are not signed up for the event, and restores participants an officer removed, on every signup or cancel. This contradicts the `update_split` doc and the test 'updating_a_linked_split_does_not_restore_removed_participants'. The call after `stop_event` runs outside the event's transaction with `?`, so a sync error returns 500 although the stop already committed.
findings.fix: In `sync_event_participants`, skip splits that are not `pending`/`awaiting_event`. Persist an 'officer-managed roster' flag, or a tombstone list of removed users, so sync only adds new signups and never deletes or re-adds manual edits. Run sync best-effort (log the error) after stop/join/leave. Decide explicitly whether late joiners should be added to a completed split.
findings.verify_note: Verified. sync_event_participants (splits/service.rs:1401-1428) calls sync_participants_from_event for every split of the event before the status check, so completed, not_completed and lost splits are mutated. This is called from stop_event, join and cancel_participation (events/service.rs:4053, 4915, 4975) and from the event mirror sync. Set reconciliation deletes manually added participants and re-adds removed ones. The post-commit call uses '?', so a sync error returns 500 after the stop has committed. The consequences of later reconcile_completed_split_credits are plausible but were not fully traced.

findings.title: Cancelling or unlinking an event strands splits in awaiting_event; lost / not-completed only work from pending
findings.description: `cancel_event` never touches linked splits. A split linked to a live or scheduled event is `awaiting_event`, and `complete_split` requires `event_has_ended` (only `stopped`/`auto_stopped`), so it can never be completed. `close_split` calls `load_with_status(.., Pending, ..)`, so `/lost` and `/not-completed` return 400 for `awaiting_event` splits. The only exit is archive, which hides the problem. `update_split` with `event_id: null` unlinks the event but leaves status `awaiting_event`, so the status drifts away from the data. `uncancel_event` also does not resync. The frontend shows a close button for awaiting_event (split-detail.ts around line 180), and clicking it gets a 400.
findings.fix: Allow `close_split` from both `Pending` and `AwaitingEvent`. On `cancel_event` and `uncancel_event`, and when an event is unlinked from a split, call a single `SplitService::reconcile_status_for_event` that recomputes the status. A cancelled event should mean the split is either `pending` (completable) or officer-closable.
findings.verify_note: Partly confirmed. cancel_event (events/service.rs:3876-3905) never touches linked splits. complete_split requires event_has_ended (stopped/auto_stopped only), so a cancelled event keeps the split uncompletable. close_split uses load_with_status(..., Pending), so lost and not-completed fail for any awaiting_event split. Overstated part: unlinking via update_split leaves the status as awaiting_event, but complete_split then has no event_id and succeeds, so that case is status drift, not a strand. Archive is the only exit for cancelled-event splits. Lowered to medium.

findings.title: Guild->alliance split sync is a one-shot snapshot at mirror creation; never refreshed on completion, and the copy spawns a second Discord forum post
findings.description: `create_mirror` returns early if an `event_sync_links` row already exists (line 67). The only automatic `share_split` call is inside `create_mirror` and only when a split already exists for the event. In practice the guild split is created after the event, or completed after the event ends, so the alliance either never gets a split or keeps a stale snapshot (`pending`, `net_value` NULL, old roster). Nothing refreshes it on split create, complete, amend, lost or archive. `attach_shared_split_to_event` sets `origin_read_only=false` on the alliance copy so the alliance bot poller creates its own forum post, while `deny_mutation` still blocks all mutations in alliance tenants. The result is a second, uneditable, stale thread. The snapshot also carries no credit status, so alliance `share_amount` falls back to `net*weight/total` without the remainder. This is the 'alliance must sync everything with member guilds' gap for splits.
findings.fix: Add an outbox-style hook: after `SplitService` create, update, complete, close and archive, and after bank status changes, enqueue a refresh of the share row (reuse the retry/idempotency pattern of the event mirror retry system). Make `create_mirror` and the event sync path re-run `share_split` for the latest linked split. Mark mirror copies `origin_read_only=true` and read-only in Discord discovery, or deliberately link a single forum thread to both tenants.
findings.verify_note: Verified. share_split is called from events/sync.rs:203 only inside create_mirror, and otherwise only from the manual router endpoint. Nothing refreshes the alliance copy on split create, complete, amend or archive. Staleness is confirmed. The 'second forum post' part is deliberate: the code comment at alliance_share/service.rs:~417 says the mirrored split is meant to be live on both Discord servers, so that part is a design choice, not a defect. The missing refresh is a real sync gap.

findings.title: Alliance-owned split distribution is unreachable from the web UI and has no progress or retry UI; retry can be permanently blocked
findings.description: The backend routes `complete` for alliance tenants to `alliance_distribution::complete`. The frontend, however, sets `isReadOnly = isAllianceTenant() || origin_read_only` and `actionablePendingSplits` returns nothing for alliance tenants, so the alliance cannot trigger distribution from the site. The `distribution-status` endpoint (router.rs:127) is never called by the frontend or the bot, so failures (`last_error`, per-recipient state) are invisible. The batch is also fragile. `load_or_create_batch` re-computes `participant_shares` from `ParticipantEntity::find()` with no ORDER BY and compares the amounts to the stored items. If the physical row order changed, the remainder goes to a different participant and every retry fails with 'shares changed after distribution began'. The only advertised fix, 'reconcile the existing batch', does not exist as an endpoint. Preflight also hard-fails the whole batch if any participant has a zero share or a missing identity.
findings.fix: Add an alliance-aware 'Distribute to guilds' action and a distribution status panel (poll `distribution-status`, retry button) in the web UI, plus the equivalent Discord surface. Sort participants by `user_id` before computing shares (in `complete_split`, `reconcile` and the distribution code). Persist the share plan in the batch and resume from it. Add an endpoint to cancel or rebuild a failed batch.
findings.verify_note: Verified. The frontend sets isReadOnly for alliance tenants (split-detail.ts:1052) and canAct and canActOn are false for them (splits.ts:1233-1240). grep finds no use of distribution-status in the frontend or the bot. The backend alliance_distribution::complete is therefore unreachable from the UI and failure state is invisible. The ordering claim is weak: participants are loaded without ORDER BY (alliance_distribution.rs:164), but projections are sorted by discord_id before the batch compare, and alliance participant mutations are blocked, so the retry-poisoning scenario is unlikely. Hard-fail preflight on zero share or missing identity is confirmed (lines 215-290). The core UI and observability gap stands.

findings.title: Regear request credits are spent with an unlocked read-modify-write: concurrent requests overspend; self-service duplicate guard is racy
findings.description: `consume_request_credit` reads the balance row and writes `balance-1` with no `FOR UPDATE` and no conditional `WHERE balance > 0`. Under READ COMMITTED, two concurrent `request_regear` calls on different deaths, or on the same death, both read 1 and both succeed. The comment says 'concurrent clicks cannot overspend', which is false. `request_regear` also flips status without a conditional update, so the same death can be requested twice and consume two credits. `create_self_service_request` checks `has_active_self_report` outside the transaction and there is no unique index, so two parallel POSTs create two pending self-reported requests for one event (two payouts). A first `get_or_create_balance` insert also races on the primary key. Self-service pricing failure is silently replaced with an empty breakdown and total 0 (`unwrap_or_else`).
findings.fix: Use `UPDATE regear_request_balances SET weekly_balance = weekly_balance-1 WHERE user_id=$1 AND weekly_balance>0 RETURNING ...` (or lock the row with `FOR UPDATE`). Flip the death status with a conditional `update_many`. Add a partial unique index on `(event_id, user_id)` for pending/approved self-reports. Fail the request or flag it when pricing fails instead of storing 0.
findings.verify_note: Verified. consume_request_credit (regear/credits.rs:~110-130) does a plain read then update of balance-1 with no FOR UPDATE and no conditional WHERE. request_regear flips status without a conditional update. create_self_service_request checks has_active_self_report outside the txn and there is no unique index (the migration comment admits it). Pricing failure falls back to an empty breakdown (service.rs:~886). The races need deliberate concurrent requests from the same user, and an officer still approves, so the impact is limited. Medium.

findings.title: Bot split forum poller stops at the first failing split (head-of-line blocking) and its cursor can skip late-committed updates
findings.description: In `checkSplitSync`, `if (!await adapter.sync(item)) return;` aborts the whole pass without advancing the `(updated_at,id)` cursor. One permanently failing split (a thread the bot cannot edit, a missing tag, a forum permission change, an event-linked archived split whose post cannot be deleted) blocks every later split forever, and the log only shows warnings. The cursor lives in the bot's local state file, not in the backend. `updated_at` is stamped with `Utc::now()` inside open transactions (`touch_linked_splits`, `touch_split_ids`), so a transaction that commits after the poller has advanced past its timestamp is never rediscovered.
findings.fix: On a per-item failure, log it, record a retry counter or backoff in the bot state, and continue to the next item. Keep the cursor behind the oldest failed item, using a separate retry queue. Stamp `updated_at` with DB `now()` and re-scan with a small overlap window, or add a monotonically increasing `sync_revision` column. Store the cursor and `thread_id` in the backend.
findings.verify_note: Verified. poller.ts:1925-1936 returns from the whole pass when adapter.sync returns false, and the cursor is not advanced, so one persistently failing split blocks all later ones. The cursor is in the bot state (this.state.splitUpdatedAt). The late-commit cursor skip is plausible: updated_at is stamped with Utc::now() inside transactions. Medium, because it only bites when a failure is persistent.

findings.title: Giveaway auto-draw is coupled to the event-session worker: skipped for tenants without Albion scope and aborted by auto-stop errors
findings.description: `draw_due` is called only from `run_cycle`. `prepare_cycle` returns `None` (no cycle) when the tenant is not an active `guild`, or when the Albion scope is not configured, so no giveaway deadline ever fires for those tenants (a giveaway tenant with no Albion setup, alliance tenants). Even where the cycle runs, `auto_stop_expired_sessions(...).await?` is called before `draw_due`, so any auto-stop error returns early and skips drawing for that tick. A giveaway whose `ends_at` has passed stays `open` (the entry endpoints return 'this giveaway has ended') until an officer force-draws.
findings.fix: Move giveaway draws, XP retry and other money-affecting jobs into their own worker loop that only needs an active tenant. At minimum, call `draw_due` before the Albion-dependent passes and ignore their errors.
findings.verify_note: Verified. draw_due is called only from run_cycle (event_sessions/mod.rs:129). prepare_cycle returns None for non-guild tenants or when the Albion scope is not configured (mod.rs:104-108). auto_stop_expired_sessions(...).await? at line 128 precedes draw_due, so an auto-stop error skips the draw for that tick. No other caller of draw_due exists. Real coupling. Medium, because most active guilds have Albion configured.

findings.title: Giveaway draw can double-credit the regear bonus under a race, and a failed credit_bonus poisons the Postgres transaction
findings.description: `draw` reads the giveaway without a row lock and does its side effects before the conditional flip. On a lost race (`flip.rows_affected != 1`) it deletes the silver transaction but then `txn.commit()`s, so the `credit_bonus` write already made to the winner's regear balance is committed. Two concurrent draws (officer 'Draw now' plus the worker) can each add the bonus, and the second winner keeps the extra credits. `credit_bonus` errors are caught and logged, but on Postgres any failed statement aborts the transaction, so the next statement fails and the whole draw errors out. The same unlocked read-then-write pattern allows two winners to be recorded in the audit log and notifications.
findings.fix: Lock the giveaway row (`FOR UPDATE`) or do the conditional flip to `drawn` first, and only then insert the silver credit and regear bonus. On a lost race, roll back (return Err or drop the txn) instead of committing.
findings.verify_note: Code confirmed. giveaways/service.rs:436-480 inserts the silver credit and calls credit_bonus before the conditional flip. On a lost race (rows_affected != 1) it deletes only the silver row and then commits, so the regear bonus stays. A failed credit_bonus statement would abort the Postgres txn. The race needs a concurrent officer draw and worker draw on the same giveaway, which is rare. Low.

findings.title: GET /bank/balance and GET /bank/transactions rewrite the ledger without a transaction or lock; consolidation can delete or corrupt rows
findings.description: `consolidate_user_open_credits` is invoked from read paths with a plain `DatabaseConnection`, so every step autocommits. It deletes the extra rows (line 231) before it updates the surviving row's amount (line 241). A failure between the two loses money. It also deletes or updates rows by id with no status guard, while `request_withdrawal` and `accept_withdrawal` can change those rows concurrently. Only `request_withdrawal` takes the advisory lock. A row that has just become `requested` or `withdrawn` can be deleted (line 257) or have its amount overwritten. Absorbing a clawback deletes the negative `Withdrawn` ledger row (lines 269-276) and shrinks a credit of another split. `reconcile_completed_split_credits` assumes per-split clawback rows exist, so a later amend of the original split re-creates the clawback or restores the credit (double deduction or lost deduction). Ledger rows are deleted despite the 'immutable ledger' stance in the docs. The alliance list path calls this once per 200-row page per guild.
findings.fix: Make reads side-effect free (derive the net balance in SQL or in memory). Run consolidation only in write paths, inside a transaction with `serialize_user_requestable_balance`, and with `status IN (pending,rejected)` guards on every update and delete. Keep clawbacks and per-split rows and net them in queries instead of deleting them.
findings.verify_note: Verified. get_balance (bank/service.rs:411) and list_transactions (668) call consolidate_user_open_credits on a plain DatabaseConnection, with no txn and no lock. It deletes extra rows before updating the survivor (lines 228-243) and has no status guards on delete or update by id. Reads that mutate the ledger are a real design defect. The concurrency corruption scenarios are plausible but narrow.

findings.title: Share remainder goes to 'the last participant' of an unordered query; cent drift and spurious clawbacks
findings.description: `participant_shares` gives the rounding remainder to the last element, but the callers load participants with no ORDER BY (`complete_split`, `reconcile_completed_split_credits`, `alliance_distribution::complete`). A weight update on a row can move its tuple in Postgres and change who is 'last'. Completing and later amending the same split can therefore give the remainder to different people, so reconcile generates +/-0.01 delta rows and tiny negative clawbacks. `round_dp` is banker's rounding and the frontend and bot preview use half-up, so the previews disagree with the paid amounts by a cent. `complete_split` also reads values, roster and fee outside the transaction and flips on status only, so a concurrent edit between the read and the flip pays stale shares. A tiny last weight can produce a negative share that `complete_split` inserts as a `pending` negative credit.
findings.fix: Sort by `user_id` (or weight, user_id) in all three places. Clamp or assert `share >= 0`. Compute shares inside the same transaction as the flip, with a version or `updated_at` check. Return the per-participant share preview from the backend and delete the client-side re-implementations.
findings.verify_note: Code facts confirmed: participant_shares gives the remainder to the last element, and ParticipantEntity::find() has no ORDER BY in complete_split (service.rs:2159), reconcile (213) and alliance_distribution (164). Heap order can change after row updates, so remainder drift is possible but unproven. Banker's rounding vs frontend half-up gives at most one-cent preview differences. The negative-share edge case is theoretical. Cent-level, so low.

findings.title: Alliance split credits written into guild ledgers lack split link, audit and notification, and are reported as guild 'other outflow'
findings.description: `project_one` inserts raw SQL into the guild `transactions` table with `split_id = NULL`, so the guild's bank and split UI cannot show which split the credit came from. No `TRANSACTION_CREATED` audit row and no `SplitCredited` notification are written for the member. `compute_economy` classifies a withdrawn row with `split_id IS NULL` that is not a regear as `outflow_other` and subtracts it from `guild_treasury_net`. So when a member cashes out an alliance-funded split, the guild's treasury is charged for it (and no tax is credited). Separately, the alliance `accept_withdrawal` and `reject_withdrawal` resolve the target guild via `resolve_target_guild(.., &caller.discord_id)`, which looks for bank rows belonging to the OFFICER, so an officer with no personal rows gets 'no member guild has bank rows' unless `guild_tenant_id` is passed (the bot cannot pass it).
findings.fix: Store the alliance reference in a nullable `source_alliance_split_id` column (already present) and exclude those rows from guild `outflow_other` (or report them separately). Route the insert through `BankService` so audit and notification happen. In alliance accept/reject use `resolve_explicit_or_only_member` and require an explicit guild.
findings.verify_note: Verified. project_one (alliance_distribution.rs:508-516) inserts raw SQL with split_id NULL and no audit or notification. compute_economy (intel/report.rs:1086-1125) puts withdrawn rows with no split_id and no regear id into outflow_other, which reduces guild_treasury_net (line 1192). The alliance accept_withdrawal and reject_withdrawal (bank/alliance.rs:~518-560) use resolve_target_guild with caller.discord_id, which looks only for the officer's own rows unless guild_tenant_id is given. The 'column already present' claim is correct (source_alliance_split_id).

findings.title: Siphoned energy balance collapses legitimately identical ledger rows, and settlement writes a donated row that does not reduce anything and has reversed direction
findings.description: Every balance query dedupes with `GROUP BY lower(player_name), occurred_at, reason, amount, source`, and `siphoned_net` uses a HashSet on the same key. Albion export timestamps have only second resolution, so two real deposits of the same amount and reason in the same second count once, and a debt is under-stated. The ingest key is the same, so such rows are silently skipped. Settlement inserts a bank row with `status=donated`, `from_user_id=NULL`, `to_user_id=<member>`, `to_guild_bank=false`. The admin analytics then labels the source 'Guild Bank' and the destination as the member, which is the reverse of what a debt payment is, and donated rows never change the member's balance. `total = debt * unit_price` is not rounded to 2 decimals. `create_entry` stores `albion_export` instead of `manual`. The manual-entry source enum is never used.
findings.fix: Add an explicit ledger identity from the export (line number or row hash with a per-export sequence) instead of collapsing on value equality. Settlement should set `from_user_id=member`, `to_guild_bank=true`. Round `total` to 2 dp. Use `SiphonedEntrySource::Manual` for manual rows.
findings.verify_note: The GROUP BY collapse on (name, occurred_at, reason, amount, source) is confirmed (siphoned/service.rs:576-605), but it is a deliberate dedupe for re-ingest idempotency, so the true loss is only for identical same-second rows. Settlement row confirmed as donated with from_user_id NULL, to_user_id member and to_guild_bank false (service.rs:809-825), unlike donate_share (bank/service.rs:606-612), which sets from=member and to_guild_bank=true. So the settlement direction is inconsistent. total = debt * unit_price is unrounded. Low.

findings.title: Event economy defines 'income' as distributed net value, contradicting the guild report; loss-estimate writer overwrites good data with zeros
findings.description: `get_event_economy` sets `income_total = sum(net_value)` of completed splits and `net = income - regear_paid`. But `net_value` is what was paid out to members, not guild income. The intel report treats guild income as the retained fee (`split_tax_total`) and `guild_treasury_net = tax + donated - regear - other`. The two screens give different, contradictory P&L for the same event, and `regear_requested_total` sums `auto_estimate_total` of every death (including rejected and merely available ones). It also includes archived splits and does not filter alliance mirror copies. `persist_battle_loss_estimate` replaces the whole row on each recompute and swallows price API failures (`unwrap_or_default`), so a transient AODP outage overwrites a priced estimate with partial or zero values. The read-then-insert is unprotected against concurrent recompute (unique violation).
findings.fix: Define one ledger-based P&L in the backend (tax retained, split payouts, regear paid) and have both endpoints use it. Do not overwrite an existing estimate when the price lookup fails or returns fewer priced items. Upsert with `ON CONFLICT (battle_id)`.
findings.verify_note: Code confirmed. get_event_economy sums net_value of completed splits as income and sums auto_estimate_total of all deaths as requested. It does not filter archived or mirror splits. persist_battle_loss_estimate replaces the whole row and swallows price failures (unwrap_or_default). The 'contradicts the intel report' point is a definitional choice, and the estimates are informational and never summed into net. The overwrite on outage is the real defect. Low.

findings.title: Split lifecycle actions are not audited; audit rows for payouts are written outside the transaction; Discord audit feed is therefore incomplete
findings.description: Complete, lost, not-completed, update (including post-completion amendments that move money), archive and participant changes write no audit entry. Only `TRANSACTION_CREATED` is logged, on `db` (a separate pooled connection), so the entry persists even if the surrounding payout transaction later fails and rolls back. A completed-split amendment (clawbacks, deletions, amounts rewritten) leaves no trace. `get_sync` hydrates audit rows and all transactions per split on every poll but the bot never renders them (it only uses `detail`), so the 'audit' and 'transaction' cursors in `UpdateSyncState` are dead weight.
findings.fix: Audit every state change inside the same transaction (SPLIT_COMPLETED, SPLIT_CLOSED, SPLIT_AMENDED with before/after, SPLIT_ARCHIVED). Either use the audit and transaction feed in the forum thread, or drop it from `get_sync` and the cursors.
findings.verify_note: Verified. splits/service.rs contains a single AuditService::log call, TRANSACTION_CREATED at line 2228, made on db (not the txn) inside the payout loop. Complete, close, update, amend and archive write no audit rows, and router.rs has none either. This is a real audit gap. The claim that the Discord bot ignores the audit and transaction feed was not independently checked.

findings.title: Whole-ledger loads in request paths: bank analytics, guild summary, split KPIs, siphoned balances, alliance bank lists
findings.description: `get_analytics_summary` does `TransactionEntity::find().all(db)` and `get_guild_summary` loads every withdrawn row into memory; they should be SQL SUM/GROUP BY. `kpi_summary` loads every non-archived split and every participant row to count distinct users. `list_balances` re-scans and groups the entire siphoned table per request. The alliance `list_transactions` fetches every page of every member guild (each page also runs the write-side `consolidate`), sorts in memory, then slices one page, and guilds are visited sequentially. `admin-withdrawals` fetches a `GROUPING_FETCH_LIMIT` dataset and groups client-side. Discord's `get_sync` runs a full `to_detail` plus two unbounded-ish queries per split per poll.
findings.fix: Push aggregates into SQL (SUM/COUNT with GROUP BY). Add backend grouping (`GET /bank/withdrawal-queue` grouped by player). Do alliance pagination with a k-way merge or per-guild limit, and fan out concurrently. Add indexes on `transactions(to_user_id,status)` and `transactions(split_id)` if missing.
findings.verify_note: Verified. get_analytics_summary uses TransactionEntity::find().all(db) (bank/service.rs:483). kpi_summary loads all non-archived splits and all participant ids (splits/service.rs:1501-1540). The alliance list_transactions fans out sequentially over all guild pages, then sorts and slices in memory (bank/alliance.rs:336-376). Real scalability problems, though they only hurt at large ledger sizes. The frontend grouping and siphoned claims were not re-verified in detail.

findings.title: Frontend recomputes net, fee and per-participant shares (and groups bank credits) in the browser with different rounding
findings.description: The backend's own OpenAPI says 'don't recompute it client-side'. The web UI does anyway. `netOf`, `estimatedShare` (`Math.round(...*100)/100`, no remainder rule), `perParticipantShare` (`Math.round` to integer), the batch `selectedTotalNet`, and the draft preview all use floating point. They can disagree with the stored `net_value` and the paid shares by cents, or more once the roster changes. The bank page groups requestable credits per split in the browser. The regear accept dialog lets the officer edit unit prices and sums the breakdown client-side; the backend only verifies that the client's rows add up to the client's total (`sum_included`), so negative or inflated rows are accepted.
findings.fix: Add a backend `POST /splits/preview` (and a `preview` block on `SplitDetail`) returning net, fee and per-participant shares computed by `participant_shares`. Return pre-grouped credits from the bank API. Validate regear breakdown rows server-side (non-negative, quantity >= 1, bounded relative to the auto estimate unless an override permission is held).
findings.verify_note: Frontend recomputation confirmed (splits.ts:1196-1225 and split-detail.ts:559 use floats, Math.round and no remainder rule). These are previews, so the discrepancy is cents. The regear accept dialog is officer-only and the backend only checks that rows sum to the total (regear/service.rs:277-283). That matches an intentional officer override and is not a vulnerability. Lowered to low.

findings.title: Discord cannot do what the web can for splits, bank review, regear and siphoned energy
findings.description: The bot exposes only `/balance`, `/balance-request` and giveaway join/leave buttons. There is no split create, complete, lost or close action, no officer withdrawal accept or reject, no donate-share action, no regear request or review (the module has zero bot code), no siphoned view or settlement. The split forum post is read-only. `/balance` ignores `balance.guilds` for alliance tenants. The balance and request replies sum `Number(tx.amount)` in JS floats. The goal of 'same actions in similar ways, driven by backend logic' is not met.
findings.fix: Add thin bot commands and buttons (officer approve or reject withdrawal, complete or close split from the forum post, regear request and review queue, donate share) that call the existing REST endpoints, and render backend-computed values only. Share DTOs and Decimal handling in one typed client.
findings.verify_note: Partly refuted. The bot does have officer withdrawal accept and reject handlers (handlers/button.ts:1157 and 1194 call api/bank/transactions/withdraw/accept and /reject), so the claim 'no officer withdrawal accept/reject' is wrong. Confirmed gaps: no split create, complete or close action, no regear module and no siphoned code in the bot (grep finds regear/siphon only in types, balance text and tests). balance-request.ts:24 sums Number(tx.amount). The parity gap is real for splits, regear and siphoned, but the description is overstated.

findings.title: Giveaway Discord announcements: duplicate posts on partial failure, stale counts for web entries, state kept only in the bot file
findings.description: `checkNewGiveaways` sends the channel message and only then PUTs `discord-message` and appends to `postedGiveawayIds`. If the PUT fails, the exception skips the checkpoint and the next poll announces the same giveaway again. A failing first giveaway also blocks later ones in the loop. The Discord embed (entry count) is edited only on a Discord button click or after a draw, so entries made from the website never update the message. `postedGiveawayIds`/`announcedGiveawayDraws` are an unbounded array in the bot-local state file while the backend already stores `discord_message_id`, which is the real idempotency key. `checkGiveawayResults` marks a giveaway announced when the message fetch fails transiently (`.catch(() => null)`), so the draw edit and winner message are lost.
findings.fix: Use backend state as the source of truth: list giveaways with `discord_message_id IS NULL AND status='open'`, announce, then PUT; refresh messages whose `updated_at` changed (add `updated_at` or `entry_count` revision to the giveaway view). Only mark results as announced after a successful edit. Process items independently.
findings.verify_note: Verified. checkNewGiveaways (poller.ts:2063-2116) sends the message and then PUTs discord-message, and lastGiveawayId advances only after the whole loop, so a PUT failure re-announces on the next poll, and an exception in the first item aborts the later ones. checkGiveawayResults treats a failed message fetch as null and still marks the giveaway announced (lines 2135-2150), so the edit and winner message are lost. postedGiveawayIds lives in the bot-local state. Moderate robustness issue, low.

findings.title: Smaller correctness gaps: self-approval of withdrawals and regears, manual transactions linked to splits get clobbered, admin edits skip state rules, roster truncation
findings.description: (a) `accept_withdrawal` and `accept_request` do not forbid the acting officer from being the recipient, so an officer can request and approve their own payout or regear (code even handles the 'officer is also the recipient' case in notifications). (b) `create_transaction` and `update_transaction` accept `split_id` on `manual_adjustment` rows and arbitrary status, so reconcile treats them as part of the split's credit and may merge or delete them on the next amend; an admin PATCH can set a row to `withdrawn` without `from_user_id`/`withdrawn_at`, or change the amount of an already-paid row. (c) Negative manual amounts become `donated` rows and do not reduce the member's withdrawable balance, only `split_credit` clawbacks do. (d) Reconcile can change the amount of a `requested` row under the officer's feet without re-requesting. (e) The Discord summary silently cuts the roster at 25 players or 1024 characters with no '+N more'.
findings.fix: Add a configurable no-self-approval rule. Reject `split_id` unless `type=split_credit` and enforce a legal status-transition table in `update_transaction`. Reset `requested` rows to `pending` on amount change. Paginate or add a 'N more' line in the Discord roster.
findings.verify_note: Code confirmed. accept_withdrawal and accept_request have no self-approval guard (accept_withdrawal even handles the officer-is-recipient notification case). create_transaction accepts split_id and arbitrary type and status on manual rows (bank/service.rs:1165-1250). All of this is admin or officer-gated policy and hygiene, and the roster-truncation point was not re-verified. Low.

logic_questions: Should the creator of a split be allowed to complete, close or archive it, or only holders of `splits.edit`/`splits.delete`? The OpenAPI text says Admin/Officer-only, but the code (and the web UI) lets the creator act. Should regular members even be allowed to set `fee` and values on create? Options: (A) any member can request a split but only officers can finalize it; (B) only officers create and finalize; (C) members may finalize their own split only if an officer approves the withdrawals (today's accidental behavior).

What should happen to `awaiting_event` splits when their event is cancelled? Options: (A) revert to `pending` so they can be paid or closed manually; (B) auto-close as `not_completed`; (C) keep waiting until the event is un-cancelled.

Should event sign-ups remain the live source of truth for a linked split's roster for the whole lifetime of the split, or only until the officer first edits the roster or the split completes? If a completed split's event gets a late joiner or a cancellation, should payouts change?

What is the intended definition of event/guild 'income' for the economy views: retained fee (tax), net distributed to members, or loot gross? The event P&L (`net_value - regear`) and the guild report (`tax + donated - regear - other`) disagree today.

For guild-owned splits shared to an alliance: should the alliance copy be a live mirror (status, net, credit status refreshed automatically, one shared Discord thread) or a manual one-time snapshot? Today it is a one-time snapshot taken only if a split already exists when the event is mirrored.

For alliance-owned splits: who may trigger distribution and where (web alliance tenant, a Discord alliance server, both)? The web UI is read-only for alliance tenants today. Should alliance-funded payouts count as guild treasury outflow in the member guild's financial report, or be tracked separately?

Siphoned energy settlement: is it a record of an in-game cash payment received (guild bank gains silver, so it should be a donation from the member to the guild bank), or should it deduct from the member's bank balance? Also: is collapsing identical (player, time, reason, amount, source) rows intentional (de-duping re-uploaded exports) even though two real identical deposits in the same second are lost?

Rounding policy for shares and fees: banker's rounding (current Rust `round_dp`) vs half-up (what JS and users expect)? Should the remainder always go to the highest-weight participant, the first, or the last by user id?
May an officer approve their own withdrawal request or regear? Should regear credit be refunded when an officer rejects a request, and should members be able to re-request a rejected death?

Giveaways: should silver prizes be funded from (and capped by) the guild bank balance, or can any officer with `giveaways.create` mint arbitrary silver? Should winners be re-validated (still a guild member) at draw time, and should auto-draw run independently of the Albion/event worker?

summary: Identity model: a Discord snowflake maps to a per-tenant `users` row in each tenant schema. The web session is an encrypted 7-day `session_user` cookie holding a profile snapshot (roles, tenant_id, permissions). It is rewritten with a fresh 7-day max_age on every `/api/auth/me` call. Tenant resolution (`tenant.rs`) takes the tenant from the cookie, or from `X-Guild-Id` only when `X-Bot-Secret` is valid. It then pins the tenant's DB pool, a per-tenant `Permissions` cache keyed by role NAME, the feature flags and the tenant kind into request extensions. The `UserContext` extractor (`rbac.rs`) has two paths. Cookie path: it re-resolves `user_id` from the discord_id, queries the control DB for tenant-owner status, and, if a bot token is configured, calls Discord for the member's roles (60 s in-process cache). It then maps role ids onto the tenant's `roles` table. A 404 from Discord means "absent", which falls back to the default role. An outage keeps the cookie roles. Bot path: `X-Bot-Secret` plus `X-Discord-Id` requires an existing local `users` row, otherwise 401. Roles come from the `X-Discord-Role-Ids` header, or from the stale `users.role` string when the header is missing. `X-Bot-Secret` without `X-Discord-Id` becomes a `bot_system` super-admin. Permissions are RBAC rows (`role_permissions`) mapped to a `Permission` enum. Platform admins and the guild tenant owner bypass every check. Platform admins live in a control-plane table cached in memory. Login (`auth/router.rs`) matches the user's OAuth guild list to registered tenants and either auto-selects one or shows `/choose-server`. `finalize_session` upserts the user, records a control-plane membership row, and snapshots roles, permissions and features into the cookie. Registration (`/api/tenants/register`) checks via the bot token that the caller owns or manages the Discord guild. It provisions the schema, sets `owner_discord_id`, and for alliances inserts pending or active `alliance_memberships`. Albion linking (`/api/albion/link`, `/register`) is self-service: it creates the link, sets the nickname, assigns the guild base role when the player is in the configured Albion guild, and fans out to the paired alliance or guild tenants. Role sync between Discord and the DB is lazy only. The bot has no member-add-remove-update or role-update handlers; its only member hook is `GuildMemberAdd` (auto-role, plus the alliance link adoption call). Web `/me` and the per-request live lookup rewrite `users.role`. The bot path never refreshes it. The admin panel can add or remove linked Discord roles through the Discord REST API. In summary, the Discord-to-DB direction is never pushed; it is only recomputed when a web request or bot header happens to arrive.

findings.title: Login upsert overwrites another user's discord_id when the Discord email matches (account takeover)
findings.description: `AuthService::upsert_user` (called by `finalize_session` on every login and tenant switch) first looks up by discord_id. If that misses, it looks up by email and calls `update_existing_user`, which unconditionally does `active.discord_id = Set(Some(profile.id))` (service.rs:530). The email is Discord's `/users/@me` email. The profile struct has no `verified` field, so unverified emails are accepted. An attacker who registers a Discord account carrying the victim's email, then logs in to any shared tenant, re-points the victim's `users` row (splits, bank, roles, history) to the attacker's snowflake. The safer `identity::upsert_discord_user` exists and states that email may only claim a row that has no discord_id. The alliance fan-out uses it, but the real login path does not.
findings.fix: Delete `AuthService::upsert_user` and call `identity::upsert_discord_user` from `finalize_session`. Deserialize Discord's `verified` flag and ignore unverified emails. Add a test: two Discord ids with the same email must produce two rows, and the old id must be kept.
findings.verify_note: Real. service.rs:475-517 falls back to an email match and update_existing_user (service.rs:520-543) sets discord_id unconditionally. finalize_session calls it at router.rs:745. DiscordUserProfile has no `verified` field. identity::upsert_discord_user only lets an email claim a row with a blank discord_id. Not critical, because the attacker needs a different Discord account whose email equals a stored users.email. Discord's own email uniqueness limits that, and it works mainly after a victim changed their Discord email or for admin-set real emails. It is still a genuine takeover primitive, so high.

findings.title: Bot refuses every command (including /register and /link) until the user has logged into the website once
findings.description: `executeSlashCommand` calls `isWebsiteUserRegistered`, which does `GET api/users/me`, on every command, including `/register`. The backend bot path 401s with 'has no linked account in this system' when no `users` row exists in that tenant schema (rbac.rs:320-325). Rows are created only by a web login (`finalize_session`), admin `POST /api/users`, or link fan-out. A Discord member who joins, runs `/register <ign>` and has never opened the website gets 'Website Account Required'. Discord onboarding therefore cannot work on its own, which contradicts 'Discord and web do the same things'. `GuildMemberAdd` on an alliance hub calls `api/albion/link/me` as the new member (index.ts:233-247). That also 401s unless the user already has a row in the alliance schema, so the adopt-existing-link sync silently never runs (the error is only logged). The extra `users/me` round trip also adds latency to every command.
findings.fix: Have the backend auto-provision the tenant `users` row on first bot request, using `identity::upsert_discord_user` with `X-Discord-Id` and a bot-supplied display name (the 'discord-<id>@alliance.local' pattern already exists in alliance_fanout.rs:543-557). Allow `/register`, `/link` and `link/me` for unprovisioned users. Remove the per-command `isWebsiteUserRegistered` gate.
findings.verify_note: Real. command-gate.ts:83 runs isWebsiteUserRegistered on every slash command, /register included. rbac.rs:320-325 returns 401 'has no linked account' when no users row exists, with no auto-provision. The same gate is in select.ts, button.ts and event-thread-command.ts. GuildMemberAdd calls link/me as the new member (index.ts:233-247). It 401s and is only logged. The gate is deliberate ('Website Account Required' reply), so it is a design blocker for Discord-only onboarding rather than a crash. Lowered from critical to high.

findings.title: No Discord to DB sync of members or roles: no member-remove/update or role-update handlers; users.role is stale
findings.description: The bot registers handlers for InteractionCreate, GuildCreate, GuildDelete, GuildMemberAdd and MessageCreate only. It has no GuildMemberRemove, GuildMemberUpdate, GuildRoleUpdate or GuildRoleDelete handler, and no periodic reconcile. `users.role` is only rewritten by `GET /auth/me` or by a cookie-authenticated request (`persist_highest_role`). The bot path never writes it. The roster, user list, role filter and sort (`filters.role` is an SQL `WHERE users.role = ?`) therefore show the role from that user's last web visit. Members who left Discord stay in the user list indefinitely. People who never log in on the web are not in the directory at all. This is the root of 'synchronizations that should exist do not work'.
findings.fix: Add the gateway events GuildMemberAdd, GuildMemberRemove, GuildMemberUpdate (role diff) and GuildRoleUpdate or GuildRoleDelete, posting to a backend `POST /api/members/sync` (bot-secret). The backend upserts the user, resolves `highest_role` and soft-marks departed members. Add a backend reconcile worker that diffs the guild member list (paged) against `users`. Stop filtering and sorting on the cached `users.role`, or refresh it in these handlers.
findings.verify_note: index.ts registers only InteractionCreate, GuildCreate, GuildDelete, GuildMemberAdd and MessageCreate. There is no GuildMemberRemove, GuildMemberUpdate or role handler, and no member reconcile worker. users.role is only written by persist_highest_role (rbac.rs:218-235) and the /auth/me path. users/service.rs:576-582 filters and sorts on the cached users.role.

findings.title: Tenant memberships are never revoked; users who left or were banned can still switch in with default-role access
findings.description: `user_tenant_memberships` is only ever INSERTed. There is no DELETE anywhere. `switch_tenant` authorizes purely on that table (`is_member`), then `finalize_session` runs with an empty access token. A confirmed-absent member (Discord 404) gets the default role, not a rejection, and `record_membership` re-inserts. A user kicked from a guild can keep switching into its tenant with the default role's permissions (view bank/splits/users, with the emails from auth-12). `list_session_tenants` also lists the tenant forever. Cross-tenant event attribution joins the same stale table.
findings.fix: Make `finalize_session` and `switch_tenant` reject (403) and delete the membership when the live lookup returns `Absent`. In `apply_live_guild_roles`, treat `Absent` as 'no session for this tenant' rather than the default role. Also delete memberships from the new GuildMemberRemove sync (auth-3).
findings.verify_note: The only SQL touching user_tenant_memberships is INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (platform/service.rs:1207) and SELECTs. There is no DELETE. switch_tenant (router.rs:415-451) authorizes on is_member alone. Absent maps to the default role in fetch_member_roles (service.rs:340-383) and login still records the membership. Impact is limited to default-role permissions, but it includes reading users and emails (see auth-12).

findings.title: Role revocation fails open and never expires: Unavailable keeps cookie roles; the cookie lifetime slides forever
findings.description: Any non-2xx, non-404 Discord response (403 when the bot is kicked or lacks Server Members access, 429 rate limit, 5xx, network error) maps to `Unavailable`, which keeps the cookie's old roles and never persists anything. With no configured bot token the live check is skipped entirely and roles are frozen at login. `/auth/me` re-issues the `session_user` cookie with a fresh `max_age(7 days)` on every call (router.rs:935-942). An officer demoted on Discord while the bot's Discord access is degraded keeps their old roles and permissions for as long as they keep using the app. There is no maximum staleness and no alert. The 60 s lookup cache is an unbounded `HashMap` that is never evicted (service.rs:629-635).
findings.fix: Stamp the cookie profile with `roles_checked_at`. If the live lookup has been unavailable for more than N minutes, downgrade to the default role or force re-auth. Do not slide the cookie lifetime on `/me`. Surface bot-access failures in the admin UI. Cap or evict the lookup cache.
findings.verify_note: Unavailable keeping cookie roles is deliberate and documented (service.rs:395-397, router.rs:897-901). The cookie is re-issued with max_age 7 days on every /me (router.rs:935-942). The lookup cache is an unbounded HashMap (service.rs:629-635), but it is bounded in practice by the number of users, so memory is not a real concern. The defect is real but needs a degraded Discord or bot-access scenario, so medium, not high.

findings.title: Alliance tenant owner gets no bypass and no seeded admin, so the alliance cannot be bootstrapped without a platform admin
findings.description: `is_guild_owner` returns true only when `kind == 'guild'` (a unit test pins this), so `is_tenant_owner` is false on alliance tenants. New tenant schemas seed roles 'Admin' (id 386488773351047168) and 'User' with `discord_role_id = NULL`, so no Discord role maps to Admin. After registering an alliance Discord, the registrar holds no permission there. They cannot link roles (`roles.manage`), set `discord_alliance_role_id` or hub settings (`admin.settings.manage`), or edit the matrix (`permissions.reload`). Only a platform admin can fix it. The inconsistency is visible in `require_tenant_feature_admin`, which accepts `owner_discord_id` regardless of kind.
findings.fix: Grant the alliance's `owner_discord_id` the same owner bypass on the alliance tenant. If the owner must not leave or alter membership, gate those specific actions on `AllianceLeave`, which already has its own check. Alternatively auto-link the seeded 'Admin' role to the registrar's top Discord role at registration.
findings.verify_note: guild_owner_matches requires kind=="guild" (platform/service.rs:2103-2105) and a unit test pins it. The seeded Admin role has a placeholder id (migration m20260708_000002:30-35) that no real Discord role maps to. require_tenant_feature_admin (admin/router.rs:625-646) does accept owner_discord_id for any kind. No owner bypass or auto-link exists for alliance tenants. It may be partly deliberate, but it leaves the registrar with no permissions on their own hub.

findings.title: Albion link has no proof of ownership; claiming a roster character grants the guild base role and alliance roles
findings.description: `POST /albion/link` and `/register` accept any Albion player id/IGN that is not already linked. The only check is Albion-guild membership for alliance hubs. If `player.guild_id == tenant albion_guild_id`, the backend assigns the configured base role (`discord_applications_accepted_role_id`, falling back to `default_role_discord_id`) to the caller. Anyone in the Discord server (public invite, or a mere member) can claim the character of an offline roster member and gain the guild role, nickname and alliance roles. Self-service DELETE /albion/link (settings.ts:1036) lets them unlink and re-claim freely, while the gate component documents unlinking as admin-only. There is no officer approval, challenge or audit event.
findings.fix: Add a verification step. Options: an officer-approval queue; an in-game challenge (e.g. a guild-note token checked against gameinfo); or only auto-assign roles for IGNs matching the Discord nickname or an application-accepted record. Rate-limit and audit link and unlink. Make the unlink policy consistent (backend and gate comment).
findings.verify_note: link_player and register_by_ign (albion/router.rs:295-432) only check that the player is unlinked and passes assert_register_allowed. On guild tenants they then call assign_guild_role when player.guild_id equals the configured guild. There is no proof of ownership. Self-service DELETE /albion/link (router.rs:440-469) is exposed and used by settings.ts:1036, while the albion-link-gate doc says unlinking is no longer self-service.

findings.title: Admin link/unlink and POST /users skip alliance guard, role assignment and fan-out that self-link performs
findings.description: `link_player` and `register_by_ign` call `assert_register_allowed`, `assign_guild_role` and `after_successful_link` (alliance copy and hub role). `admin_link_user_handler`, `admin_unlink_user_handler` and `create_user` do none of that: no guild-role assignment on admin link, no alliance fan-out, no `after_successful_unlink` (hub and alliance roles are never revoked and the paired tenants' links are left behind), and no alliance-outsider check. `create_user` also builds the roster from `get_configured_guild_roster()`, which is empty for alliance tenants, so provisioning on a hub cannot work. An officer-provisioned member is therefore in a different state from a self-linked one. The same action produces different outcomes depending on whether it is done by web admin, web self-service or Discord.
findings.fix: Extract a single `AlbionLinkService::link_and_sync(tenant, discord_user, player)` and `unlink_and_sync` used by every entry point (self, IGN, admin, create_user, bot). It should do the alliance validation, role assignment, nickname and fan-out in one place. Make `create_user` kind-aware.
findings.verify_note: admin_link_user_handler (router.rs:540-565) only does admin_link_user plus sync_guild_nickname. admin_unlink_user_handler (590-604) only does revoke_guild_role. Neither calls assert_register_allowed, assign_guild_role, after_successful_link or after_successful_unlink. create_user (users/router.rs:427-499) uses get_configured_guild_roster and never calls the fan-out. Real parity gap.

findings.title: Accepting an alliance invite or adding a guild never backfills existing members' links and alliance roles
findings.description: `accept_alliance_membership` only flips `alliance_memberships.status` to active. Fan-out of links, users and the hub role (`after_successful_link`) runs only at the moment an individual links. A guild with 100 already-linked members joins an alliance and none of them get a user row, link copy or hub role on the alliance Discord until each one re-links manually or someone calls `link/me` on the alliance. That endpoint only runs on the web or on `GuildMemberAdd`, and the latter 401s (auth-2). Setting a member's hub `discord_role_id` via PATCH also assigns nothing to existing members. Role grants are recorded for later revocation, but nothing ever reconciles grants.
findings.fix: On accept, on setting `discord_role_id` or `discord_alliance_role_id`, and on a schedule, run an alliance reconcile job. For every linked user in each active guild tenant, ensure the user and link exist in the alliance tenant and the correct hub role is held, and record the grant in `alliance_role_grants`. Make it idempotent and expose a manual 'resync' button in the admin alliance panel and a bot command.
findings.verify_note: accept_alliance_membership (platform/service.rs:871-902) only UPDATEs the status. alliance_fanout.rs has no backfill or reconcile. The only adoption is on-demand via adopt_existing_member_link, when someone hits link/me on the alliance (web, or the bot's GuildMemberAdd, which 401s per auth-2). So nothing proactively syncs existing members.

findings.title: Alliance role-revocation retries only run when the guild itself calls /leave again; pending revocations are never retried
findings.description: `mark_alliance_left` writes `alliance_role_revocations` rows as 'pending'. `retry_alliance_role_revocations` is called only from `leave_active_alliance`, and only for that guild. If Discord fails (bot offline, hierarchy), the row stays 'pending' with a detail string forever unless someone presses leave on an already-left membership. Untracked roles (a configured alliance role with no recorded grant) are stored 'ambiguous' and never revoked. Members of a guild that left keep access roles on the alliance hub. `reset_alliance_setup` marks active members left with an empty untracked list and never calls the revoker at all (service.rs:664-667).
findings.fix: Add a background worker (like the existing events fanout worker) that retries pending revocations with backoff and exposes failed ones in the admin UI. Call the revoker from `reset_alliance_setup`. For ambiguous cases, resolve by listing holders of the role via the Discord API.
findings.verify_note: retry_alliance_role_revocations has a single caller, leave_active_alliance (service.rs:1038). reset_alliance_setup (664-667) calls mark_alliance_left with an empty untracked list and no revoker. No worker retries pending rows.

findings.title: Admin invite adds any guild without checking Albion alliance membership (register and configure do check)
findings.description: `register_alliance_tenant` and `configure_alliance_setup` call `ensure_guilds_in_albion_alliance`. `invite_alliance_membership` does not, and does not require the alliance to have `albion_alliance_id`. An alliance owner can invite any registered guild. Because the guild owner must accept, this is limited, but it breaks the invariant that the plan relies on (`plan_register_fanout` matches on Albion guild id). Separately, `list_attachable_guilds` ignores `_actor` and `_managed_ids` and returns every active guild tenant in the platform to any logged-in user, a cross-tenant name leak. The invite endpoint then lets that user spam invites to guilds they do not own.
findings.fix: Call `ensure_guilds_in_albion_alliance` in `invite_alliance_membership`. Make `list_attachable_guilds` require the caller to own the alliance and filter by the Albion alliance, or drop the unscoped variant.
findings.verify_note: The missing ensure_guilds_in_albion_alliance in invite_alliance_membership (service.rs:828-862) is real, but only the alliance owner can invite and the guild owner must still accept. list_attachable_guilds ignores _actor (service.rs:454-480), but its doc comment and plans/alliance-management.md:102 make that deliberate (search by name among guild tenants). The 'any logged-in user can spam invites' claim is wrong because the invite is owner-gated. Residual issue is a missing invariant check plus guild-name exposure.

findings.title: Every authenticated member can list all members' emails and filter by email; the role list is open too
findings.description: `GET /api/users` and `/api/users/{id}` require only a session (`_user: UserContext`) and return `UserProfile { email }`, the Discord OAuth email, for the whole tenant. There is an exact-match `email` filter (enumeration). Combined with auth-4, a removed member keeps this access. `GET /users/{id}/roles` is also open and makes a live Discord call for each request (cost and rate-limit amplification).
findings.fix: Drop `email` from the public profile (or gate it behind `users.create`/`roles.manage`). Remove or restrict the email filter. Gate `/users/{id}/roles` or serve it from synced data (auth-3).
findings.verify_note: list_users, get_user and get_user_roles take only UserContext (users/router.rs:226-310). UserProfile includes email (users/service.rs:35-37). There is an exact-match email filter (service.rs:576-577). Open access is documented as intended for the split participant picker, but exposing OAuth emails is unnecessary. get_user_roles makes a live Discord call per request.

findings.title: Auth overhead per request: 3+ DB queries and possible Discord HTTP in the extractor; N sequential Discord calls for the tenant rail
findings.description: Every cookie request runs `users` lookup by discord_id, a control-DB query to `get_tenant` for owner status (`tenant_owner_for_request`), a full `roles` table SELECT, and, on a cache miss once per minute per user, a blocking Discord GET inside the extractor (no single-flight, so concurrent requests all call out). If the highest role changed it also does an UPDATE inside a GET. The bot path loads all `roles` rows for each request (`resolve_bot_role_ids`) and computes `granted_permissions` that is then discarded (`_permissions`, rbac.rs:345-353). `list_session_tenants` makes one sequential uncached Discord request per membership each time the tenant rail loads and may write `discord_icon_hash`. Each tenant pool uses the sqlx default size (no `set_max_connections`), and `evict` creates a second pool because the sync workers keep the old one.
findings.fix: Keep an in-memory (TTL or invalidate-on-write) cache of roles and tenant owner in `TenantContext`/`Permissions`. Remove the unused permission computation. Use single-flight for the Discord role lookup, or have the bot push roles (auth-3). Cache guild icons server-side (refresh in the sync job, not on read). Configure pool size per tenant.
findings.verify_note: Verified: extractor does a users query plus a control-DB owner lookup, plus a roles SELECT and a Discord lookup in apply_live_guild_roles (rbac.rs:131-216). The bot path computes _permissions and discards it (rbac.rs:345-353). list_session_tenants fetches the Discord icon sequentially per membership (router.rs:384-404). No max_connections is set anywhere. I did not verify the 'evict creates a second pool' sub-claim.

findings.title: Frontend admin gates use legacy permission keys while the backend enforces the granular ones
findings.description: The progression admin page and nav require `progression.settings.manage`, but the handlers require `progression.settings.create/.edit`. A role given only the granular keys cannot reach the page. A role holding only the legacy key sees it and gets 403 on every save. `PermissionCache::role_has` only expands the legacy `events.manage` into granular permissions. `intel.manage`, `progression.settings.manage` and the others are not expanded. `battle-detail.ts` gates on `intel.manage` while the backend uses `intel.create/edit`. The `PermissionKey` union is also hand-copied in `api.models.ts` and `bot/types.ts` (the bot copy is missing most keys), so it drifts.
findings.fix: Replace legacy gates with the granular keys in the frontend. Either expand every legacy `*.manage` to its granular set in `role_has` (data-driven), or migrate role rows and remove legacy variants from the enum. Generate the TS permission union from the OpenAPI schema or the matrix endpoint.
findings.verify_note: Progression mismatch is real. The route and nav gate on progression.settings.manage (app.routes.ts:271-275, nav.ts:296-304) while handlers need .create/.edit (progression/router.rs:165,225,261). role_has only expands events.manage (permission_cache.rs:27-39). The default Admin holds both keys through migrations m20260826_000002 and m20260902_000006, and tenant owners get all permissions, so it only bites custom role matrices. The battle-detail claim is wrong: battle-detail.ts:1226-1227 checks intel.create OR intel.manage. Lowered to low.

findings.title: Platform admin with no tenant cannot reach /platform; link gate and login failures strand users
findings.description: `/platform` is a child of the shell route guarded by `tenantGuard`, which redirects to `/needs-tenant` when `tenant_id` is empty. `platformGuard` and the backend field doc ('so /platform can gate even when the session is not tenant-scoped') are unreachable in exactly that case, and `needs-tenant` has no link to `/platform`. `AlbionLinkGate` is rendered for every session with a tenant, including platform admins and tenant owners. It is a non-dismissible overlay with no logout. On an alliance hub, a user whose Albion guild is not a member gets a 403 from `assert_register_allowed` and is locked out. `needs-tenant` lists every Discord guild (not only `can_manage` ones), and users find out they cannot register only after clicking. OAuth callback errors (e.g. no email, `upsert_user` Unauthorized) are returned as raw JSON on the redirect URL.
findings.fix: Move `/platform` outside `tenantGuard`. Skip the gate for platform admins, tenant owners and non-players, or add an escape (logout, switch server). Show the 'not in an alliance member guild' reason. Filter the register list to `can_manage`. Have the callback redirect to a friendly `/login?error=...` page.
findings.verify_note: Mixed. /platform is under the tenantGuard shell (app.routes.ts:19-24, 317-327). However needs-tenant.ts:13-14 and needs-tenant.spec.ts:44 explicitly say it is deliberately 'not the platform admin console', so the no-tenant case is intended. Real parts: the AlbionLinkGate overlay renders for every session with a tenant (shell.ts:133-135), with no platform admin skip and no logout. An alliance hub outsider gets 403 from assert_register_allowed and is stuck behind it. OAuth callback error handling and the can_manage filter were not verified.

findings.title: Module availability per tenant kind is defined in three places, and the bot's application manager gate duplicates RBAC
findings.description: The bot hard-codes `ALLIANCE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS`. The frontend has `guildOnlyGuard` and per-page `tenant_kind === 'alliance'` checks. The backend gates only by feature flags (`FEATURE_GATES`) and does not know which modules an alliance may use, so the API serves guild-only endpoints on alliance tenants. The bot's application buttons decide 'isManager' locally from `discord_applications_manage_role_id` or Discord ManageGuild, while the backend separately requires the `applications.manage` RBAC permission. A role can pass one gate and fail the other, so Discord and web give different answers for the same person. The bot also handles buttons, selects and modals without the tenant-registered or alliance checks that slash commands get.
findings.fix: Expose `available_modules` or `allowed_commands` per tenant kind from the backend (`/tenants/{id}/status` and `/auth/me`) and make the bot and frontend consume it, with the backend enforcing it. Drop the bot-local `isManager` and rely on the backend permission result (the backend should return 403, the bot renders it).
findings.verify_note: The bot hardcodes ALLIANCE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS (command-gate.ts:16-25). The frontend has guildOnlyGuard (auth.guard.ts:111-118). FEATURE_GATES in tenant.rs:467-501 has no kind-based gating. The bot's isManager (button.ts:260-272) is local, while the backend requires applications.manage (applications/router.rs:188). It is a parity and duplication problem, not a security hole, because the backend still enforces.

findings.title: Tenant leakage: fights and battles still use the deployment-wide ALBION_GUILD_ID and allied lists
findings.description: `albion_scope.rs` states that env `ALBION_*` is never mixed in. But `friendly_side(config)`, the fight trends, and the `BattlesService` built at startup use `cfg.albion_guild_id` and `cfg.albion_allied_guild_ids()` for every tenant. A second guild tenant therefore has its fights classified as win, loss or draw from the first deployment's guild, and its own guild's side is treated as an opponent. `albion_guild_id` is also a required env var, so a multi-tenant deployment must set a meaningless value.
findings.fix: Resolve `AlbionScope` per request from the control plane (as regear and the albion router do) and pass it into `friendly_side` and `BattlesService`. Remove the env fields.
findings.verify_note: fights.rs:719-725, 1590-1597 and 1851-1854 use config.albion_guild_id and the env allied lists. BattlesService is built from cfg at lib.rs:104-109. config.rs:68 makes albion_guild_id a required env var. Nothing overrides Config per tenant. Fight outcomes for any tenant other than the deployment guild are classified wrongly.

findings.title: Guild settings accept unvalidated ids; channels and roles are not checked against the tenant's own Discord guild
findings.description: Older fields (events/battles/cta/flash/forum channels, tags, audit-log, spam, event role) go through `normalize`, a trim with no snowflake validation. Newer ones use `normalize_discord_snowflake`. Nothing verifies that a channel or role belongs to this tenant's guild (only autorole is checked against the guild role list). An admin can store a channel id from another server where the shared bot is also present, and the bot will post tenant data there. `discord_alliance_role_id` and the applications accepted role are never checked for existence or whether the bot can assign them. They fail silently later (`assign_discord_role` only logs a warning).
findings.fix: Validate all ids as snowflakes. When a bot token is configured, check channel and role ids against `fetch_discord_channels/roles` for the tenant's guild on save. Show assignability (managed or above the bot) in the response.
findings.verify_note: Code is as described. Older fields use normalize (a trim only) and newer ones use normalize_discord_snowflake (admin/service.rs:113-206). Only autorole is checked against the guild role list. No channel or role is verified to belong to the tenant's guild. Exploit needs a tenant admin acting against their own tenant, so it is a validation gap rather than a privilege escalation. I did not verify whether the bot checks channel.guildId before posting.

findings.title: Tenant owner without a role cannot assign or remove roles; priority check ignores the owner bypass
