findings.description: `UserContext::require` lets the tenant owner pass `roles.manage`, but the handlers pass `user.is_superadmin()` (platform admin only) and `user.roles` to `ensure_priority_allowed`. An owner whose own Discord roles map to nothing has `actor_max = 0` and gets 'cannot assign or remove a role above your own' for any role with priority above 0. Equal-priority roles can be promoted by the editor.
findings.fix: Pass `is_superadmin || is_tenant_owner` into the priority check. Document and decide whether equal priority may be assigned.
findings.verify_note: post_user_role passes user.is_superadmin() and user.roles (users/router.rs:328-345) into add_user_role, whose ensure_priority_allowed is at member_roles.rs:269. The tenant-owner bypass in UserContext::require (rbac.rs:63-71) is not applied to the priority check. I did not verify the equal-priority sub-claim.

findings.title: Dead code: unrouted albion-settings page; bot's api/auth/me fallback can never succeed
findings.description: `AlbionSettings` is never imported or routed, yet its doc says it is the only UI for the `albion/search`, `players/{id}` and `guilds/{id}` lookups. The /albion/guild/roster docs still describe the removed ALBION_GUILD_ID env. `resolveInternalUserId`'s second fallback and `ApiClient.getDiscordProfile` call `GET api/auth/me` with `X-Discord-Id`, but `get_me` only reads the session cookie, so it always 401s. Bot `/link` asks the user to type a raw Albion `player_id` and name (no search), while `/register` by IGN is the only usable path. The three Albion passthrough routes have no rate limit or caching.
findings.fix: Route or delete `albion-settings`. Remove the dead bot fallback and `getDiscordProfile`. Make bot `/link` search-based (autocomplete via `albion/search`) or remove it in favour of `/register`. Cache passthroughs.
findings.verify_note: albion-settings is only referenced by its own file and READMEs, and has no route in app.routes.ts. The bot's api/auth/me fallback (resolve-user.ts:22-30) and getDiscordProfile (client.ts:74-86) call an endpoint that reads only the session cookie (router.rs:818-832), so they always 401. Dead code.

logic_questions: Albion linking has no proof of identity (auth-7). Which model do you want? (a) first-come with officer review, (b) an in-game challenge such as a code in the guild note or a chat check, (c) trust only the Discord nickname or an accepted application, or (d) keep it open but never auto-grant guild or alliance roles from a self-claim. Should self-service unlink remain allowed? The link gate says it should not, while the settings page and the API allow it.

Should a Discord member who has never logged into the website be auto-provisioned on first bot interaction or on join (recommended), or should the 'log in to the website first' rule stay deliberate? This decides whether /register and /link may work with no prior website login, and whether alliance hubs can adopt links from guilds on member join.

When a member leaves or is banned from the Discord guild, should the backend delete their tenant membership and user row, soft-deactivate them (keeping splits, bank and history attribution), or keep them as is? Today nothing is ever removed and a removed member can still switch in with the default role.

Who is the owner of an alliance tenant (`owner_discord_id`)? Should they bypass all permissions on the alliance hub the way a guild owner does? Today they do not, so a fresh alliance has no admin at all unless a platform admin intervenes. Should ownership be transferable, given that the registrar need only hold Manage Server and may not be the true Discord owner?

When Discord role information is unavailable (bot kicked, missing Server Members intent, outage), should the backend fail closed (downgrade to the default role after N minutes) or keep honouring the cookie's roles (current behaviour, up to 7 days sliding)? What maximum staleness is acceptable?

What should 'alliances sync EVERYTHING with member guilds' include for people: users and links, alliance hub roles and the per-guild role mapping, and removal of those roles when someone leaves the guild or the Albion guild? Should alliance gestionale roles and permissions be inherited from the guild tenants or stay independent per hub? Should the alliance owner be able to invite guilds outside the Albion alliance?

The platform-admin and tenant-owner bypass skips all permission checks everywhere. Do you want that, or should platform admins have explicit tenant-scoped grants and an audit trail of cross-tenant actions? Also, should `permissions.reload` (which can edit the whole permission matrix) remain a separate permission from `roles.manage`, given that holding it lets a role grant itself anything?

Which legacy permission keys should be retired (`*.manage` alongside `.view/.create/.edit/.delete`)? Do you want a migration that rewrites role rows and removes them from the enum, or should the permission cache keep expanding them? Today only `events.manage` is expanded, so the frontend and backend disagree for the others.

summary:
Builds and comps live in each tenant's schema (build_categories, comp_categories, builds, build_items, build_item_spells, comps, comp_builds). They are served by comps/router.rs (about 1.5k lines) and comps/service.rs (about 5k lines, with large test modules). A build version is a full copy row. Its group is the triple (created_by, trimmed lowercased name, category_id), computed in code with no group id (service.rs:285-324). The only DB guard is a unique index on (created_by, name, category_id, version) (migration m20260910_000001). A comp version copies the comp and keeps pointing at the same build version ids (service.rs:557-633). Comps can expand from a parent (parent_id), and capacity is checked strictly increasing along the chain. Items are stored with a client-supplied name, icon, tier, quality and enchantment. The backend validates them against the bundled openalbion catalog.json only when the numeric id is in the catalog (service.rs:83-163). The catalog (807KB) and abilities (423KB) are embedded JSON served by /api/openalbion/*. The frontend downloads the whole catalog and re-implements slot filtering and tier availability locally (shared/data/albion-equipment-catalog.ts). Pricing is live from AODP with a 300s in-memory cache. Combat (Item Power, readiness, roster-fit, calibration, scenarios) is computed in Rust from bundled datasets.

Alliance sharing is a one-way, manual, point-in-time snapshot of a single artifact. A guild officer clicks share in the web UI (POST /api/alliance/shares), and alliance_share/service.rs copies the build or comp graph into the alliance tenant schema. It records the mapping in the control-plane alliance_shares table. Nothing re-syncs on later edits, and nothing pushes alliance artifacts back to member guilds. The one reverse path is the event fanout worker, which copies an alliance event's comp and builds into each guild through copy_alliance_comp_to_tenant, with an asset map scoped to one fanout job.

Discord only has /build (view one build as a rendered image) and /event-create with a raw numeric comp_id. There is no way to create or edit builds or comps, list or view comps, pick versions, or share, and the bot has no autocomplete. The web side is the full workspace (comps.ts, comp-detail.ts, comp-build-detail.ts).

The creator-dependent version group is still present and intentional in code. It spreads into the uniqueness index, the web grouping, the bot's lookup key and the alliance copy identity.

The performance hot spots are N+1 summaries on every list and detail, and per-comp HTTP calls from the web list.

findings.title: Alliance event fanout re-inserts comp builds on every update job (unique-index violation, so updates never sync)
findings.description: process_target calls load_build_id_map(control, target). That reads event_fanout_assets WHERE job_id = <current job> AND tenant_id = <target>. Every publish, update or archive enqueues a NEW job (lifecycle.rs:376-618, router.rs:1070/1358), so for any job after the first the map is empty. copy_alliance_comp_to_tenant(.., previous_comp, &empty) then calls copy_build_graph(existing=None) for every build in the comp, and that goes to insert_build_row. The guild already holds a copy with the same (created_by, name, category_id, version), because upsert_discord_user resolves the same creator. The unique index idx_builds_creator_name_category_version_unique rejects the insert. The target is marked failed and retried against the same error, so edits to an alliance event that has a comp (time, roster roles, comp quantity changes) never reach the guilds after the first publish. The unit test only passes because it feeds the previous mapping in by hand (service.rs:1933-1941). The same defect also duplicates or collides when a second alliance event reuses the same alliance comp.
findings.fix: Key the build and comp copy mapping by (source_tenant, artifact_type, source_id), the way alliance_shares does, not by job_id. Add a durable guild-side mapping table, or reuse the control-plane one. In copy_build_graph, look up an existing guild row by mapping first, and fall back to the (creator, name, category, version) identity before inserting, so a retry or update converges instead of colliding. Add an integration test that runs two successive Update jobs.
findings.verify_note: load_build_id_map (fanout_worker.rs:431-447) filters event_fanout_assets by the current job_id, and the table PK/FK is per job (m20261030_000001:44-57). Every Update enqueues a new job (lifecycle.rs:143), so the map is empty. copy_build_graph then gets published_id=None and calls insert_build_row (alliance_share/service.rs:638-659, 882-901). That insert is not preceded by any identity lookup, and the unique index (created_by,name,category_id,version) is not partial (migration m20260910_000001:94-110). The collision is real. sync.rs:518-541 already resolves mappings across jobs (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1), which shows the worker's job-scoped lookup is the odd one out. The unit test at service.rs:1933 feeds the mapping in by hand, as claimed.

findings.title: Alliance share of builds/comps is a one-shot manual snapshot: no re-sync, stale builds, no push to member guilds
findings.description: Sharing only happens when an officer clicks share in the web UI. Nothing hooks create_build, update_build, upsert_build_item, set_build_item_spells, create_*_version, archive or delete to refresh the published copy, so the alliance copy goes stale after the first share. share_comp calls ensure_build_published, which returns early with the existing published id and does not re-copy it (service.rs:727-729). Re-sharing a comp to refresh quantities therefore leaves the builds inside it out of date. Direction is guild to alliance only (README: 'not into other guild tenants'). Alliance-authored builds and comps never reach member guilds except as a side effect of an alliance event fanout (comps-1), and guild officers cannot browse them. Discord has no share command at all. This contradicts the stated goal that alliances sync everything with their member guilds.
findings.fix: Add a backend-driven sync: write comp and build changes to an outbox the way events do (fanout_outbox), keyed on artifact mappings. Have a worker refresh published copies for every artifact that has an alliance_shares row. Add an alliance-to-guild distribution that is policy-driven (auto-share on create, and an alliance catalog that member guilds can import or follow). Make ensure_build_published refresh the build when its source updated_at is newer than the share. Expose share and unshare through a backend command that Discord can call too.
findings.verify_note: Share is manual and guild-to-alliance only (README:5; router.rs dispatches to share_build/share_comp). The comps module has no reference to alliance_shares, so edits trigger no refresh. ensure_build_published returns early with the existing published id (service.rs:700-731), so re-sharing a comp does not refresh its builds. An explicit POST of the build does refresh it through share_build, so the staleness is a missing automation rather than something impossible to recover. The Discord bot has no share command. This is a design and feature gap against goal #3, so I lowered it to medium.

findings.title: Discord can only view one build; no create/edit/list/version/share for builds or comps, and event-create needs a raw numeric comp_id
findings.description: The only comp-related bot surface is /build (read-only) and the comp_id integer option of /event-create. A user cannot list comps, look up a comp's id, view a comp or its builds, see versions, price or readiness, create or edit builds or comps, archive them, or share to the alliance. There is no autocomplete anywhere in the bot. The web UI does all of it (comps.ts, comp-detail.ts, comp-build-detail.ts), so officers in Discord must open the browser to find a comp id before they can create an event. Parity goal #2 is not met for this whole area.
findings.fix: Add /comp (list/show with autocomplete), and a comp option on /event-create that autocompletes from GET /api/comps. Add /build-edit style commands (or modal flows) that call the same backend endpoints. Add share and unshare commands that call POST/DELETE /api/alliance/shares. Keep all rules in the backend, and add the missing fields (version, archived_at) to the bot's types.
findings.verify_note: The bot's only comp-related surfaces are the read-only /build and a required integer comp_id on /event-create (event-create.ts:22-27). A grep for 'autocomplete' in discord-bot/src returns nothing. BuildSummary in api/types.ts:45-54 has no version or archived_at. There is no share command. This is a real parity gap against stated goal #2.

findings.title: Version group is still creator-scoped, and the Discord /build lookup cannot distinguish versions
findings.description: Prior finding verified, still present. A build or comp group is (created_by, name, category). When officer B opens a build made by A and clicks new version, the copy stays in A's group (the 'let _ = creator_id' parameter is discarded). B cannot version under their own name. A same-name build from B is a separate group, so the same logical build fragments per author. list_builds returns every version as a separate row, with no latest flag and no version count. The web build table has no version column, so v1..vN of one build look identical in the list (comps.ts:743-762). The Discord key is 'name category creator' and has no version. findBuildMatches returns every version (V1, V2...) because list_builds returns all non-archived rows. The command then answers 'Più varianti trovate' and lists identical labels, so the user cannot make the command pick a version. BuildSummary in the bot does not even declare version.
findings.fix: Decide the group identity in the backend. Likely (name, category) per tenant, with created_by only as metadata and a stored group_id (or a canonical root build id) instead of recomputing the triple. Return is_latest and version_count from list endpoints and offer a latest_only=true filter. Make the bot resolve to the latest version by default and accept an optional 'vN' suffix. Add the version column to the web list.
findings.verify_note: Verified in code: build_version_group and comp_version_group are keyed by the (created_by, name, category) triple (service.rs:285-324), and create_*_version discards creator_id (568, 1221). Note that the doc comment at 555-557 says this is intentional, so the 'creator cannot version under own name' part is a design choice and not a bug. The concrete defects are real. list_builds returns every non-archived version with no latest filter (811-870). The web build table has no version column (comps.ts:735-762). The bot's findBuildMatches matches only on name, category and creator, so it returns identical-label variants and answers 'Più varianti trovate'. The bot types do not declare version on BuildSummary. Lowered to medium because the bug only shows when a build has more than one version.

findings.title: List and detail endpoints are N+1 on every row, and the comps page fires one /performance call per comp
findings.description: to_build_summary runs 3-4 queries per row (category lookup, username_of, item count). to_comp_summary runs 3 per row. to_comp_detail runs find_by_id plus to_build_summary for every comp_build. to_build_detail runs read_item_spells per item plus a version-group scan. loadComps requests 500 comps (OPTIONS_LIMIT), which is roughly 1.5-2k queries. It then fires one GET /api/comps/{id}/performance per comp via Promise.all. That is up to 500 parallel HTTP requests, each running get_comp_performance and build_performance_stats. The comp detail page fires comp, performance, share status, price (live AODP), readiness (heavy) and then GET /builds/{id} for each build (loadBuildDetails), which is another N+1 on the wire. The Discord /build command pulls limit=1000 summaries (about 4k queries) just to match a name client-side, though list_builds already supports a 'search' filter.
findings.fix: Batch-load in the service: categories and users with is_in maps, a GROUP BY count for items, comp_builds joined with builds. Add a bulk performance endpoint or include the stats in the comp list response. Add a comp-detail endpoint that returns builds with their items in one call. Make the bot call list_builds with search= and a small limit.
findings.verify_note: to_build_summary does category, user and count queries per row (service.rs:658-690). to_comp_summary does 3 queries per row (1556-1589). to_comp_detail does find_by_id plus to_build_summary per comp_build (1596-1618). loadComps requests limit 500 and then awaits loadCompPerformance, which fires one GET per comp through Promise.all (comps.ts:2433-2461, 2523-2547). That await sits before loading.set(false), so the page stays blocked until every performance call returns. comp-detail.ts:2515-2540 fires one GET /builds/{id} per build. The bot requests limit=1000 and filters client-side (build.ts:31-37), and MAX_PAGE_LIMIT is 1000, so the request is honored.

findings.title: update_comp merges parent builds into the comp before validating, leaving a polluted comp when validation fails
findings.description: When req.parent_id is set on a parentless comp, merge_parent_builds_if_additions writes the parent's comp_builds into the child with db (no transaction) when the child's capacity is not greater than the parent's. validate_expansion_parent runs afterwards. Empty child: after the merge its capacity equals the parent's, so the validation fails with 'capacity greater than its parent', yet the parent's builds are already persisted. Cycle: setting A's parent to a descendant B merges B's builds into A and then errors on 'beneath one of its descendants'. The caller sees a 400 while the data has changed. The heuristic also silently inflates a comp that was deliberately a smaller full snapshot. update_comp also skips the 'archived parent' check that create_comp has (service.rs:1753).
findings.fix: Validate first (cycle, archived, self-parent), then do the merge, parent_id update and capacity-invariant check in a single transaction. Better, make the 'additions' shorthand an explicit request flag (merge_parent=true) rather than an inference from capacity.
findings.verify_note: update_comp calls merge_parent_builds_if_additions on a bare DatabaseConnection (no txn) before validate_expansion_parent (service.rs:1892-1904, 1919-1968, 2033-2080). If the validation fails, the parent's builds are already written into the child. update_comp has no archived-parent check, while create_comp does (1753-1760). Verified.

findings.title: Removing a build item sets the build signal to null (DELETE returns 204, frontend expects a BuildDetail)
findings.description: The backend remove_build_item returns StatusCode::NO_CONTENT. The frontend calls api.delete<BuildDetail> and does this.build.set(updated ?? null). With an empty body ApiService.delete yields null/undefined, so the page's build becomes null right after a successful delete. The UI then shows the empty or not-found state until a reload. The service also returns Ok for a build id that does not exist (no existence check), so a typo is silently a 204.
findings.fix: Have the endpoint return the updated BuildDetail (consistent with upsert_build_item and set_build_item_spells), or reload the build after delete. Return 404 if the build does not exist.
findings.verify_note: The backend remove_build_item returns 204 (router.rs:652-683) and does no existence check (service.rs:1540-1553). The frontend calls api.delete<BuildDetail> and does this.build.set(updated ?? null) (comp-build-detail.ts:1191-1197). ApiService.delete maps an empty body to null (api.service.ts:73-78), so the build signal becomes null after a successful delete.

findings.title: Price failures are cached as zero-silver prices for 5 minutes; quality and unresolved items are ignored; cache is not invalidated on edits
findings.description: fetch_price_index does albiondata.prices(..).await.unwrap_or_default() twice, sequentially. An AODP outage or timeout becomes 'no listings'. Every item prices at 0 and the zero-total view is cached for 300s via cache.put_build/put_comp, so an outage shows free builds for five minutes. Items whose identifier cannot be resolved are skipped (continue), so the total is understated with no flag. There is no unpriced_items count. Item quality is not part of the price lookup, so a masterpiece weapon is priced like a normal one. The cache has no invalidation, and comp-build-detail refetches the price right after saving an item, so it shows the stale pre-edit total for up to 5 minutes.
findings.fix: Propagate the AODP error and do not cache failures. Return unpriced_item_count/ids in the view. Run the two AODP calls concurrently. Include quality (or document it). Evict the build and any comp price entries containing that build in upsert/remove/spells/update.
findings.verify_note: fetch_price_index uses unwrap_or_default on both AODP calls, run sequentially (pricing.rs:406-420). Unresolved items are skipped (pricing.rs:57-63). The router caches whatever view comes back for 300s (router.rs:1424-1431, 1466-1472; price_cache.rs TTL=300). A grep found no invalidation anywhere. An outage is therefore cached as zero-silver prices, as claimed.

findings.title: Alliance share collides on the creator-scoped unique index when the same user (or same-named build) is shared from two guilds
findings.description: Published rows take created_by from resolve_created_by (the source user's discord_id upserted into the alliance schema) and copy name, category and version verbatim. Two guilds sharing 'Heavy Mace / Crystal / v1' authored by the same Discord user (an officer in both guilds) both resolve to one alliance user. The second insert violates the unique index. The API returns the generic 409 'That value is already in use.' and the share fails with no actionable message. The refresh path, which sets version/name/category on the existing published row, can hit the same violation after a rename. The identity check the service uses on create (ensure_build_identity_free) is not applied to the copy.
findings.fix: On share, detect the identity clash. Either attach the share to the existing alliance build when it is the same logical artifact, or disambiguate the published copy (for example attribute it to a per-guild synthetic creator, or add source_tenant to the identity). Return a descriptive error.
findings.verify_note: share_build calls resolve_created_by and then copy_build_graph. With no published_id it calls insert_build_row (alliance_share/service.rs:638-659, 882-901) with no identity pre-check. The unique index is on the creator-scoped identity. The same Discord user in two guilds sharing a same-named build at the same version will collide. It needs a specific scenario (one user in two member guilds with homonym builds), so it is less common than comps-1.

findings.title: Deleting/renaming a guild build or comp never touches its alliance copy or share row
findings.description: delete_build and delete_comp (and archive_*, update_*) do not reference alliance_shares at all (no match for alliance_shares in the comps module). After the guild deletes a shared build, the published alliance copy and the control-plane mapping row stay forever. unshare_build needs the share row, but the source build is gone, so the UI cannot reach it. The alliance copy keeps being offered. When unshare_build is called while an alliance comp still references the build, delete_or_hide_published_build silently archives it (FK violation), so the published comp keeps rendering a build that is no longer shared. unshare_comp leaves its builds behind, so orphans accumulate with no listing to clean them up.
findings.fix: Make comp and build delete and archive call into the share service (inside the same flow), removing or archiving the published copy and the mapping. Cascade unshare of builds that no remaining published comp references. Give alliance officers a published-artifacts listing.
findings.verify_note: The comps module never references alliance_shares. The only users of that table are platform, alliance_share, events/sync and migrations. Deleting or archiving a guild build or comp therefore leaves the alliance copy and the share row. delete_or_hide_published_build silently archives on FK violation (alliance_share/service.rs:985-1000). Real orphan and staleness problem.

findings.title: Build item name, icon, tier are trusted from the client (no catalog resolution); the bot fetches arbitrary icon URLs
findings.description: validate_catalog_item returns Ok(()) for any id not in the bundled catalog (service.rs:91-94), and for known ids it never checks or overwrites openalbion_item_name or openalbion_item_icon. icon_url_with_quality only appends or rewrites ?quality=, so any string is persisted and returned. loadIcon in the bot does fetch(iconUrl) for any http(s) URL (8s timeout) and pipes the bytes into sharp. An officer with comps.builds.edit can make the bot request an internal URL (blind SSRF), or make sharp parse hostile data. A wrong or garbage name and tier on a known id also lands in embeds and Item Power (tier_from_stored trusts the stored tier). The backend does not own the item data it stores.
findings.fix: Resolve name, icon, tier and type server-side from the catalog by id, reject unknown ids, and ignore client-sent name/icon. Allow-list the icon host (render.albiononline.com) in the bot, or have a backend endpoint render the build image.
findings.verify_note: validate_catalog_item returns Ok for unknown ids (service.rs:91-94). The name and icon sent by the client are stored as-is (1455-1466), and icon_url_with_quality only appends or rewrites the quality parameter (status.rs:239-257). The bot fetches any http(s) URL (build-image.ts:99-117). It needs comps.builds.edit permission, and it is a blind GET whose result goes through sharp and falls back to a placeholder on failure, so the impact is limited. Lowered from medium to low.

findings.title: Frontend re-implements backend rules: version grouping by username string, catalog availability, slot compatibility, a 1055-line local equipment list
findings.description: comp-detail groups build versions with the key `${category_id}::${created_by_username}::${name}`. The backend group is (created_by id, trimmed lowercase name, category). Two users with the same display name merge in the picker, and case or whitespace variants of one name split. isAlbionCatalogItemAvailable duplicates is_valid_catalog_identifier and belongsToSlot duplicates validate_catalog_item. The app ships a local fallback equipment catalog and downloads the full 800KB catalog just to filter client-side with .slice(0,100). Version diffing and party simulation run in the browser only. Discord cannot show any of them, and the rules can drift.
findings.fix: Add backend endpoints for item search (slot, tier, query, limit) and for version diff and grouped builds (return group_id or is_latest). Keep the web as a thin renderer. Delete the duplicated tier and slot tables.
findings.verify_note: The group key in comp-detail.ts:1696-1697 uses created_by_username, a string, where the backend uses the creator id and a normalized name. The frontend ships a 1055-line local equipment catalog (albion-equipment-catalog.ts:790+) and filters with slice(0,100) at line 811. Version diff and party simulation exist only in the web app. Real duplication, but its practical impact is low (the picker grouping only matters when two users share a display name), so I rated it low.

findings.title: Builds table re-sorts only the current server page and shows a wrong slot count
findings.description: The table is serverMode with server sort and pagination, but rows come from buildsGrouped, which re-sorts the page's 10 items by creator and then name. The user's chosen sort is ignored within a page and the order is inconsistent between pages. The cell prints `{{ item_count }}/10 slots`, but item_count counts every build_items row including the swap loadout (no loadout filter), so it can read '14/10 slots'.
findings.fix: Remove buildsGrouped and rely on server order, or add a creator sort to list_builds. Return main_item_count and swap_item_count (or total slots) from the backend.
findings.verify_note: The builds table binds rows to buildsGrouped(), which re-sorts the current page by creator then name (comps.ts:730, 1202-1204; group-by-creator.ts). item_count counts all build_items, including the swap loadout, because there is no loadout filter (service.rs:672-675), while the cell prints '/10 slots'. Verified.

findings.title: Saving a slot is two non-atomic requests (item PUT, then spells PUT)
findings.description: upsert_build_item and set_build_item_spells are separate endpoints. If the spells PUT fails validation (stale ability list), the item is already replaced. The user sees an error toast, but the item changed and the draft state is discarded or inconsistent. upsert_build_item itself does the update plus drop_abilities_the_item_no_longer_offers without a transaction.
findings.fix: Accept spells in the item upsert body (create_build already does) and apply everything in one transaction.
findings.verify_note: saveSlot does the item PUT and then a separate spells PUT (comp-build-detail.ts:1146-1167). upsert_build_item does the update and drop_abilities_the_item_no_longer_offers without a txn (service.rs:1457-1486). Valid but minor, since spells normally validate against the same item.

findings.title: OpenAlbion catalog and abilities are served uncached; detail reads clone the entire catalog
findings.description: GET /openalbion/catalog does catalog_items().to_vec() (a full clone of the item vec) and serializes about 800KB with no Cache-Control or ETag. /abilities is another 423KB. The data only changes on deploy. resolve_missing_icons also calls list_catalog() (a full clone) on every build-detail read where any icon is NULL. The frontend only caches in memory per page load. The O(types × ids × catalog) loop there is also quadratic.
findings.fix: Return &'static slices, and add a strong ETag plus Cache-Control: public, max-age (versioned by build hash). Build an id->icon HashMap once in a OnceLock. Migrate NULL icons once and drop the read-time fix-up.
findings.verify_note: list_catalog does catalog_items().to_vec() (openalbion/service.rs:94-96), and resolve_missing_icons calls it on read (comps/service.rs:761-808). A grep found no Cache-Control or ETag in the openalbion module. get_abilities already returns a &'static map, so only the missing HTTP caching headers apply there. Minor performance issue.

findings.title: Combat roster-fit and calibration are per-user and per-observation query loops
findings.description: build_roster_fit loads every specialization row, then does find_by_id plus display_name::resolve for each member with specs, then truncates to MAX_FIT_MEMBERS, so the DB work is unbounded. calibration loads all users, all event participations, and ALL battle snapshots. For each player of each matched snapshot it runs build_item_power (a build_loadout query plus a spec query), build::find_by_id and display_name::resolve, which is thousands of queries in one GET with no cache and no limit. list_scenarios and list_runs do N+1 for username and run_count.
findings.fix: Batch users and display names with is_in, truncate before resolving names, precompute and cache per-build loadouts and per-user specs inside the request, and cache calibration (recompute on a schedule or only when new snapshots arrive).
findings.verify_note: build_roster_fit loads all specialization rows and then does find_by_id plus display_name::resolve per user (combat/service.rs:156-190). calibration loads all links, users, participations and snapshots. For each player it runs build_item_power, build::find_by_id and display_name::resolve (814-921). Real N+1 pattern, but it is a rarely used analytics endpoint.

findings.title: Published alliance copies are normal editable rows, so local edits are silently overwritten on re-share
findings.description: Splits get origin_read_only on the published copy. Builds and comps have no equivalent flag. Alliance officers can edit, rename, version or archive a published build or comp through the normal endpoints. The next guild re-share, or event fanout, deletes all build_items (delete_many) and comp_builds and reinserts from the source, discarding those edits. copy_comp_graph also forces parent_id = NULL, so expansion structure (parent/child comps) is lost in the alliance and in fanout copies.
findings.fix: Add origin_tenant, origin_id and read_only to builds and comps and enforce read-only in the comps service. Preserve the parent chain by mapping parent comps through the share table.
findings.verify_note: origin_read_only exists only for splits (alliance_share/service.rs:424, 1072). comps/entities.rs has no origin field. copy_comp_graph forces parent_id to None (service.rs:792, 844) and deletes and reinserts comp_builds and build_items on refresh (796, 804). Verified. This is an architecture and design gap and not a crash.

findings.title: Discord build image drops tier, enchantment, quality and abilities, and icons never encode enchantment
findings.description: tileSvg prints only slot, the name truncated to 22 chars, and MAIN/SWAP. The embed field lists slot and name. Tier, enchantment, quality and chosen abilities, which the web shows and which the backend stores, are not shown. The catalog icon URL is built from the base identifier with no @N suffix, so an enchanted item renders as the plain item in both web and bot. The image is composed in the bot (sharp and fetch per icon), so it is not reusable by the web.
findings.fix: Add a backend render endpoint (for example GET /api/comps/builds/{id}/image) that composes the full build card including enchantment (@N in the render URL), quality and abilities. Let the bot just attach it, and the web can reuse it.
findings.verify_note: tileSvg prints only slot, a name truncated to 22 chars, and MAIN or SWAP (build-image.ts:124-140). render_icon_url builds the URL from the bare identifier with no @N suffix (openalbion/service.rs:513-518), and the frontend albionEquipmentIconUrl does the same. The image composition lives in the bot. Cosmetic.

findings.title: Minor drift: unused creator_id parameters, dead assignment, README and docs mismatch
findings.description: create_*_version take creator_id and discard it. 'let _ = category_id' is a leftover. list_comp_categories claims 'ordered by name' but has no order_by. READMEs and OpenAPI descriptions say 'comps.builds.manage' while the code checks the granular CompsBuildsEdit/Create/Delete permissions (archive and unarchive use Delete). The retry loops in create_*_version retry on any AppError::Database, not just the unique collision.
findings.fix: Remove the parameters or use them to record who made the version. Add the order_by. Sync the docs with the real permission names. Retry only on UniqueConstraintViolation.
findings.verify_note: Verified: let _ = creator_id at service.rs:568 and 1221, and let _ = category_id at 1149. list_comp_categories says 'ordered by name' but has no order_by (service.rs:472-478). The retry loops match any AppError::Database (583, 1237). Trivial drift.

logic_questions: Version identity: should a build/comp group be (name, category) for the whole tenant, so any officer can add a version to it, or stay per creator? Per-creator means B cannot version A's build under B's name, and the Discord lookup needs the creator name in the key. If the group is tenant-wide, what happens to the existing same-name builds that different officers made? Merge them into one group, or keep them as separate groups?

Alliance sync direction and scope: should the alliance auto-publish everything guilds create (builds, comps, categories), or only what officers explicitly share? Should alliance-owned comps and builds be pushed to or importable by member guilds? Is a guild copy read-only and followed, or a fork the guild may edit? What should happen to the guild copy when the guild leaves the alliance: keep, archive, or delete?

When a shared build changes after sharing, should the alliance copy update automatically (live follow) or only on an explicit re-share? Should a comp share always refresh its builds (today it reuses stale ones)?
When a guild deletes or archives a shared build or comp, should the alliance copy be removed, archived, or kept as a frozen snapshot?
Should any user with comps.builds.edit be able to edit any officer's build, or only the creator (and admins)? Today 'mine' is only a list filter.

Should the build list show all versions as rows, or only the latest per group with a version selector? In the Discord /build command, should a bare name resolve to the latest version, and how should older versions be addressed?

Should a build price count quality, and should it flag items with no market listing? A missing price is currently 0 and silently under-counts. What is the intended behaviour when the market API is down: error, last known price, or zero?
Should comp versions pin build versions (as now), or offer an 'update all builds to latest' action? Should an expansion comp's parent_id follow the parent's new versions?

For Discord parity, which comp and build actions must be available in Discord (create, edit items and abilities, versions, archive, share), and which stay web-only? A rendered build image from the backend: yes or no?

summary: Battle data flow today: a per-guild-tenant worker (apps/backend/src/battle_sync.rs, spawned from tenant.rs/lib.rs only for kind != alliance) wakes every 120s, re-reads the tenant's Albion guild/region/allies from the control DB (albion_scope.rs, per-tenant and correct for guild tenants), builds a fresh BattlesService, calls list_guild_battles (up to 20 sequential AlbionBB list pages, then sequential per-battle detail fetches for the visible page), and for each of the newest 50 battles without a guild_battle_snapshots row calls get_battle_detail_with_losses. That function fetches battle + kills from AlbionBB, prices victim gear via Albion Data, and best-effort writes: snapshot (JSON blobs incl. raw kills), normalized evidence tables, enemy identity tables, equipment fingerprints, battle_loss_estimates, a canonical Fight (fight_battles), and recomputed fight_stats. After that, the worker runs intel auto-scout over the newest 50 snapshots and groups orphan fights. HTTP: /api/battles (list), /api/battles/{id} (the same heavy hydrate+persist path on every GET), /api/battles/me, /api/fights (+detail, trends, merge/split/move), /api/fight-analytics/{id} (reads persisted fight_stats), /api/intel/* (scouts, guild report cached 5 min, leaderboards), /api/enemies/*, /api/fingerprints/*, plus unthrottled raw /api/albionbb/* and /api/albiondata/* passthroughs. Frontend: battles page 'guild' tab reads /api/fights, 'me' tab reads /api/battles/me then fetches every row's full detail; detail pages identify 'our' guild by comparing the Discord tenant name to the Albion guild name. Discord bot: /battles lists /api/battles; the poller scans every page of /api/battles each 60s to announce new battles using env GUILD_NAME for win/loss. Alliance tenants have no battle/fight/intel data at all (workers skipped, endpoints reject them because there is no albion_guild_id, no mirroring from member guilds), and guild tenants' friendly-side only comes from manually-entered allied CSV columns, not alliance membership. Two parallel fight-analytics implementations exist (fights.rs recomputing from snapshots with global env Config vs persisted fight_analytics), and two different loss-estimate calculations.

findings.title: Alliance tenants get no battles/fights/intel and nothing syncs from member guilds
findings.description: starts_sync_workers() is false for kind=alliance, so battle_sync/event_sessions never run for an alliance tenant. All battle handlers go through scoped_battles() -> load_albion_scope(), which requires albion_guild_id and returns NotConfigured -> AppError::Validation('tenant has no Albion guild configuration') for an alliance tenant (400). Nothing mirrors guild_battle_snapshots, fights, fight_stats, battle evidence, enemy_* or scouted_comps from member guild schemas into the alliance schema (events mirroring exists in events/sync.rs but contains no battle/fight data; alliance_share only copies builds/comps/splits). The frontend also guards /battles and /intel with guildOnlyGuard. Separately, a guild tenant that joins an alliance does not get the other member guilds as friendly: its FriendlySide/BattleLinkingContext only reads the manually edited albion_allied_guild_ids/names columns, so outcomes, evidence.is_friendly, enemy classification and fight analytics treat sibling guilds as enemies unless an admin types their ids by hand. Result: alliance view of 'everything the member guilds fought' does not exist.
findings.fix: Define an alliance read model: either (a) a backend job on the alliance tenant that queries member guild schemas (alliance_memberships) and materializes/aggregates snapshots, fights, fight_stats, enemy facts and scouts into alliance tables, or (b) alliance endpoints that fan out read-only to member tenant DBs. Use EventReadScope (albion_scope.rs:134-200) for the alliance context. Also derive a guild tenant's allied ids/names from its alliance_memberships siblings at scope-load time (extend load_albion_scope to union active member guild ids) so every battle/fight classification is alliance-aware without manual CSV.
findings.verify_note: Code paths are real. tenant.rs:84 starts_sync_workers is false for alliance, and lib.rs:120 skips those tenants. load_albion_scope (albion_scope.rs:90) needs albion_guild_id, and battles/router.rs:224 scoped_battles always uses it. A guild tenant's friendly side comes only from the manual albion_allied_guild_ids/names columns; I found no sibling-guild derivation. But plans/alliance-management.md:105 and :248 deliberately say no battle/event workers on alliance tenants. So this is an unbuilt feature that conflicts with the owner's goal 3, not a regression. 'Critical' is inflated, so high. EventReadScope already shows the alliance-aware pattern for events.

findings.title: Battle catalog cache is never hit: every request and every sync tick rebuilds it with up to 20 sequential AlbionBB calls
findings.description: BattlesService carries a 60s catalog_cache, but for_scope() calls Self::new(), creating a brand-new empty cache. scoped_battles() calls for_scope on every HTTP request, and battle_sync builds a new BattlesService every tick. So list_guild_battles always runs guild_catalog() cold: up to GUILD_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES=20 strictly sequential AlbionBB /battles pages, then hydrate_page() does one sequential get_battle per visible row (10-50). Each /api/battles page click costs ~20-70 serial upstream round trips (seconds), and the 60s TTL comment/design is dead code. The sync worker pays the same cost every 2 minutes per tenant just to read page 1.
findings.fix: Hold the catalog cache in a process-wide structure keyed by (tenant_id or guild_id+server, min_players), e.g. put it inside AlbionBbService or a shared Arc in Extension, with single-flight on miss. Better: stop hitting AlbionBB for lists on read at all; serve /api/battles from guild_battle_snapshots/battle_guild_stats (already persisted by the worker) with SQL filter/sort/paginate, and let the worker be the only caller of AlbionBB. In the worker fetch only page 1 (no 20-page catalog, no hydrate_page).
findings.verify_note: for_scope (service.rs:100) calls Self::new, which builds an empty catalog_cache. scoped_battles does this on every request, and battle_sync.rs:56 builds a new BattlesService every tick. So the 60s cache can never hit. guild_catalog fetches up to 20 sequential AlbionBB pages (service.rs:57, 151). One nuance: hydrate_page's get_battle goes through the shared AlbionBbService 24h cache (a clone of the same Arc), so the detail fetches are mostly warm after the first pass. The main cost is the 20 list pages, not '20-70' cold calls every time.

findings.title: Discord poller multiplies backend/upstream load and can re-announce the same battles forever
findings.description: checkNewBattles() runs every POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60s per guild and calls listSinceCheckpoint('api/battles', limit 10), which loads every page up to 50. Each page request is a full catalog rebuild on the backend (battles-2): up to 50 requests x (20 AlbionBB list pages + 10 detail fetches) ~ 1,500 upstream calls per guild per minute. Also, when the catalog exceeds 50 pages (500 battles, plausible with 20 upstream pages), complete=false, so lastBattleId is never advanced (line 2054 only advances when complete) and the same newBattles are re-announced every minute. A battle is announced the first time it appears, i.e. often while still in progress with partial totals (see battles-5).
findings.fix: Add a cheap backend endpoint (e.g. GET /api/battles?after_id=X&sort=id or /api/battles/since/{id}) that reads only from snapshots and returns the delta, ordered by id; poller fetches page 1 only. Better, move announcement decisions to the backend (an outbox row per newly finalized battle, like events/fanout_outbox) so the bot just delivers. Advance the cursor on partial scans to the highest contiguous announced id, never leave it stuck.
findings.verify_note: poller.ts:751-780 reads every page up to 50 with limit 10. Each page call rebuilds the catalog (battles-2). lastBattleId only advances when complete (poller.ts:2054). The worst-case figure of about 1,500 upstream calls per minute is speculative. It needs a catalog over 500 battles, and the AlbionBB page size isn't visible in the code. Even a 200-battle catalog is about 20 backend calls times 20 upstream pages every 60s per guild. The stuck-forever re-announce only happens once the catalog passes 500 battles. The partial-data announcement depends on battles-5.

findings.title: GET /api/battles/{id} runs the whole persistence pipeline on every read, and the UI fans it out
findings.description: get_battle_detail_with_losses is a read endpoint that, on every call, re-fetches kills from AlbionBB (uncached), calls Albion Data, loads RoleClassifier, deletes and reinserts battle_guild_stats/battle_player_stats/battle_kills, upserts every enemy guild/player with 3+ queries each, recomputes fingerprints, rewrites battle_loss_estimates and recomputes fight_stats. evidence_writer inserts each kill with a separate INSERT RETURNING plus an items insert_many (N+1: hundreds of kills = hundreds of round trips inside one txn). enemies::writer does select-then-insert/update per guild/alias/player (no ON CONFLICT). The 'me' tab calls buildPersonalScopeStats which issues one full api/battles/{id} per visible row in parallel (page size 10+), and battle-group fires one per selected id; each triggers all the writes above concurrently, and they race with battle_sync hydrating the same battle (delete+insert interleaving, unique violations swallowed as warnings).
findings.fix: Split read from write: GET detail should read the persisted snapshot/evidence (and only fall back to hydrate if absent, behind a per-battle lock/single-flight). Make hydrate idempotent: skip when snapshot exists and battle is finalized. Batch kill inserts (insert_many with generated ids or ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), upsert enemy rows with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. Replace buildPersonalScopeStats' per-battle detail calls with a backend /api/battles/me stats field.
findings.verify_note: get_battle in router.rs:134-166 calls get_battle_detail_with_losses on every GET. That method runs the full write pipeline: snapshot upsert, evidence delete and reinsert, enemy upserts, fingerprints, loss estimate, fight analytics recompute. evidence_writer.rs inserts each kill with its own INSERT inside a loop (about line 173). enemies/writer.rs uses select-then-insert/update per guild. The frontend fans out api/battles/{id} in battles.ts:838 (Promise.all) and battle-group.ts:409. Concurrent delete and insert races with battle_sync are plausible.

findings.title: In-progress battles are cached 24h and snapshotted once, so partial data becomes permanent
findings.description: AlbionBbService::get_battle caches every battle detail for 24h with no check that the battle is finished. The sync worker runs every 2 min and the first time it sees a battle it persists the snapshot; on later ticks already_saved skips it forever (battle_sync.rs:141), so a battle seen mid-fight keeps its early partial guild/player/kill totals, loss estimate, evidence, enemy facts and fight stats. Re-opening in the UI doesn't help for up to 24h because get_battle returns the stale cached detail while get_battle_kills is deliberately uncached, so kills and players/guilds can disagree. The bot announces the same partial numbers and win/loss.
findings.fix: Treat a battle as final only when end_time is set and older than a settle window (e.g. 10-15 min since last kill). Cache non-final battles with a short TTL (or not at all), keep long TTL only for final ones. In the worker, re-hydrate snapshots whose fetched_at is within the settle window of end_time/start_time, and delay Discord announcement until final.
findings.verify_note: The code facts hold. get_battle caches every detail for 24h with no finality check (albionbb/service.rs:19, 59). battle_sync skips any battle that already has a snapshot (battle_sync.rs:141). Kills are uncached. But nothing in the repo shows that AlbionBB actually returns in-progress battles with partial totals, so the real-world impact is unproven. persist_battle_snapshot does upsert on a re-read, so a detail view after the 24h cache expires would refresh it. High is inflated; medium.

findings.title: fights.rs classifies the friendly side from global env Config, not the tenant
findings.description: list_fights, get_fight and get_fight_trends take Extension<Config>, which is the single process-wide env config (lib.rs:179; resolve_tenant never overrides it). friendly_side(config), build_fight_trend_period and observed_friendly_players build the friendly guild/allies from config.albion_guild_id / ALBION_ALLIED_GUILD_*. In a multi-tenant deployment every tenant except the one matching the env guild gets outcome Unknown/Defeat, wrong win rates, K/D, kills/deaths in /fights/trends and an empty or wrong observed_friendly_players list; if ALBION_GUILD_ID is blank, friendly_guild_ids contains '' and matches every player whose guild_id is blank (see battles-7). The battle module itself was already moved to per-tenant albion_scope; fights.rs was missed.
findings.fix: Replace Extension<Config> in fights.rs with the tenant scope: load_albion_scope(control, tenant_id) (or EventReadScope) and build FriendlySide from it, as battles/router.rs does. Better, stop recomputing: read fights.outcome and fight_stats written at hydration time using the tenant-correct side.
findings.verify_note: fights.rs:479, 1424 and 1749 take Extension<Config>. friendly_side(config) at fights.rs:719 uses config.albion_guild_id and the env allied lists. lib.rs:179 injects one global cfg, and resolve_tenant (tenant.rs:~690) does not override it. Any tenant other than the env guild gets wrong or Unknown outcomes and trends.

findings.title: Snapshot players have blank id/guild_id, so fight rollups collapse all players into one and friendly filtering by guild id fails (verify against live payload)
findings.description: The AlbionBB player model documents that player id and guildId are 'Not currently exposed' by the battle-detail endpoint, and the real-payload test fixture has players with only name/guildName. BattlePlayer::from copies those blanks into the snapshot players_json. fights.rs then keys PlayerRollup and player_ids by player.id (HashMap entry(player.id.clone())), so every player collapses into a single '' entry: fight detail unique_players becomes 1, players list has one merged row, observed_friendly_players merges everyone, and the roster-coverage / planned-participant matching (matching albion_player_id against observed ids) can never match. Friendly filters use friendly_guild_ids.contains(&player.guild_id) which is false for blank ids; own-guild name is not in friendly_guild_names (only allied names), so own players are dropped from trends kills/deaths. The evidence layer was built to avoid this (player_key/identity_source) but fights.rs ignores it.
findings.fix: Key rollups by a stable player key (lowercased name + guild name when id blank), or better read battle_player_stats (player_key, is_friendly already computed with the tenant side) instead of players_json. Include the own guild name in the friendly set. Add a test using the real fixture shape (no ids).
findings.verify_note: The client.rs:139-145 docs say player id and guild_id aren't exposed, and the real-payload fixture (client.rs:~640) has players with only name and guildName. BattlePlayer::from copies the blanks (models.rs:287). fights.rs:1870 and :2094 key HashMaps on player.id, so all players collapse into the '' entry. The friendly filters use friendly_guild_ids.contains(&player.guild_id), and the own guild's name is not in friendly_guild_names (fights.rs:1855). The evidence layer already handles this with player_identity (evidence.rs:281).

findings.title: /api/fights and /api/fights/trends load the entire fights/snapshots tables and parse JSON blobs per request
findings.description: list_fights does fight::find().all(), then all fight_battles, then all guild_battle_snapshots rows for those battles (full players_json/kills_json/losses_json columns selected), json-parses guilds_json per fight for the outcome, builds all items, sorts/filters in memory and only then paginates. Cost grows linearly with total history for every list page, tab switch, 5-minute auto refresh and search keystroke. get_fight_trends parses every snapshot's players_json and guilds_json twice (once per 30-day window) per call. Meanwhile fights.outcome, fights.outcome_method and fight_stats (totals, friendly kills/deaths/fame, unique players) are already persisted by fight_analytics and are sufficient for the list.
findings.fix: List from fights + fight_stats with SQL WHERE/ORDER/LIMIT (outcome, needs_review, min_players, sort on persisted columns, join events for title). Compute trends with SQL aggregates over fight_stats grouped by window. Select only needed columns if snapshots must be read.
findings.verify_note: list_fights does fight::find().all(), then loads all segments and all snapshot rows with the full JSON columns. It parses guilds_json per fight, filters and sorts in memory, and paginates last (fights.rs:486-570). Correction: get_fight_trends is bounded to a 60-day window (fights.rs:1431-1435). It is not the whole table, but it is still heavy JSON parsing.

findings.title: Outcome filter and deaths/outcome sort run on un-hydrated list payloads that lack ids, kills and deaths
findings.description: list_guild_battles filters/sorts the catalog (built only from AlbionBB list payloads) and hydrates just the visible page afterwards. The real list payload fixture shows guilds with name/alliance/killFame only (no albionId, kills, deaths). FriendlySide::contains matches by guild id, or by allied NAME only (never the own guild's name), so for list-only summaries the own side can't be identified: outcome=victory|defeat filters and sort=outcome|deaths return wrong rows/ordering and total_items/total_pages are wrong, while the badge shown after hydration uses different data and can contradict the filter that selected the row.
findings.fix: Move the filter/sort to data that has complete guild lines (snapshots/battle_guild_stats with is_friendly), i.e. fix battles-2 by serving from the DB. If AlbionBB list must be used, include own guild name in FriendlySide and disable outcome/deaths sort without hydration.
findings.verify_note: filter_sort_page_battles (service.rs:~551) applies outcome filter and sort to the catalog before hydration. The catalog is built from list payloads, and the real list fixture has guild name, alliance and killFame only, with no albionId, kills or deaths. FriendlySide::contains (outcome.rs:107) matches by id, or by allied name only, never the own guild's name. So list-only summaries mostly come out Unknown. outcome=victory/defeat and sort=outcome/deaths are effectively wrong.

findings.title: Loss estimates silently empty for large losses; two different pricing algorithms; no market price cache
findings.description: estimate_losses joins ALL unique victim item ids into one prices() call; parse_item_ids rejects more than 120 ids with a Validation error. Any battle where our side lost >120 distinct items (a normal zerg fight: 15 deaths x ~8 slots) fails, and unwrap_or_default() at line 265 swallows it, persisting an empty estimate in guild_battle_snapshots.losses_json permanently (until a reopened detail recomputes, which hits the same error). economy::writer::price_index_for has the same single-call limit with unwrap_or_default. Snapshot estimate uses min(sell_min, sell_max, buy_price_max) across all qualities and cities (underprices; includes buy orders) while battle_loss_estimates uses cheapest_price_index with the regear pricing settings, so the UI (snapshot losses) and fight_analytics/reports disagree on the same battle. The snapshot estimate counts only the tenant's own guild id, ignoring allies. AlbionDataService has no cache, so each hydrate re-requests prices.
findings.fix: Chunk price requests (<=100 ids) in AlbionDataService::prices_bulk with a TTL cache (e.g. 15-30 min keyed by server+item+location). Use a single loss-estimate implementation (economy::estimate with FriendlySide) and read it for both snapshot display and analytics; drop estimate_losses/build_price_index from battles/service.rs. Log (not hide) price failures and mark the estimate as incomplete.
findings.verify_note: estimate_losses (service.rs:974) sends all unique item ids in one prices() call. parse_item_ids rejects more than 120 (albiondata/service.rs:198), and unwrap_or_default at service.rs:265 hides the error. economy/writer.rs:174 and :183 also use unwrap_or_default on the same single call. build_price_index (service.rs:1171) takes the min over sell/buy fields, while economy uses cheapest_price_index with the regear settings, so the two estimates differ. There is no price cache. A zerg fight can exceed 120 unique ids, but typical battles may not.

findings.title: battle_sync cycle: N+1 snapshot checks, hydrates 50 rows every tick, min_players=10 gap, no backlog catch-up
findings.description: Every tick: list_guild_battles with limit 50 (rebuilds the 20-page catalog and hydrate_page 50 sequential detail calls, see battles-2) just to get ids; then one SELECT per summary to see if a snapshot exists (50 queries) instead of a single IN query. min_players is not passed so the default 10 applies: smaller skirmishes never get a snapshot (so no fights/evidence/enemy data for them), while the bot and UI present them elsewhere. Only the newest 50 are ever considered, so after >50 new battles in an outage window or first onboarding of a tenant, older battles are never backfilled (no cursor like the intel backfill has). tokio interval() uses MissedTickBehavior::Burst, so a slow cycle (it is serial and upstream-bound) is followed by back-to-back cycles. Every guild tenant runs this independently for the same global upstream.
findings.fix: Worker: fetch AlbionBB page 1..K for the guild without hydrate, one query for existing battle_ids (is_in), process only missing ones, with bounded concurrency and a per-tenant cursor for backfill. Set MissedTickBehavior::Skip. Make min_players a per-tenant setting shared with the UI/bot.
findings.verify_note: battle_sync.rs does one SELECT per summary (:131-141). It passes min_players None, so the default of 10 applies (service.rs:121). It only looks at the newest 50 with no backfill cursor. tokio interval defaults to MissedTickBehavior::Burst. All of these are real.

findings.title: AlbionBB client has no retry/backoff/429 handling, no rate limit, no single-flight, and a cache that clones large payloads
findings.description: get_json performs a single attempt: any 429/5xx/timeout (60s default) becomes AppError::UpstreamService and aborts the whole list or my-battles request (note the `?` on every get_battle in list_my_battles). There is no global concurrency cap or token bucket although N tenant workers plus HTTP callers all share one upstream; concurrent misses on the same battle/guild all go upstream (no single-flight). The battle cache holds 500 entries globally: with several tenants and 50-battle windows it thrashes, and each insert does an O(n) retain + O(n) min scan under the write lock and each hit deep-clones the full BattleDetail. Three separate reqwest clients exist (AlbionBb, AlbionData, shared) with different timeouts.
findings.fix: Add a shared upstream gateway: semaphore (e.g. 4 concurrent), retry with jittered backoff honoring Retry-After, moka/in-flight-dedup cache storing Arc<BattleDetail>, larger capacity with TTL by finality (battles-5). Persisted snapshots should be the primary read source so upstream is only touched by the worker.
findings.verify_note: AlbionBbApiClient::get_json (client.rs:469) makes a single attempt with no retry, 429 handling or semaphore. list_my_battles propagates with ? on each get_battle. The battle cache clones the full detail on every hit and prunes O(n) on insert (albionbb/service.rs:56-80). The 500-entry cap and the 'three clients' remark are minor details.

findings.title: Raw /api/albionbb/* and /api/albiondata/* passthroughs need no permission and are uncached
findings.description: Handlers only require a session (UserContext, no Permission), unlike /api/battles which requires fights.view. Any member of any tenant can enumerate other guilds' battles/kill feeds (arbitrary guild_id/search) and drive unbounded uncached upstream traffic (list, kills, player stats, market prices with arbitrary server/locations) through the shared client, risking upstream bans for all tenants. This also bypasses the tenant scoping the battles module enforces.
findings.fix: Require fights.view (or remove the routes if the frontend doesn't use them: it uses /api/battles), add per-user rate limits and cache list/prices responses. Prefer deleting unused passthroughs.
findings.verify_note: The handlers do require only UserContext, with no Permission (albionbb/router.rs:84, 126, 157; albiondata/router.rs:62). But the data is public AlbionBB/Albion Data content, so there is no tenant data leak. The 'bypasses tenant scoping' claim is overstated. The real risk is authenticated upstream amplification, and grep shows no frontend or bot caller. Low.

findings.title: /api/battles/me scans 5 upstream pages with serial detail fetches and fails wholesale on one error; UI then refetches every detail
findings.description: list_my_battles loops up to 5 AlbionBB pages and, for each battle, awaits get_battle serially (cold = hundreds of upstream calls), propagating any failure with `?` so a single upstream hiccup returns 502 for the whole tab. Matching is by lower-cased name against the live payload, with hard-coded min_players=10, and silently limited to ~5 pages of history. Persisted battle_player_stats (player_name/player_key, is_friendly, kills, deaths, kill_fame) already contain exactly this data. The frontend 'me' tab then computes personal stats client-side by fetching /api/battles/{id} for each row (triggering battles-4) and filtering players by name in the browser.
findings.fix: Query battle_player_stats joined to snapshots for the caller's linked albion_player_name/id with SQL pagination, and return per-battle personal kills/deaths/fame/outcome in the list payload so the UI makes one request.
findings.verify_note: list_my_battles (service.rs:444-495) loops up to 5 pages and calls get_battle serially with ?, so any error fails the whole request. min_players is hard-coded to 10. The frontend buildPersonalScopeStats (battles.ts:833-852) fetches api/battles/{id} for every row (battles-4 write amplification) and matches by name in the browser.

findings.title: Intel auto-scout and guild report re-scan and re-load heavy data repeatedly
findings.description: scout_recent_snapshots loads the newest 50 snapshots with all JSON columns every 2 min. A battle that yields no drafts (battles we weren't in, or too few players) returns an empty Vec and writes no scouted_comp_battles row, so it is never marked processed and is re-parsed on every tick until it falls out of the 50-row window. For each unscouted snapshot scout_battle runs RoleClassifier::load (2 queries) and scouted_comp::find().all() (whole scout table) per battle instead of once per batch. build_guild_report loads every snapshot in the window with kills_json/players_json/losses_json (plus all users, links, comps, builds, scout_links) into memory; the 5-min ReportCache is only invalidated by the manual refresh route, never when sync adds battles.
findings.fix: Record a 'scouted_at' (or negative marker) per snapshot, load classifier and existing scouts once per batch, select only needed columns, and precompute report inputs from evidence tables (battle_player_stats/battle_guild_stats, fight_stats) with SQL aggregates. Invalidate ReportCache for the tenant from battle_sync when new snapshots land.
findings.verify_note: scout_recent_snapshots reads the newest SCAN_LIMIT=50 snapshots with all JSON columns. Battles with empty drafts get no scouted_comp_battles row, so they are re-parsed every tick. scout_battle reloads RoleClassifier and scouted_comp::find().all() per battle (intel/service.rs:201-213). The cost is bounded (50 rows per 2 minutes), so this is low rather than medium. I did not re-verify the ReportCache invalidation claim at depth.

findings.title: Discord battle embeds compute win/loss from env GUILD_NAME instead of the backend outcome
findings.description: The web client was fixed to render the backend's single outcome rule, but the bot still finds 'our' guild by guild.name === GUILD_NAME (env, default 'Weaklings', one value for every tenant the bot serves) and reads guild.winner: draws and unknown show as DEFEAT, allied-side wins are missed, a guild tenant whose Albion name isn't the env value gets no guild stats at all. BattleSummary already carries outcome (stamped by the backend). The announcement and /battles list therefore disagree with the website for the same battle.
findings.fix: Use battle.outcome and a backend-provided friendly flag (battles-17) in battle.embed.ts; drop GUILD_NAME. Better: have the backend return a ready-to-render announcement payload so both clients render identical data.
findings.verify_note: battle.embed.ts:34-36 finds the guild by name === guildName (config GUILD_NAME, default 'Weaklings') and uses guild.winner. It ignores the backend outcome, which the bot's BattleSummary type does not even declare (types.ts:401). poller.ts:2050 passes GUILD_NAME. Draws and unknown show as DEFEAT.

findings.title: Frontend decides which guild is 'ours' by comparing the Discord tenant name to the Albion guild name
findings.description: BattleGuildSummary has no is_friendly/is_own marker, so detail, fight-detail and group pages guess: profile.tenant_name (the Discord server name) lowercased and matched to guild names, falling back to the literal 'weaklings'; ally detection then uses the matched guild's alliance name. A tenant whose Discord server name differs from its Albion guild (the common case) shows no 'our guild' stats, ally split, K/D, survivors or friendly/enemy player filter. The backend already knows the answer (FriendlySide/evidence.is_friendly).
findings.fix: Add is_friendly / is_own_guild to BattleGuildSummary and BattlePlayer (and per-kill participants) in the API, fed by the tenant FriendlySide (alliance-aware, battles-1); delete the name-matching code in the three components.
findings.verify_note: The backend models.rs has no is_friendly or is_own field. fight-detail.ts:1254-1282 matches profile.tenant_name to the guild name with a 'weaklings' default (DEFAULT_OUR_GUILD_NAME). battle-group.ts:432 and battles.ts:859 use the same name guess. The Discord tenant name often differs from the Albion guild name, so 'our guild' stats go missing.

findings.title: Discord can only list battles and announce them; web-only battle detail, fights, trends, intel, enemies, fingerprints, and different data source for the list
findings.description: The bot has no command for battle detail, fights/trends, intel scouts/matchups/report, enemy dossiers or fingerprints; all exist as backend APIs and web pages. The web 'guild' tab lists canonical Fights (/api/fights) while /battles in Discord lists raw AlbionBB battles (/api/battles), so the 'same' list differs in grouping, counts and outcome semantics. The nav buttons parse the page with `Number(rest[0]) ?? 1` (NaN instead of 1 on a bad id) and /battles always uses limit 10 without a min_players option.
findings.fix: Add /fight (list+detail with outcome, losses), /intel and /enemy commands that call the same endpoints and render backend-shaped data; point /battles at the same /api/fights source (or expose a unified endpoint). Fix the NaN fallback with Number.isFinite.
findings.verify_note: The bot commands directory has no fight, intel or enemy command, and nothing in the bot references api/fights or api/intel. /battles uses api/battles with limit 10 (commands/battles.ts:25-40), while the web guild tab uses fights. The NaN claim is technically true (button.ts:1068, Number(rest[0]) ?? 1) but trivial, because the bot builds those customIds itself.

findings.title: Two parallel fight-analytics implementations disagree (fights.rs from snapshots vs fight_analytics persisted)
findings.description: /api/fights/{id} recomputes outcome, totals, guilds, players and losses by re-parsing snapshot JSON (3.3k-line fights.rs) with env Config, while /api/fight-analytics/{id} and intel matchups/reports read fights.outcome and fight_stats computed from the evidence tables with the tenant FriendlySide. The same fight can therefore show different outcome, kills/deaths and silver lost depending on the page. get_fight_trends uses a third rule (guild.winner OR-ed across any matching guild, fights.rs:1645-1650) rather than battle_outcome, so trend win rate contradicts the list. Is_stale/outcome_method from fight_analytics is never surfaced in /fights.
findings.fix: Make fight_analytics the single source: /api/fights list and detail read fights.outcome + fight_stats (+ battle_guild_stats/battle_player_stats for tables), trends aggregate fight_stats. Delete the snapshot re-derivation in fights.rs and shrink the file to grouping/mutation endpoints.
findings.verify_note: /api/fights recomputes outcome from snapshot JSON with env Config (fights.rs:738+). fight_analytics persists fights.outcome and fight_stats from the evidence tables. Trends OR the guild.winner flag (fights.rs:~1645) instead of using battle_outcome. Three rules coexist, so results can disagree.

findings.title: Giant battle payloads and unbounded side loads (raw kills in every response, all albion_links, role filter loads all enemies)
findings.description: BattleDetail returns every kill with the entire upstream raw JSON (full equipment/inventory/participant arrays) plus all players on each GET, and the same blobs are stored again in guild_battle_snapshots.kills_json and in battle_kills/items, tripling storage; no response compression layer is configured in lib.rs. fight_participant_analytics loads every albion_link row for the tenant instead of the participant ids. enemies list_players with a role filter loads all enemy_players and a latest-battle lookup for every one before paginating in memory.
findings.fix: Drop raw from the default payload (separate ?include=raw or a /kills endpoint) and stop persisting it in kills_json; add tower-http CompressionLayer; filter albion_links by discord ids from participations; push the role filter into SQL via a latest-battle join/materialized last role column.
findings.verify_note: BattleKillEvent.raw returns the full upstream JSON in every detail response (models.rs:150). fight_participant_analytics loads albion_link::find().all() (fights.rs:~1945). enemies list_players with a role filter does query.all() and filters in memory (enemies/service.rs:288). The backend has no CompressionLayer, though a reverse proxy may compress. Low.

logic_questions: Alliance scope: should an alliance tenant show an aggregated, read-only view of all member guilds' battles/fights/enemy intel (materialized into the alliance schema vs live fan-out), and which member data is private (e.g. silver loss, per-player stats, scouts) versus shared? Should alliance admins see per-guild breakdowns, and should members opt out?

Friendly side: when a guild joins an alliance, should all sibling member guilds (alliance_memberships) automatically count as friendly for outcomes/evidence/enemy classification, in addition to the manual allied ids/names? And should the guild's own Albion alliance (albion_alliance_id / the alliance tag AlbionBB reports) also count as friendly?

What is a 'battle result' for an in-progress or split battle: how long after the last kill should a battle be considered final before it is snapshotted, announced in Discord and counted in fights? Should the bot announce at start, at end, or both (edit the message)?

Which battles should be tracked at all: is min_players=10 the intended product rule (smaller skirmishes ignored by the worker, fights, intel) or should it be a per-tenant setting? Should the bot, web list and worker share the same threshold?

Which list is canonical for the guild: raw AlbionBB battles (/api/battles, used by Discord) or canonical Fights (/api/fights, used by the web 'guild' tab)? Should Discord expose both and should outcome/stats always come from fights.outcome + fight_stats?

Loss estimates: should silver loss be priced at snapshot time and frozen, or recomputed with current market prices? Which pricing rule (sell-min in the regear pricing city with fallback vs min of sell/buy across all qualities) is the product rule, and should allied guilds' losses count as 'ours'?
Should the raw /api/albionbb/* and /api/albiondata/* passthroughs remain public to every authenticated member, or can they be removed/permissioned since /api/battles supersedes them?

Is a per-battle write on GET (hydrate on open) intentional product behavior (e.g. officers expect opening a battle to refresh it), or should detail be strictly read-only with a separate 'refresh from AlbionBB' action?

summary: Members/warns/progression/applications/notifications/audit are per-tenant Postgres schemas, each with a Rust service and an Axum router. Discord (bot) and Angular both call the same HTTP API; the bot authenticates with X-Bot-Secret plus X-Discord-Id (and X-Discord-Role-Ids) and is mapped to a local users row. Users are keyed by discord_id. They are created at OAuth login, by /register, or by POST /api/users, and alliance tenants receive copies only through albion/alliance_fanout.rs at register/link time. Warns: POST /api/warns inserts a row, optionally overwrites the account XP multiplier of the covering season, opens at most one escalation row at the threshold, writes an inbox notification (status 'pending' DM) and an audit row; nothing touches Discord roles or officers. Progression: XP is idempotent per (season, key); message XP comes from a bot MessageCreate handler with a local cooldown gate, event and VOD XP are awarded server-side, and officers adjust XP via /xp or the user-detail page. guild_ranks carry Discord role ids that are display-only. Applications and tickets are Discord-only flows: the bot posts, the backend records state and returns role ids, and the bot itself applies the Discord roles. Trials rows are written on accept-as-trial and then nothing ever reads them. Notifications are an in-app inbox plus a broadcast; the 'Discord DM worker' referred to in the code does not exist. Audit is a manual AuditService::log call in about 40 places, which inserts a row and then synchronously posts embeds to Discord. Attention is an enemy-intel recompute endpoint with no consumer. Alliance gating (no warns, applications, etc.) exists only in the bot command allowlist and Angular guards, not in the backend. Net: web and Discord overlap on warn, xp, rank and users. Applications, tickets, VODs and trials have no web counterpart; the web inbox, broadcast and role management have no Discord counterpart. Alliance member aggregation and the notification-to-Discord path are essentially unimplemented.

findings.title: Discord DM delivery for notifications is never implemented; every DM stays 'pending' forever
findings.description: insert_many marks every non-event notification discord_dm_status='pending' ('Waiting for the background worker'), but no worker exists in backend or bot: grep for DiscordDmStatus/discord_dm finds only the writer and entity. So a warn issued on the web, regear/bank/split/giveaway results and officer broadcasts reach only people who open the web inbox. Discord-first members never get them, and the DM rows pile up as pending/attempts=0 (status never leaves 'pending'). Only /warn in the bot DMs the target itself (warn.ts:80-105), so web-issued and bot-issued warns behave differently.
findings.fix: Add a backend DM outbox worker (like events/fanout_worker.rs and mirror_retry) that claims pending rows with attempts/backoff, sends via the bot token to users.discord_id, and sets sent/skipped/failed. Remove the DM from commands/warn.ts. Optionally add a /notifications bot command that reads the same inbox.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. insert_many sets discord_dm_status=Pending for every kind where queues_discord_dm() is true (service.rs:251-256). Grepping DiscordDm/discord_dm over backend and bot code finds only the notifications writer, status and entity, plus the migration. No worker or bot poller consumes them. The rows stay pending/attempts=0. Not critical: the web inbox works, the notifications README documents that it sends no Discord messages, and nothing is lost or corrupted. Downgraded from critical to high.

findings.title: VOD XP claim trusts client-supplied thread/forum/owner data; any member can farm XP via the web API
findings.description: vod.submit is granted to every member.
