POST /api/vods accepts forum_channel_id, thread_owner_discord_id, discord_thread_id from the request body and only compares them to the configured forum id (readable via GET /api/progression/settings by anyone with progression.view) and to the caller's own discord id. A web session or any member can POST arbitrary unique URLs with fabricated thread data and receive xp_vod each time (dedupe is only per normalized URL). The backend never verifies the thread exists, the owner, that the URL is in the thread, or the URL host. The bot's success embed says 'Pending Officer Review' but the XP is already granted, and no officer review step exists.
findings.fix: Verify server-side with the bot token that the thread exists, its parent is the VOD forum and its owner_id equals the claimer, and that the message/URL is in it (or restrict the endpoint to bot-secret requests only). Add a daily cap, a host allowlist (youtube/twitch/etc.), and either a real officer approval state before XP or fix the copy.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. VodService::submit (vods/service.rs:47-84) only compares the client-supplied forum_channel_id to the configured forum, and thread_owner_discord_id to the caller's own id. It never verifies the thread, the URL, or the host. vod.submit is granted to every member (seed migration line 36). Dedupe is only per season+URL (unique index). XP is awarded immediately, while the bot embed says 'Pending Officer Review'. Real, but it needs an authenticated member and only inflates XP, so medium rather than high.

findings.title: Alliance member directory only syncs at /register time; POST /api/users, guild accept and failures never reach the alliance tenant
findings.description: The only path that copies a user + Albion link into the paired tenant is after_successful_link, called from albion/router link/register handlers. (1) create_user (web 'Add member') never calls it, so web-provisioned members are missing in the alliance schema. (2) accept_alliance_membership only flips status to active; guild members who registered earlier are never backfilled into the alliance schema (and the alliance role grant is not applied). (3) Every step in the fan-out discards errors (let _ = record_membership, tracing::warn on link copy) with no outbox/retry, unlike the event mirror system. (4) Role/username/unlink changes do not propagate. (5) No alliance-wide roster/members/warn-summary/leaderboard endpoint aggregates the member guilds, so /api/users in an alliance tenant lists only whoever happened to register after joining.
findings.fix: Move membership sync into a backend job: on membership activation backfill all guild users with an Albion link into the alliance tenant; on create_user/unlink/rename enqueue a persistent outbox item per active alliance; add GET /api/alliance/members that aggregates users (and optionally XP/warn counts) across active guild tenants with a guild column.
findings.verify_note: Partly true, partly wrong. True: create_user (users/router.rs:427-499) never calls alliance_fanout. Fan-out steps swallow errors (let _ = record_membership, tracing::warn on link copy) with no retry. Role and username changes are not propagated. There is no alliance-wide members aggregate endpoint. False or overstated: unlink does propagate (albion/router.rs:466 -> after_successful_unlink, alliance_fanout.rs:216-252). Accept does not backfill eagerly, but adopt_existing_member_link (alliance_fanout.rs:296-352, called from GET /api/albion/link/me, and from the bot's GuildMemberAdd handler for alliance tenants) lazily copies a guild link into the alliance schema on the member's first alliance touch. So the gap is members who never touch the alliance tenant, plus the missing outbox and aggregate roster.

findings.title: Trial system is half-built: rows are written on accept-as-trial and never read, expired or removed
findings.description: modules/trials has no router, no list, promote, terminate or extend endpoints and no expiry job; no frontend or bot code reads trials. The bot adds the Trial Discord role on accept-as-trial but nothing ever shows remaining time, marks 'expired', removes the role, or notifies officers. Acceptance criteria 4-6 of the plan (trials.view/manage permissions, /admin/trials page, promote/terminate/extend with audit) are unimplemented. start_from_accept also runs after resolve(accepted), so a failure at that point leaves an accepted application with no trial row.
findings.fix: Implement slices 3-4 in the backend: GET /api/trials (computed remaining_seconds/expired), POST promote/terminate/extend using assign/revoke_discord_role, audit entries, trials.* permissions, a periodic expiry notification to officers, plus a web page and a /trials bot command. Wrap resolve + trial insert in one transaction.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. trials/mod.rs exposes only entities and service, with no router. mod.rs says the list and manager actions 'land in later slices'. Nothing in the frontend or bot reads trials. start_from_accept runs after ApplicationService::resolve (applications/router.rs:210-212), so there is no transaction. Mostly an acknowledged unfinished feature, so medium.

findings.title: GET /api/users/me/metrics loads every event and every battle snapshot twice and parses JSON per request
findings.description: get_metrics does GuildBattleSnapshotEntity::find().all() and deserializes every losses_json (line 368), then personal_activity does event::Entity::find().all() (412) and a second GuildBattleSnapshotEntity::find().all() deserializing every players_json (467). The dashboard calls this on every load alongside bank, progression, events. Cost grows with battle history and blocks the page the owner calls slow. Correctness: attendance_streak (line 422) counts from the newest event including future/cancelled ones, so a single upcoming event the member has not joined makes the streak 0; events_total/attendance_rate include future and cancelled events.
findings.fix: Aggregate in SQL or against already-parsed per-player rows (battle player tables) filtered by the member's player id/name, cache the result per user for ~60s, and restrict events to past, non-cancelled ones for streak and rate.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. users/service.rs get_metrics runs GuildBattleSnapshotEntity::find().all() and parses losses_json (lines 366-377). personal_activity then runs event::Entity::find().all() (412) and a second full snapshot scan that parses players_json (467-478). The streak takes the newest event, including future or unjoined ones (lines 416-424), so it can read 0. events_total counts all events, with no status filter. Real hot-path cost.

findings.title: AuditService::log can panic on a multi-byte JSON truncate, after the audited mutation already committed
findings.description: det_str is serde_json::to_string_pretty output (non-ASCII not escaped). When it exceeds 1000 bytes, String::truncate(1000) panics if byte 1000 is not a char boundary. Warn reasons / audit details with Italian accents, Cyrillic or emoji make this reachable (the warn reason is included in the details). The panic occurs after the warn row, XP multiplier and escalation were committed, so the officer gets a failed/dropped request, retries and creates a duplicate warn.
findings.fix: Truncate on a char boundary (det_str.chars().take(...) or floor_char_boundary) and cap the reason length at input validation.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. String::truncate(1000) at audit/service.rs:231-234 and 309-312 panics when byte 1000 is not a char boundary. It is reachable when details exceed 1000 bytes and contain multibyte characters, with a warn reason in details (warns/service.rs:108-121). It only runs when Config::try_from_env succeeds, a bot token is set, and an audit channel is configured. The warn row, multiplier and escalation are already committed by then. Severity medium: conditional on a long non-ASCII reason plus audit channel config.

findings.title: Every audited action awaits Discord HTTP, re-parses env, creates a new reqwest Client and does extra DB lookups inline
findings.description: AuditService::log calls Config::try_from_env() (envy parse) on every call, loads guild settings, looks up the actor and the target user, builds embeds and POSTs to Discord with up to 3 attempts and sleep(retry_after) on 429, all awaited inside the request handler (e.g. warn issue/revoke/ack, XP adjust, role changes). A Discord slowdown or rate limit adds seconds to the web and Discord commands and a new TLS client is built per call. audit_middleware is dead code (a no-op with stale comments).
findings.fix: Insert the audit row only inside the request; push the Discord embed into a background queue/task using a shared Client and the Config from Extension. Delete audit/middleware.rs.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. AuditService::log calls Config::try_from_env() per call (service.rs:143-160), does guild settings and user lookups, and awaits send_discord_payload. That creates Client::new() per call and retries up to 3 times with sleep(retry_after) on a 429 (lines 367-420), all inline in the request. audit/middleware.rs is a no-op and audit_middleware is not referenced anywhere.

findings.title: Warns have no Discord-side effect and escalation notifies nobody; the bot DM promises automatic penalties that do not exist
findings.description: Reaching warn_threshold only inserts a warn_escalations row plus an audit entry; no officer notification, attention item, Discord ping, role (e.g. 'Warned'), timeout or review ticket is produced. Officers only see it if they open /warns or the web tab. The DM text in warn.ts says 'Repeated warnings escalate automatically to guild penalties or removal', which is false. A warn issued on the web produces no DM at all (see members-1), so the same action behaves differently depending on the surface.
findings.fix: On escalation open, notify users holding warns.issue (inbox + Discord channel post), and optionally apply a configurable Discord role. Do the DM in the backend for both surfaces and change the copy.
findings.verify_note: Mostly confirmed. maybe_open_escalation (warns/service.rs:407-453) only inserts the row and writes an audit entry. There is no notification, role or timeout. warn.ts:90-94 does claim 'escalate automatically to guild penalties or removal'. One qualification: the WARN_ESCALATION_OPEN audit entry is posted to the Discord audit channel when one is configured, so 'notifies nobody' is slightly overstated. It is a design or parity gap rather than a defect, so medium.

findings.title: Revoking a warn does not undo the XP multiplier it applied; no-expiry multipliers stay forever
findings.description: issue() overwrites progression_accounts.xp_multiplier for the covering season (also overwriting a stronger or longer existing penalty/boost), and revoke() only closes the escalation. A mistaken strike with multiplier 0 and no expiry zeroes the member's XP for the whole season even after revoke; the only fix is a manual /xp multiplier. The multiplier failure is also swallowed (warn only logged) so the warn row exists while the multiplier silently was not applied. warn insert, multiplier, escalation are not in a transaction (a concurrent issue hits the unique open-escalation index after the warn is saved, returning 500 for a persisted warn).
findings.fix: Store the multiplier on the warn row only and compute the effective multiplier from active (non-revoked, non-expired) warns, or restore the previous multiplier on revoke. Wrap issue in one transaction.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. revoke() (warns/service.rs:230-273) only closes the escalation and never touches progression_accounts. apply_account_multiplier (progression/service.rs:562-580) overwrites xp_multiplier and expiry unconditionally. A multiplier failure is only logged. The warn insert, multiplier and escalation are separate non-transactional steps (service.rs:80-106).

findings.title: Members cannot see their own warns on web or Discord, and the warn notification links to a page they cannot open
findings.description: GET /api/warns requires warns.view (Officer+). WarnIssued notifications set link_path '/warns', whose route needs permissionGuard('warns.view'), so a plain member clicking their inbox item is bounced. user-detail loads warns only if canViewWarns. /me in Discord shows no warns, and /warns is Officer+. The only record a member gets of a warn is the bot DM (not sent for web-issued warns).
findings.fix: Add GET /api/warns/me (self-or-officer like progression/users/{id}), point the notification link at /users/{self} or a 'my record' section, and show active warn count and the threshold gauge in /me.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. GET /api/warns needs warns.view. WarnIssued uses link_path '/warns' (warns/service.rs:131). The /warns route needs permissionGuard('warns.view') (app.routes.ts:200-202). user-detail loads warns only if canViewWarns (user-detail.ts:564, 754). The bot /me and /rank commands show no warns.

findings.title: Progression /me reports an expired XP multiplier as active and never exposes the expiry
findings.description: award_inner correctly treats a multiplier as 1.0 once multiplier_expires_at passed, but get_me returns row.xp_multiplier raw. A member with an expired ×0.5 warn penalty keeps seeing ×0.5 in /rank, /me and the web dashboard/user page until the next award rewrites the row. The view also lacks multiplier_expires_at, so neither surface can show 'ends in 3 days'.
findings.fix: In get_me apply multiplier_expired(), and add multiplier_expires_at to ProgressionMeView, then render it in the bot and the web.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. get_me returns row.xp_multiplier raw (progression/service.rs:78-82, 96), while award_inner applies multiplier_expired (208-218). ProgressionMeView carries no expiry. This is a display-only inaccuracy, so low.

findings.title: guild_ranks Discord role ids are configured but nothing ever assigns them; XP/rank/level-ups never reach Discord
findings.description: Admins can store a discord_role_id per rank tier (validated, unique), but rank_tier_for_xp is used only to display the tier name in the API view. No code assigns or removes those roles on level-up, season change or XP adjust, and the bot has no handler or poller for it. The bot /rank and /me do not even show the guild_rank tier name that the web shows. No level-up announcement or notification exists either.
findings.fix: After award/adjust/season activation compare old and new rank tier and enqueue a role change through the backend Discord role helper (assign_discord_role/revoke_discord_role), plus an inbox notification; show guild_rank in /rank and /me.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. guild_ranks_json is read only by rank_tier_for_xp (service.rs:96) for display, and validated and stored. No code assigns or revokes Discord roles from it. The bot rank.ts shows no guild_rank. A configured-but-dead feature.

findings.title: Bot /warns labels all escalations 'Open' (never passes open_only) and the per-member record undercounts
findings.description: The overview calls api/warns/escalations with no query, so the backend returns all escalations (acknowledged and closed too, open_only defaults false) with the default limit of 10, but the embed is titled 'Open Escalations (N)' and colours the embed red whenever any exist. For a single member it fetches limit 20 sorted newest first and computes active warns and the gauge from that page, so members with more than 20 warns (including revoked) get a wrong count.
findings.fix: Pass open_only=true, and add a backend per-user summary field (active_count, threshold) on a dedicated endpoint instead of recomputing in the bot.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. warns.ts:35-38 calls api/warns/escalations with no open_only, and the backend defaults it to false (warns/router.rs:207). The embed is titled 'Open Escalations (N)' (line 73-77), and the default limit is 10. The per-member view uses limit 20 (line 100-105) and computes active warns from that page. Cosmetic or accuracy issue, so low.

findings.title: Applications, tickets and VODs are Discord-only; the web cannot list or review them, and accept relies on the bot to apply roles
findings.description: The applications API has only create/active/latest/reopen/accept/decline/close and tickets only create/active/close: there is no list or detail endpoint, and no frontend page other than the settings form. accept/decline require UserContext so they work from the web, but the backend only returns default_role_discord_id/trial_role_discord_id and the bot applies them (remove auto role, add member role, add trial role). An accept from any non-bot client marks the application accepted and assigns nothing. If the bot's members.fetch/roles.add throws after the backend resolved (e.g. the applicant left), the application is permanently non-open with no role and no retry. ApplicationService::create and TicketService::create also check-then-insert (only the unique index on applications prevents duplicates; tickets rely on the check). /applications-panel is gated by Discord ManageGuild in the bot, not by backend permissions.
findings.fix: Add GET /api/applications and /api/tickets (filters, pagination) and an inbox page. Move role assignment into the backend accept handler (using assign_discord_role with the bot token) so web and bot behave the same, and make it idempotent/retriable.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. The applications router (router.rs:56-66) has no list or detail route. The tickets router has only create, active and close (tickets/router.rs:46-52). There is no web inbox page. Role assignment on accept happens only in the bot (button.ts:313-330) after the backend has already resolved the application, so a throw in members.fetch or roles.add leaves it accepted with no role and no retry. A web accept assigns nothing. This is a real parity break against goal 2.

findings.title: Alliance exclusion (no warns, applications, VODs, tickets) is enforced only in the bot and Angular, not the backend
findings.description: FEATURE_GATES in tenant.rs has no entries for /api/warns, /api/vods, /api/tickets, /api/notifications, /api/users POST, and nothing checks CurrentTenantKind there. A session bound to an alliance tenant (or a bot request with X-Guild-Id of the alliance) can call POST /api/warns, /api/applications, /api/vods and receive state in the alliance schema, contradicting plans/alliance-management.md ('Un Discord alleanza non espone bank/warns/regear/applications').
findings.fix: Add a kind requirement table next to FEATURE_GATES and reject guild-only prefixes for kind=alliance in resolve_tenant.
findings.verify_note: Partly overstated. FEATURE_GATES (tenant.rs) does gate /api/warns and /api/applications behind the 'warns' and 'applications' feature flags, enforced in resolve_tenant. So they are blocked for alliance tenants unless the alliance's rank grants those features. /api/vods, /api/tickets, /api/notifications and POST /api/users have no gate and no kind check, so that part holds. Reaching it requires a session bound to an alliance tenant or a bot request, and the UI and bot hide it. Low severity.

findings.title: No member offboarding or role-change sync from Discord; ex-members stay in users, leaderboards and broadcasts
findings.description: The bot handles only GuildMemberAdd (join role, alliance link adoption). There is no GuildMemberRemove/Update handler, no users.active/left_at column, and users.role is a cache refreshed only at login or via the web role editor. A member who leaves Discord keeps appearing in /users, the XP leaderboard, member pickers (warn form), regear/split lists and as a broadcast recipient; roles changed directly in Discord are stale on /users and the role filter until that person logs in again.
findings.fix: Add a left_at/active flag set by a GuildMemberRemove handler (and by a periodic reconcile against the Discord member list), filter leaderboards and pickers by active, and handle GuildMemberUpdate to refresh the cached role.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. The bot has no GuildMemberRemove or GuildMemberUpdate handler (grep finds none). The users entity has no left_at or active column. Broadcast sends to UserEntity::find().all() (notifications/service.rs:179-185). I found no code that deletes users. users.role is a cache refreshed at login.

findings.title: GET /api/users and /api/users/{id} expose every member's email to any authenticated user; sort/role use stale columns
findings.description: The directory is open to all logged-in members and UserProfile includes email (real Discord OAuth emails for those who logged in). Any member can dump all emails with limit paging. sort=username sorts the raw Discord username column while the UI displays the Albion name resolved via display_name, so the table order looks random; role filter matches the cached users.role string.
findings.fix: Drop email from the response unless the caller has users.view-sensitive permission, and sort/filter on the resolved display name via a join on albion_links.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. list_users takes only _user: UserContext with no permission check, and UserProfile includes email (users/service.rs:41-50, 620-640). The frontend shows the email column (users.ts:261). The sort map uses the raw Username column while display names are resolved afterwards. Privacy exposure within a guild.

findings.title: Web warns page: member picker limited to first 100 users, stat cards computed from the current page only
findings.description: loadMembers fetches api/users with limit 100 and no search, so guilds with more than 100 members cannot warn the rest from the web (the bot path has no such cap). activeWarnsCount, strikesCount and notesCount are derived from this.warns(), i.e. the loaded page (default 20), not totals, so the headline numbers change when paging or filtering. user-detail fetches only 50 warns without a total.
findings.fix: Use a server-side searchable member combobox and expose aggregate counts from the backend (e.g. /api/warns/summary).
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. warns.ts:718 loads api/users with limit 100 and no search. The stat counters are computed from this.warns(), the loaded page (lines 470-478). user-detail fetches limit 50 warns with no total (lines 1217-1223).

findings.title: VOD claim is not atomic: a failed XP award is swallowed and the URL can never be reclaimed
findings.description: The vod_reviews row is inserted first; if ProgressionService::award errors (DB blip, locks) it is only logged and the API still returns success. Resubmitting the same URL then returns 409 'already claimed', so the member permanently loses the XP while the UI said it was submitted. A concurrent double submit hits the unique index after the existence check and returns 500 instead of 409.
findings.fix: Insert the claim and the award in one transaction (or make the award idempotent with retry), and map the unique violation to 409.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. The vod_reviews row is inserted first, then an award error is only logged (vods/service.rs:87-126). Resubmitting then hits the existing-row check and returns 409. A concurrent double submit would hit the unique idx_vod_reviews_season_url after the existence check and surface as a DB error, giving 500 rather than 409. It needs an award failure or a race, so low.

findings.title: /api/attention/findings has no consumer and does a delete-and-reinsert write transaction on every GET
findings.description: No frontend or bot code calls it (the dashboard's 'attention' list is computed locally from balance/metrics/events). The endpoint is a GET that scans 60 days of fights and fight_stats and rewrites the attention_findings table each call; two concurrent callers contend on the same delete/insert. Its rules are about enemy intel and win rate, not about members (open escalations, expiring trials, unlinked members, pending applications), so there is no member attention feed at all.
findings.fix: Either wire it to a UI with a scheduled recompute (worker) and read-only GET, or remove it. Add member-attention rules (open escalations, expired trials, unlinked members, pending applications) in the backend and render them on both surfaces.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. Grepping the frontend and bot finds no call to api/attention. The dashboard attention list is computed locally. The handler calls recompute_attention_findings, which rewrites the table, on every GET (attention/router.rs:50-58). It is dead code or an unused endpoint.

findings.title: Broadcast and mark-all-read are O(n) sequential statements; several notification kinds are never emitted
findings.description: broadcast loads all users and runs one INSERT per user inside the transaction (hundreds of round trips for large guilds, including ex-members); mark_all_read selects all unread rows then updates each one individually instead of a single update_many. EventCreated and EventReminder1h kinds are defined and documented but nothing emits them; applications accepted/declined, trial events, XP adjusts and escalations create no notification.
findings.fix: Use insert_many with on_conflict do_nothing and a single UPDATE ... WHERE user_id AND read_at IS NULL; emit the missing kinds or delete them.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed. mark_all_read selects every unread row and updates each one individually (notifications/service.rs:141-153). broadcast runs one insert per user inside the transaction (insert_many loop, lines 257-285). EventCreated is only referenced in a unit test (service.rs:644). Nothing in production code emits EventCreated or EventReminder1h.

findings.title: No hierarchy or self checks on warn, revoke and XP adjust; several member actions are not audited
findings.description: An officer can issue a warn against an Admin or themselves, revoke warns issued against themselves, and use progression.adjust on their own account (add_xp/set_multiplier); only the role-assignment path enforces priority. Audit rows exist for warns, role changes, XP adjust, but not for applications accept/decline/close, trial creation, POST /api/users member provisioning, VOD claims or broadcasts. The audit web table shows a raw numeric user_id for the operator.
findings.fix: Reuse ensure_priority_allowed for warn/revoke/adjust targets, forbid self-adjust/self-revoke, add AuditService entries for the missing actions, and return operator display names in /api/audit.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed as a policy gap. warns issue and revoke have no target hierarchy or self check, and the code even handles self-warn (req.user_id != issuer_user_id). progression adjust_user checks only the permission. ensure_priority_allowed is used only in users/member_roles.rs. The applications, vods, trials and notifications modules have no AuditService calls. Low severity.

logic_questions: Alliance scope: should an alliance tenant aggregate member guilds' data (member roster, warns/escalation counts, XP leaderboard, applications), read-only or with write actions? plans/alliance-management.md says the alliance must not behave like a guild with warns/applications, while the goal is that alliances sync everything with member guilds. Options: (a) alliance only gets a unified read-only roster + leaderboard, (b) alliance officers can see/issue warns across member guilds, (c) strictly no member discipline data in the alliance.
Should a warn on a guild affect that person's standing in the alliance tenant (shared warn, alliance-level ban list) or stay local to the guild?

Trial system: confirm that auto-removal at expiry stays off (plan says managers decide), but should an expired trial notify officers and be visible in a web list, and should promote/terminate be executable from both the web and a Discord command?

Warn multiplier semantics: should the multiplier be tied to the warn (disappears on revoke or expiry, and the effective value is the minimum across active warns), or remain an account-level override that officers set manually?

guild_ranks.discord_role_id is documented as display-only. Do you want rank tiers to actually assign Discord roles on level-up (and remove the previous tier role)? If yes, should that run in alliance tenants too?

VOD reviews: is XP meant to be granted immediately on claim (current behavior) or only after an officer approves it? The bot copy says 'Pending Officer Review'. Also which hosts count as valid VODs and what daily limit per member is acceptable?

Notifications: should every inbox notification also be DM'd on Discord by default (current intent via discord_dm_status), or should members opt in per kind? Should broadcasts also post to a Discord announcements channel?
Members who leave the Discord: should their users row be deactivated (hidden from leaderboards/pickers but kept for history/bank), and should warns/XP survive if they rejoin?
Should plain members be allowed to see their own warn history (reasons, issuer) on web and /me, or only be told via notification that a warn exists?
Applications: should web officers be able to accept/decline applications (with the backend assigning Discord roles itself), or is the Discord ticket thread meant to remain the only workflow?

summary:
The bot is a single Node process with one discord.js Client. Backend changes reach Discord through polling only. index.ts creates a PollerManager (services/poller-manager.ts). It starts one Poller per Discord guild that is a registered tenant, whether the tenant kind is guild or alliance. It discovers new tenants on GuildCreate and through a 5-minute reconcile(). Each Poller runs setInterval at POLL_INTERVAL_MS (default 60s). Every tick runs poll() (poller.ts:476), a long sequential pipeline: application status, new events, VOD forum, event revisions, closed events, restored events, roster sync, calendar sync, giveaways, giveaway results, event lifecycle (mass/start/auto-stop), voice sweep, then battles, 1h reminders and split sync via Promise.allSettled.

The cursors are NOT stored in the backend. They live in a per-guild JSON file under POLLER_STATE_DIR (poller.ts:87-143, 329-336). The file holds lastEventId, lastBattleId, lastGiveawayId, the split (updated_at,id) cursor, the pendingAnnounces retry queue, and the Discord ids of every event thread, parent message, signup card and calendar page. The event-thread to event-id mapping that thread slash commands use (findEventIdForThread) exists only in that file. The backend events entity has no discord_thread_id (apps/backend/src/modules/events/entities.rs:60-76). Splits are the exception: the backend stores thread_id and the bot uses a backend cursor contract (api/splits/discord-sync). Applications also store their panel message id in backend settings.

New-record detection lists the backend with sort=created_at desc and scans every page up to 50 pages on every tick (listSinceCheckpoint, poller.ts:751-781). Updates are detected through a cheap api/events/revisions fingerprint. Several time-based behaviours are implemented in the bot instead of the backend: scheduled mass and start, the 1h reminder, voice-empty auto-stop, the flash undo window, and the voice-channel sweep. The bot calls the backend with the shared X-Bot-Secret, X-Guild-Id and the actor's X-Discord-Id/Role-Ids (api/client.ts). It has no timeout, retry, 429 handling or batching.

Tenant settings and tenant status are cached for 60s (settings.ts, tenant-gate.ts). The bot does little alliance handling. command-gate.ts has a hard-coded alliance command allowlist. event-join-guild.ts resolves guild attribution. index.ts adopts Albion links on member join. poller.ts:2163-2205 posts to an alliance channel from a member guild's poller via event.alliance_discord_channel_id. The Poller never learns the tenant kind, so an alliance tenant runs the same guild-oriented checks, such as battles.

The backend already has more mechanisms the bot does not use. These include a durable fanout_outbox with leased targets (modules/events/fanout_outbox.rs), fanout_worker/mirror_retry ticks, and an event_sessions worker with a 30s tick. The worker does not start for alliance tenants (tenant.rs:84-86). The backend also holds the bot token and calls Discord REST itself for roles and nicknames (albion/discord_guild_role.rs, discord_nick.rs). A notifications table queues Discord DMs (discord_dm_status=pending), but nothing consumes it.

Failure modes found: lost or corrupt state files cause silent reseeding that swallows announcements, and cursors can freeze or repeat. Mid-batch failures cause duplicate battle and giveaway posts. A start-up race creates duplicate Pollers. The lifecycle and reminder logic only looks at page 1 of a date-sorted list. A pruning bug drops thread mappings. Delivery failures are invisible to admins and the web. Polling cost grows with history.

findings.title: All Discord bindings and sync cursors live only in per-guild local JSON files, written non-atomically
findings.description: The event to thread to signup-card mapping, parent message ids, calendar message ids, lastEventId/lastBattleId/lastGiveawayId, pendingAnnounces and split cursors exist only in poller-state-<guild>.json. The backend event row stores no thread id. saveState() calls writeFileSync directly onto the target file, with no tmp+rename and no fsync. A crash mid-write, a lost volume or a redeploy onto an empty /app/data makes loadState() hit the catch branch and return createDefaultState() with initialized=false. adoptCheckpointBaseline() then reseeds every cursor to the current maximum and sends nothing. This silently swallows every event, battle and giveaway created while the state was unavailable. It also forgets every thread mapping, so roster/signup cards stop syncing and thread slash commands (resolveEventFromThread -> findEventIdForThread) answer 'not an event thread'. The same state ties the bot to exactly one running instance. Two replicas would each announce everything. The web cannot know what was delivered where.
findings.fix: Move bindings and cursors into the backend: a discord_bindings table (tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, channel_id, message_id, thread_id, revision, state) plus an outbox table, as in the target architecture (bot-arch-21). The splits contract (api/splits/{id}/discord-sync with saveState PUT of thread_id) already does this for one entity, so generalise it. Short term: write state via tmp file + rename, keep a .bak, and refuse to reseed when a previous file existed but is unreadable.
findings.verify_note: Core claim holds. All cursors and thread/signup mappings live in poller-state-<guild>.json (poller.ts:87-143). saveState uses plain writeFileSync with no tmp+rename (poller.ts:329-336). An unreadable file falls to createDefaultState() with initialized=false (poller.ts:172-196, 313-318), then the baseline reseed silently swallows everything created meanwhile. The backend event row holds no thread id, only vod_forum_thread_id (events/entities.rs:74). Not critical: docker-compose.yml:88-90 mounts a persistent named volume, so the lost-volume scenario is not the default. A mid-write crash needs a very narrow window. Real impact is the architecture gap: the web cannot see delivery state, and it is single-instance only.

findings.title: Partial-scan flag freezes baseline and cursors, and makes battles re-post forever once history exceeds 50 pages
findings.description: listSinceCheckpoint reads at most min(total_pages, 50) pages and returns complete=false beyond that. Events and giveaways use limit 50, so the cap is 2,500 rows. Battles use limit 10, so the cap is 500 rows. The backend allows limit up to 1000. When complete is false, adoptCheckpointBaseline throws, so a tenant that was never initialised stays silent forever. In checkNewBattles the loop sends every battle above lastBattleId on each tick and only advances the cursor if complete. With an incomplete scan, the same battles are re-posted into Discord every 60s. In checkNewEvents an incomplete scan never advances lastEventId, so the same announceable set is reconsidered every tick. Any long-lived tenant (every flash mass is an event) will eventually hit the 2,500 cap.
findings.fix: Stop paginating history. Use a backend cursor endpoint (id > after, ascending, limit N, has_more) or the outbox in bot-arch-21. Never gate cursor advance on a full scan. Send-then-advance per item, as checkSplitSync does.
findings.verify_note: Mechanics are real. listSinceCheckpoint caps at 50 pages and returns complete=false (poller.ts:751-781). adoptCheckpointBaseline throws on an incomplete scan (poller.ts:670-672). Battles and giveaways advance the cursor only if complete (poller.ts:2054, 2108). checkNewBattles re-sends every battle above the cursor on each tick, and checkNewGiveaways ignores postedGiveawayIds. Event re-announcement is blocked by the eventThreadIds guard (poller.ts:877-881), so duplicates there are limited. Reach is overstated: the cap is 2,500 events or giveaways, or 500 battles. Battles come from a catalog capped at GUILD_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES=20 upstream pages (battles/service.rs:57), so tripping the cap depends on the AlbionBB page size, which I could not confirm. Long-term risk, not immediate.

findings.title: Each guild poller rescans the whole history through HTTP every minute
findings.description: listSinceCheckpoint loops page 1..maxPages with no early exit, even when the first page is entirely at or below the checkpoint and the list is sorted by created_at desc. Per tick, per guild, that is up to 50 event pages, 50 battle pages and 50 giveaway pages (battles go through the AlbionBB hydrate path). On top of that: api/events/revisions, api/events/calendar, application settings, VOD pending/archived, split discovery, a 50-row events page for lifecycle, a 20-row page for reminders, and one GET per open giveaway. Cost grows linearly with history and with the number of tenants. This is a direct cause of the 'app is slow' report on the backend. All tenant pollers also start on the same 60s phase, so the load arrives in synchronised bursts.
findings.fix: Replace list-and-diff with a change feed (bot-arch-21). Interim: sort id desc and stop at the first page whose max id <= checkpoint; request limit=1000; add a bot-level aggregated endpoint, e.g. GET /api/bot/delta?since=<cursor>, that answers every poll in one call; add jitter to poller start times.
findings.verify_note: The loop runs page 1..maxPages with no early exit (poller.ts:769-780), every 60s per guild (config.ts POLL_INTERVAL_MS=60000). Battle pages go through list_guild_battles, which calls hydrate_page. That makes one AlbionBB get_battle per row on the page (battles/service.rs:125-170), and only the catalog is cached (60s TTL). At limit=10, N battles cost N/10 pages and about N detail calls per tick. Events and giveaways are sorted created_at desc, so an early exit is trivially possible. Cost scales with history and tenant count.

findings.title: Duplicate posts when a batch fails midway (battles, giveaways, alliance ping)
findings.description: checkNewBattles sends every new battle and advances lastBattleId only after the whole loop. If send #3 throws (permissions, rate limit, 5xx), posts 1 and 2 are already in Discord, the cursor is unchanged, and the next tick re-sends them. checkNewGiveaways has the same shape. Its filter is only id > lastGiveawayId, so postedGiveawayIds (which exists) is never consulted. If the PUT discord-message call fails after channel.send, the giveaway is posted again. postAllianceAnnouncement sends first and only then PATCHes alliance_discord_message_id. If the PATCH fails, the retry posts a second role-pinging alliance message. When no battles channel is configured, checkNewBattles returns without advancing, so whenever an admin finally sets a channel the whole accumulated backlog is flooded in.
findings.fix: Persist per-item delivery before moving on: write the Discord message id to the backend (outbox ack) immediately after send, and key idempotency on (entity,id,revision) in a backend delivery table. Skip items already in postedGiveawayIds. Advance the cursor per item. For a missing channel, mark the item skipped_unconfigured instead of leaving it as a backlog.
findings.verify_note: checkNewBattles sends in a loop and advances the cursor only after the loop (poller.ts:2049-2057). A throw is swallowed by the outer catch, so the sent items are re-sent next tick. checkNewGiveaways posts, then PUTs discord-message (poller.ts:2090-2097). A PUT failure, or a failure of a later item, leaves lastGiveawayId unchanged, and postedGiveawayIds is not used as a filter. With no battles channel, it returns without advancing (poller.ts:2043-2044), so the backlog floods in once a channel is set. postAllianceAnnouncement does send then PATCH, and a PATCH failure is only warned (poller.ts:2177-2186). The alliance ping repeats only when announceEvent retries, via pendingAnnounces or a later failure in the same call. That is narrower than the finding says, but real.

findings.title: Scheduled mass/start/1h-reminder only inspect page 1 of a date-sorted list, so due events are skipped
findings.description: checkEventLifecycle fetches api/events page 1, limit 50, with no status filter and the default sort. The default sort is event_date_utc DESC, newest-dated first, and it includes stopped events. checkUpcomingEvents does the same with limit 20. An event that is due now (date in the past or within the hour) sits behind every future-dated event. With more than 50 future or recent events, which an alliance with fanned-out copies reaches easily, the due event is never massed, never started and never reminded. The backend list supports ?status=scheduled and order=asc, but the bot does not use them. The lifecycle also uses a local massedEvents array as the idempotency key.
findings.fix: Move scheduling to the backend: the event_sessions worker already ticks every 30s. Make it perform the scheduled->live transition and emit mass_due / start_due / reminder_1h outbox items. The bot then only performs the Discord side effects (voice channel, thread message) and acks. Interim: query api/events?status=scheduled&order=asc, or add a dedicated GET /api/events/due.
findings.verify_note: checkEventLifecycle fetches api/events page 1, limit 50, with no status filter (poller.ts:1717-1718). checkUpcomingEvents uses limit 20 (poller.ts:1947-1953). The backend default sort is event_date_utc DESC (events/service.rs:2678-2696), so future-dated events fill page 1 ahead of due ones. It needs more than 50 (or more than 20) future or recent events to bite, which is plausible with alliance mirrors. Mass is idempotent via massedEvents and start is guarded by status. Severity is medium because it depends on volume.

findings.title: Thread-mapping pruning and the 200-id revisions cap make live threads get forgotten or closed
findings.description: (a) checkUpcomingEvents prunes pinged1hEvents to 50, then also filters state.eventThreadIds down to only those 50 pinged ids. Mappings of events that were announced but not recently pinged are deleted. That covers far-future scheduled events, flash masses, and events cancelled before the 1h mark. Those events then stop receiving roster/signup-card refreshes (checkEventRosterSync iterates eventThreadIds), are never closed when they end, and thread commands stop resolving. The related signup/parent/revision maps are not pruned, so they leak. (b) parse_event_revision_ids sorts ids ascending and truncate(200), so the newest ids are dropped. The backend also omits missing ids. checkClosedEvents treats 'id absent from revisions' as 'event deleted': it calls closeEventThread and forgetEventThread. Once more than 200 mappings are tracked, the bot closes and forgets the live threads of the newest events.
findings.fix: Prune by event terminal state (stopped/cancelled/archived and older than N days), never by the pinged list. Make revisions chunk ids client-side at <=200 per request, or better have the backend return explicit {id, deleted:true} rows so absence is never read as deletion. Longer term, store bindings in the backend.
findings.verify_note: (a) is a real, certain bug. Once pinged1hEvents exceeds 50, every ping run filters eventThreadIds down to those ids (poller.ts:2007-2015). That drops mappings of announced future or flash events, so they lose roster/card sync and close handling, and thread commands stop resolving (findEventIdForThread, poller.ts:1419). The 1h ping partly self-heals through a thread-by-name lookup (poller.ts:1975-1980), but sync and close do not. (b) is real but latent: ids are sorted ascending and truncated to 200 (events/router.rs:497-498), and missing ids are treated as deleted (poller.ts:1489-1498). It needs more than 200 live mappings, which the (a) pruning makes unlikely, but the effect is destructive.

findings.title: PollerManager.ensure has a check-then-await race that creates duplicate Pollers for one guild
findings.description: ensure() checks getPoller(guildId), then awaits isRegisteredTenant (an HTTP call), then creates, registers and starts a Poller, with no re-check after the await. The `reconciling` flag guards only reconcile() against itself. GuildCreate calls ensure() directly (index.ts:213). At startup GuildCreate fires for every guild and ClientReady then runs reconcile() immediately. Both can pass the guard while the status call is in flight. registerPoller() replaces the map entry, but the first Poller keeps its setInterval, is unreachable and is never stopped. Both load the same state file into separate in-memory objects, so each announces new events, and each save() overwrites the other's checkpoints. The comment in reconcile() claims the overlap is prevented.
findings.fix: Track in-flight starts in a Map<guildId, Promise<void>> and make ensure() idempotent: re-check getPoller() after the await, or register a placeholder before awaiting. Have registerPoller stop any previous poller it replaces.
findings.verify_note: ensure() checks getPoller, awaits isRegisteredTenant, then creates and registers with no re-check (poller-manager.ts:108-122). registerPoller just overwrites the map entry without stopping the old poller (poller.ts:2228-2230). GuildCreate (index.ts:212-215) and ClientReady reconcile (index.ts:305-307) can overlap for the last-arriving guilds, giving two live setIntervals on the same state file. The window is narrow (HTTP latency at startup) but the result is permanent until restart. Downgraded from high on likelihood.

findings.title: Backend-to-Discord signals that should exist have no consumer; DM notifications queue up as 'pending' forever
findings.description: The backend's notify() inserts rows with discord_dm_status='pending' for broadcast and warn_issued kinds. The notifications router exposes only inbox, read and broadcast routes, and nothing in the bot or the backend ever reads or sends them. A warn issued from the website therefore sends no DM. The Discord /warn command DMs by itself in the bot (warn.ts:107), which is a parity gap and duplicated logic. The poller is the only inbound channel and it covers only events, battles, giveaways, applications status, splits and VOD. Bank/balance requests, warns, regear, trials, rank/XP changes, role changes and alliance-level broadcasts have no Discord delivery path.
findings.fix: Put DMs and channel posts on the same outbox as everything else (kind=dm, target discord_id). The bot claims them with a lease, sends, acks sent/failed(reason). Remove the bot-side DM from /warn so web and Discord share one path. Alternatively the backend, which already holds the bot token (albion/discord_guild_role.rs, discord_nick.rs), sends DMs itself.
findings.verify_note: insert_many marks warn_issued and broadcast rows discord_dm_status='pending' (notifications/service.rs:251-267, status.rs:57-62). A repo-wide grep finds no reader or sender of discord_dm_status outside tests and entities. The notifications router has no bot route (router.rs:49-53). Warns from the web therefore never DM. The Discord /warn sends its own DM in the bot (warn.ts:95-112), so the logic is duplicated and the web and Discord paths differ.

findings.title: Event lifecycle policy (auto mass/start, voice-empty auto-stop, undo window) is owned by the bot, so it fails when the bot is down and diverges from the web
findings.description: The scheduled->live transition at start time is triggered only by the poller calling POST api/events/{id}/start. If the bot is down, misconfigured, or the guild is an alliance tenant (the backend event_sessions worker does not start for alliance tenants, tenant.rs:84-86), scheduled events never start and never auto-stop. The backend does have an auto-stop-by-deadline worker, so there are two competing stop policies: backend deadline vs bot empty-voice. The 30s flash undo window is enforced only in the bot (FLASH_UNDO_WINDOW_MS, the button handler and flashUndoTimeRemaining), so a web user can cancel at any time and the web UI has no matching rule. Mass/start/stop messages and voice provisioning are coupled in one function, so the web 'Start' button does not create the voice channel or post the start message until the bot's lifecycle notices.
findings.fix: Backend owns state transitions and timing for every tenant kind. Add scheduler steps to the existing worker. The bot only reacts to outbox items (create voice channel, post mass/start message), reports voice occupancy as a signal (or the backend reads it via the bot-reported heartbeat), and acks.
findings.verify_note: Scheduled->live is triggered only by the bot calling /start (poller.ts:1738-1747, event-lifecycle.ts:97-101). The backend worker only auto-stops by deadline (auto_stop.rs) and does no start or mass. FLASH_UNDO_WINDOW_MS and the 30s rule live only in the bot (poller.ts:164, button.ts:493). Voice-empty auto-stop in the bot competes with the backend deadline stop. Correction: the claim that alliance tenants never start is overstated, because the bot's PollerManager runs a poller for alliance tenants too (no kind check), so the bot would start them if its poller worked. In practice the alliance poller probably never initializes (see bot-arch-10). The 'logic outside backend' point is valid, but this is a design gap more than a breakage.

findings.title: Alliance sync stops at the database: the Discord side is a per-guild poller with no tenant-kind awareness and a second delivery path
findings.description: The backend fanout outbox and mirror retry copy alliance events into member-guild tenant schemas. Discord propagation then depends on each member guild's own 60s poller discovering a new id, with no delivery acknowledgement back to the fanout job. The Poller class is never told whether its tenant is a guild or an alliance (kind is only known to tenant-gate and command-gate). An alliance Discord therefore also runs battles, splits, VOD, applications and giveaways checks, and battles fail on every tick because scoped_battles needs an Albion guild scope that alliance tenants do not have. Guild events are also pushed into the alliance Discord by a separate cross-tenant path (postAllianceAnnouncement posts into alliance_discord_channel_id from the member guild's poller, using the member bot's permissions in a different guild). The mirror copy in the alliance tenant is announced by the alliance tenant's own poller as well. So the same event can be delivered twice through two mechanisms. Events are the only entity that is synchronised. Splits, giveaways, battles, XP, rank, warns and roles have no alliance-wide Discord propagation. Alliance Discord blocks every command except 8 (ALLIANCE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS), including event creation.
findings.fix: Give each tenant a kind-aware delivery profile from the backend (which outbox kinds apply). Emit outbox items for fanout targets in the same transaction as the fanout target creation, and mark fanout_outbox targets complete only on bot ack, so alliance state is end-to-end observable. Pick one delivery path per alliance event (see question 2).
findings.verify_note: The core point holds. Fanout and mirror retry stop at the DB (fanout_worker.rs:20-45). Poller and PollerManager have no tenant-kind awareness (no kind handling in poller.ts apart from event_kind). ALLIANCE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS has exactly 8 entries and excludes event-create (command-gate.ts:22-31). Correction that makes it worse: alliance tenants have albion_guild_id=None (platform/service.rs:321), so scoped_battles fails with NotConfigured (battles/router.rs:222-231, albion_scope.rs:46-51). In adoptCheckpointBaseline, Promise.all rejects (poller.ts:648-668), so the alliance poller never sets initialized=true. It stays silent forever, and no event, giveaway or split sync runs there. That makes the 'same event delivered twice via two mechanisms' claim doubtful. The alliance-tenant poller likely never announces the mirror copy, so the only alliance-Discord delivery is the member bot's cross-guild postAllianceAnnouncement.

findings.title: Discord delivery failures are invisible to admins and the web; ambiguous items are dropped permanently
findings.description: Misconfigured routes, missing permissions, a deleted channel and Discord errors are recorded only in console.warn and in pendingAnnounces inside the local state file. There is no backend-visible status, so the web cannot show 'not announced because no flash channel is configured' and an admin cannot retry. Failed entries retry every 60s forever with attempts counted but no backoff or cap. Entries marked 'ambiguous' (forum create threw) and VOD 'attempted' are never retried and never surfaced, so the event is silently never announced. Calendar failures are reported only to the manual /event-calendar-refresh command. Users get a raw err.message ('fetch failed' for network errors) from the generic catch in index.ts.
findings.fix: Persist a delivery record per (entity, target) in the backend with state pending/sent/failed/ambiguous, last_error, attempts and next_attempt_at. Expose it in event detail and the admin Discord settings page. Add exponential backoff. Give ambiguous items a 'verify then retry' action that looks for an existing thread by name or event id.
findings.verify_note: Failures only go to console.warn and local pendingAnnounces (poller.ts:913-925). 'ambiguous' entries are skipped in retry loops (poller.ts:836-838, 904), and VOD 'attempted' is never retried. 'failed' entries retry every tick with an attempts counter but no backoff or cap. No backend-visible delivery state exists. The generic catch in index.ts surfaces raw err.message.

findings.title: Discord /event-create cannot express what the web can, and the Discord surface differs by tenant kind
findings.description: The backend CreateEventRequest has ping_alliance, discord_delivery, create_split, island_tab_id, vod_forum_post_enabled, regear, mass/start times and discord_role_ids. The bot's slash command sends only title, date, comp id, description and call_to_arms, and its CreateEventRequest type does not even declare ping_alliance, create_split, island_tab_id, vod_forum_post_enabled or discord_delivery. The bot also has no event edit or archive command, although UpdateEventRequest exists. The alliance capability matrix is a hard-coded set in the bot, unrelated to whatever the web uses, so the two surfaces cannot stay in step. The date option is a raw ISO string. Commands are registered identically on alliance and guild servers, so alliance members see commands that always answer 'Guild Discord only'.
findings.fix: Expose a backend capability/schema endpoint (GET /api/tenants/{id}/capabilities and OpenAPI-derived option schemas) and generate the slash-command definitions per tenant kind from it. Add the missing options through a shared modal, as /flash already does.
findings.verify_note: /event-create exposes only title, date (raw ISO string), comp_id, description and call_to_arms (event-create.ts:7-36). The bot CreateEventRequest type lacks ping_alliance, create_split, island_tab_id, vod_forum_post_enabled and discord_delivery (types.ts:356-369), while the backend model has them (events/models.rs:580-633). The commands directory has no event edit or archive command. The alliance allowlist is a hard-coded bot-side set.

findings.title: Business rules duplicated in the bot (split pool maths, message-XP gating, alliance allowlist, thread mapping)
findings.description: pendingSplitPool re-implements calculate_net_value ('matches calculate_net_value') and will drift when fee rules change. MessageXpGate re-implements the backend's cooldown, min-length and channel deny-list checks from a cached copy of api/progression/settings. When a setting changes, there is up to a 60s window of wrong local decisions. The alliance command allowlist is code in the bot. Guild attribution for alliance joins (zero/one/many guilds) is orchestrated across three bot files. Several responsibilities are split across bot and backend with no contract: the permission check endpoint returns booleans the bot re-validates (typeof checks), and the roles claim is derived in the bot.
findings.fix: Have the backend return the computed values (net pool, can_manage, allowed_commands, join_options) and let the bot render them. Delete the local copies. For message XP, drop the gate and use a batched ingest endpoint (see bot-arch-17).
findings.verify_note: pendingSplitPool does duplicate the net-value maths (split-summary.ts:46-60). MessageXpGate does duplicate the cooldown, min-length and deny-list checks locally from cached settings (message-xp-gate.ts:34-62). The gate is a deliberate perf optimization that fails open, and the backend still enforces the rules. The drift risk is small and bounded to the 60s cache. Overstated as a medium item.

findings.title: One long sequential poll per guild: one slow or failing step delays everything, and pollNow() silently no-ops
findings.description: poll() awaits about 12 steps in order, several of which loop over every event, thread or giveaway with HTTP and Discord calls. A slow Discord call in checkEventLifecycle delays battle and split sync, and a long cycle eats the tick (setInterval keeps firing but the `polling` guard drops it). pollNow(), used by /event-create, /flash, flash undo and all thread actions to make announcements 'instant', calls poll() which returns immediately if a poll is already running. The event just created is then not announced until the next 60s tick, and the command has already told the user it will appear shortly. ApiClient.request uses fetch with no AbortSignal, so a hung backend connection stalls a guild's poller for undici's default timeout (about 5 min) with polling=true. There is no retry/backoff and no 429 handling for the backend.
findings.fix: Split into independent loops or per-concern tasks with their own timers and error isolation. Make pollNow() queue a follow-up run when one is in flight. Add AbortSignal.timeout (about 10s) and bounded retry with jitter to ApiClient. Longer term, replace polling with outbox push (bot-arch-21), which also makes 'instant' the default.
findings.verify_note: poll() returns immediately if polling is true, so pollNow() silently no-ops while a poll runs (poller.ts:476-479, 472-474). Callers are event-create.ts:112, button.ts:503, modal.ts:161 and event-thread-command.ts:104. The poll is a long sequential chain of about 12 steps (poller.ts:487-504). ApiClient.request calls fetch with no AbortSignal or timeout and has no retry or 429 handling (client.ts:88-103).

findings.title: Slash commands round-trip the backend before deferring, risking Discord's 3s interaction timeout; the error path can double-reply
findings.description: executeSlashCommand does requireRegisteredTenant (cached 60s, else an HTTP call) and then isWebsiteUserRegistered, an uncached GET api/users/me on every invocation, and only then runs command.execute, which is where deferReply happens. With a slow backend (the owner reports slowness) the 3s window expires and Discord shows 'application did not respond'. The catch block in index.ts then calls interaction.reply or followUp on an expired interaction, which throws again inside the event listener (only logged as an unhandled rejection). The same pattern exists for buttons and selects, where the registration check is done in the join flow after deferReply but other handlers call the API before deferring. The web account check is a separate round trip that could be folded into the first authorised call.
findings.fix: deferReply first in the dispatcher (ephemeral by default), then do gate checks and editReply. Cache the website-registration answer per Discord id for a short TTL, or let the backend return 401-with-reason on the real call and map it, with no pre-flight. Wrap error replies in a safe-reply helper that swallows 10062/40060.
findings.verify_note: executeSlashCommand runs requireRegisteredTenant (cached 60s), then an uncached GET api/users/me via isWebsiteUserRegistered, and only then command.execute, where deferReply happens (command-gate.ts:47-87, website-account.ts:24-36). A slow backend can exceed the 3s interaction window. The index.ts catch then calls reply/followUp on a possibly expired interaction without protection (index.ts:121-140). It only bites when the backend is slow, but the owner reports slowness.

findings.title: Event calendar panel is maintained even when delivery is 'message' or 'forum'
findings.description: performEventCalendarSync derives configuredChannelIds from the routes regardless of delivery mode. Inside the per-event loop it skips every event when eventDelivery() !== 'calendar', so for message or forum guilds the per-channel event list is empty, but the loop over configured channels still builds payloads and sends or edits a calendar page (an empty calendar) in the events and flash channels. The delivery check is inside the event loop, so it also never short-circuits the Discord fetches. In calendar mode it also fetches every saved calendar message on every tick just to detect manual deletion, an extra Discord GET per page per minute per guild.
findings.fix: Check delivery once at the top of performEventCalendarSync and return early (and remove stale panels once on a mode change). Detect deletion through the message delete event or on edit failure instead of a fetch per tick.
findings.verify_note: calendarChannelIds(routes) returns the events and flash channels regardless of delivery mode (event-channels.ts:43-45). performEventCalendarSync skips every event when delivery != calendar, inside the loop (poller.ts:1228-1232). The channel loop still runs and sends or edits panels with an empty event list (poller.ts:1243-1275). The fetch-per-page-per-tick for deletion detection is also real (poller.ts:1283-1292). The result is an empty calendar panel posted in message or forum mode.

findings.title: Split sync stops at the first failing split (head-of-line blocking) and does an N+1 per tick; cursor is local
findings.description: checkSplitSync processes the batch in cursor order and does `if (!await adapter.sync(item)) return;` on the first failure. A permanently failing split (deleted tag, missing forum permission, thread locked) blocks every later split forever and is retried on every tick. For each discovered split it makes a second GET api/splits/{id}/discord-sync, an N+1. The (updated_at,id) cursor is stored in the local file, not the backend, so state loss re-syncs or skips splits. Roster sync additionally issues one GET per split of each changed event.
findings.fix: Track per-split state in the backend (the contract already stores thread_id). Mark a split 'blocked: reason' after N failures and continue. Return the full payload in the discovery batch to avoid the N+1. Keep the cursor server-side.
findings.verify_note: checkSplitSync returns on the first failed adapter.sync (poller.ts:1930), so one permanently failing split blocks all later ones and is retried every tick. Each split costs a second GET api/splits/{id}/discord-sync (poller.ts:1928-1929, an N+1). The (updated_at,id) cursor is local state (poller.ts:119-120). The thread_id binding is already backend-stored, as the finding itself notes.

findings.title: Unbounded state growth with a synchronous full-file rewrite on every mutation
findings.description: massedEvents, postedGiveawayIds, announcedGiveawayDraws, archivedEventIds, eventParentMessageIds, eventSignupMessageIds and eventSignupRevisions are append-only. Only pinged1hEvents is trimmed, and that trim is the destructive one in bot-arch-6. save() runs after almost every mutation (tens of times per poll) and does JSON.stringify(state, null, 2) plus writeFileSync on the shared event loop. Latency for interaction handling, XP awards and every other guild's poller grows with the size of each guild's state. Membership checks like massedEvents.includes are O(n) per event per tick.
findings.fix: Remove local state (bot-arch-1). If any is kept, debounce saves (coalesce per tick), use a Set or Map, and prune on terminal event state with a retention window.
findings.verify_note: The append-only arrays (massedEvents, postedGiveawayIds and others) are real, and saveState does a full pretty-printed writeFileSync on each save. In practice the state stays a few KB to tens of KB, so this is not a measurable latency problem. The real harm of the one pruning is the destructive trim in bot-arch-6. Overstated as a perf item.

findings.title: Message XP: one backend call per message with unbounded concurrency and an unbounded per-user map
findings.description: Each non-bot message spawns a fire-and-forget async job doing the tenant check, a settings check and a POST api/progression/award/message, with no queue or concurrency cap. Several messages from one user inside the same second all pass the gate, since lastAwardedAt is only updated after the response, so they all reach the backend. The lastAwardedAt Map is never evicted (one entry per user ever awarded). A chat burst becomes a burst of parallel backend writes, in a setup where the owner reports the backend is slow.
findings.fix: Batch locally (per guild, per user, flush every N seconds) into POST api/progression/award/messages, or move the entire policy to the backend with the bot only forwarding message counts. Bound the map with a TTL.
findings.verify_note: Each message spawns a fire-and-forget job (index.ts:261-298). lastAwardedAt is set only after the response and the Map is never evicted (message-xp-gate.ts:97-124). Bursts within the same second from one user all reach the backend. The backend enforces the cooldown and returns 'skipped' without writing, so 'parallel backend writes' is overstated. Minor.

findings.title: Process-global GUILD_NAME and per-event embed branding used for every tenant
findings.description: GUILD_NAME (default 'Weaklings') is read once from env and used for embed footers and, in buildBattleEmbed(battle, GUILD_NAME), to decide win or loss in battle reports for every tenant. A second guild's battle posts are labelled and scored against the wrong guild name. Separately, GuildMemberAdd adopts an alliance link via a GET (api/albion/link/me) with a side effect. Adoption happens only at join time: members who already sit in the alliance Discord, and members who link on their home guild later, are not backfilled until they run /register or /me. Registration of slash commands also happens twice at startup (GuildCreate and ClientReady) for every guild, including non-tenant guilds.
findings.fix: Resolve the guild name per tenant from the tenant status/settings (already fetched in fetchTenantStatus) and pass it into embed builders. Make link adoption a backend event (outbox 'member_linked' fans out to the alliance tenant and role assignment) rather than a bot GET on join. Register commands once per guild on ready only, and register by tenant kind.
findings.verify_note: buildBattleEmbed(battle, GUILD_NAME) matches guildSide by name against the process-global env value (poller.ts:2050, embeds/battle.embed.ts:35-37, theme.ts:13). Every tenant whose Albion guild is not named 'Weaklings' gets every battle rendered as DEFEAT with the wrong branding. That is a user-visible multi-tenant bug, more than low. The double command registration at startup (GuildCreate at index.ts:209 plus ClientReady at index.ts:298-302) is also real. The GuildMemberAdd adoption backfill point was not verified in depth.

findings.title: Target architecture: backend outbox + push stream to a stateless bot, with bindings and delivery status stored in the backend
findings.description: The backend already contains the needed patterns: a leased, retryable control-plane outbox (fanout_outbox.rs: ClaimedTarget with lease_token, attempts, state pending/processing/complete/failed), a 15s retry worker, a 30s per-tenant worker, a roster websocket hub, and a Discord-REST-capable bot token for roles and nicks. Proposal: (1) Add a control-plane table discord_outbox(id bigserial, tenant_id, kind, entity_type, entity_id, revision, payload jsonb, created_at, available_at, lease_token, leased_until, attempts, state, last_error), written in the SAME transaction as the domain change by EventService (create, update, roster bump, status change, archive/restore), GiveawayService (create/draw), battle_sync (new battle), applications (status), splits, notifications (DM), alliance fanout (one row per target tenant). The fanout worker's per-target job also creates outbox rows for each member guild. (2) Add a discord_bindings table (tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, channel_id, message_id, thread_id, signup_message_id, revision, state) replacing the whole JSON checkpoint (the split sync contract already works this way). (3) Expose bot-only endpoints under /api/bot: GET /outbox/stream (SSE or websocket, one connection for all tenants, resumable via Last-Event-ID = outbox id, tenant filter = guilds the bot is in) with a poll fallback GET /outbox?after=..&limit=.., POST /outbox/{id}/ack {binding updates, discord ids}, POST /outbox/{id}/fail {retryable, reason}. Leases give exactly-one-active consumer, safe horizontal scaling and crash recovery. (4) Move scheduling (mass_due, start_due, reminder_1h, auto-stop) into the existing worker and emit these as outbox kinds, extended to alliance tenants (tenant.rs:84-86). (5) The bot becomes a thin executor: one reducer per kind (event.upsert: create thread + signup card or edit; event.close; giveaway.post; dm.send; split.upsert...). Thread->event lookups call GET /api/bot/bindings?thread_id=. The poller, JSON state, PollerManager reconcile, listSinceCheckpoint and the local gates all go away. The bot keeps the guild list only for gateway/interaction duty. (6) Delivery status is stored in the backend and shown in the web event page and the admin Discord settings page. (7) Commands and buttons call the same backend actions the web calls and re-render from the response; the resulting outbox row refreshes the card for everyone, with no local message.edit (button.ts:583-584 and 709-710 currently edit the clicked message on their own, parallel to the poller's refresh).
findings.fix: Phase 1: add the discord_bindings table and ack endpoints and migrate events from the JSON file. Phase 2: add the outbox and stream for events and battles/giveaways, and remove listSinceCheckpoint. Phase 3: move scheduling and DMs. Phase 4: delete the Poller.
findings.verify_note: This is a design proposal, not a defect. The cited backend patterns do exist: a leased fanout_outbox with lease_token and attempts (fanout_outbox.rs:37-51, 142-162), a 15s retry worker (fanout_worker.rs:20), a 30s event-sessions worker, a roster hub, and button.ts message.edit calls parallel to the poller's refresh (button.ts:583-584). The proposal is sound and consistent with the confirmed findings, but it is a recommendation with no defect to confirm, and it is a large scope.

logic_questions: Event announcement during downtime: when a tenant is first onboarded or the bot's state is lost (initialized=false), the current code reseeds cursors and swallows everything created in the gap. Should a catch-up be sent instead, either all unannounced scheduled events or only those starting in the future? Today scheduled future events created while the bot was down are never announced.

Alliance Discord double delivery: a guild event with ping_alliance is posted in the alliance channel by the member guild's poller (cross-tenant, with alliance roles), and its mirror copy in the alliance tenant is announced again by the alliance tenant's own poller (thread, signup card, calendar). Is that intended (ping message plus workspace copy), or should one path exist? If one, which one?

Who owns scheduled lifecycle: should scheduled->live (and mass/voice creation) happen at the scheduled time even when no bot is online, or when the event is in an alliance tenant? Today only the bot does it. Should the backend auto-start, with the bot reacting to the state change?

Should alliance Discords offer the same actions as guild Discords (create/edit events, flash, splits, giveaways, bank), or only the 8 allowlisted commands? Should the alliance event creation flow be available from Discord, and who may publish to member guilds?

Which things must the alliance sync to member guild Discords beyond events: splits, giveaways, battles, announcements, rank/XP, warns, roles? Should alliance-level giveaways and broadcasts appear in each member guild's channels, and should member guild activity (battles, XP) appear in the alliance Discord?

Delivery failure policy: for 'ambiguous' Discord creates (the call threw but the thread may exist), should the system auto-verify and retry, require an admin click, or stay dropped? Should admins see a per-event Discord delivery status in the web UI?
Calendar panel: should it exist only for 'calendar' delivery guilds, or always (the current code keeps one even for message/forum delivery)?

Notifications: which backend notification kinds are meant to be DMed (broadcast, warn_issued, etc.)? Should DM delivery be done by the bot or by the backend using its existing bot token, and should members be able to opt out?

Expected scale: how many tenant Discords per bot process and is horizontal scaling or sharding planned? That decides whether SSE/websocket with a lease, or a plain cursor-paged outbox poll, is enough.
Message XP: is per-message award latency important, or can message activity be batched (for example every 10-30s) per guild? Should the bot keep any local anti-spam gate?

Battle announcements: should every new battle above the min_players threshold be posted, and for alliance tenants should battles be posted per member guild or combined? What should happen with the backlog when the battles channel is first configured?

summary:
AREA: parity matrix web vs Discord vs backend (read-only static audit; client-call extraction was regex-based, so "unused" means no literal URL found, dynamic URLs were spot-checked).

HOW IT WORKS: Backend mounts ~33 module routers under /api (apps/backend/src/modules/mod.rs:46-80) plus /api/platform, /api/tenants (public) and /api/alliances (lib.rs:139-142; platform/public.rs:34-67). The web talks through ApiService (core/services/api.service.ts), which unwraps the {status,data} envelope and returns T. The bot talks through ApiClient (discord-bot/src/api/client.ts) with X-Bot-Secret plus optional X-Discord-Id, X-Guild-Id and X-Discord-Role-Ids. A bot request without X-Discord-Id becomes "bot_system" with Admin and super-admin (auth/rbac.rs:290-304). With X-Discord-Id the actor's permissions come from live Discord role ids (rbac.rs:329, 488), whereas a web session uses stored roles. Poller-driven sync is bot-side: events, calendar, revisions, VOD forum posts, giveaways and split forum threads via /splits/*/discord-sync. Alliance tenants are gated differently per client: the web uses the nav flag hiddenForAlliance and guildOnlyGuard (layout/nav.ts, auth.guard.ts:110-118); the bot uses ALLIANCE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS (services/command-gate.ts:22-31).

BROKEN CLIENT CALLS: 2 confirmed. (a) Web PUT /api/splits/{id} does not exist (event-detail.ts:5153, 5167). (b) Web participation-guilds reads response.data after the envelope was already unwrapped (event-detail.ts:5520). No broken bot routes found by static match; all 64 literal bot URLs map to a backend route.

findings.title: Web alliance event signup is always blocked: participation-guilds response unwrapped twice
findings.description: Backend returns {status,data:[guilds]}. ApiService.get already maps to r.data, so the page receives the bare array. loadParticipationGuilds then types it as ParticipationGuildListResponse and reads response.data ?? [], and an array has no .data, so guilds is always []. In an alliance tenant guildChoiceBlocked is then true (participationGuilds().length === 0) and the template shows the 'join_guild_none' error for every user. The spec masks it because it mocks api.get to return {data:[...]}, which the real service never emits. The bot treats the same endpoint as a bare array and works. Net result: on web, nobody can join an alliance event, the core alliance sync scenario, while Discord can.
findings.fix: Type the call as api.get<ParticipationGuildOption[]>, use the array directly, delete ParticipationGuildListResponse, and fix the spec mocks to return arrays. Add a test that goes through the real ApiService envelope.
findings.verify_note: ApiService.get maps r.data (api.service.ts:55). Backend returns ApiResponse<Vec<ParticipationGuild>> (router.rs:1616-1636), so the page gets a bare array. event-detail.ts:5515-5521 reads response.data ?? [] and gets []. In an alliance tenant guildChoiceBlocked (3430-3432) is then always true and the 'none' error shows (2090). The spec mocks {data:[...]} (event-detail.spec.ts:716-720), which the real service never emits. The bot types it as a bare array. Real defect. I rate it high rather than critical: it only affects web signup on alliance tenants, and Discord signup works.

findings.title: Web 'link split to event' / 'unlink split' calls PUT /api/splits/{id}, which does not exist
findings.description: The split route /{id} is registered with get/patch/delete only. The web sends PUT {event_id}, so axum answers 405 and the toast shows an error. The backend update_split (PATCH) does support event_id: Option<Option<i64>> and syncs participants. Attaching or detaching an existing split from the event page therefore never works. Only the create_split-at-event-creation path works.
findings.fix: Change both calls to api.patch(`api/splits/${id}`, {event_id}). Add a frontend test asserting the HTTP method, or add a contract test that checks client paths and methods against the OpenAPI document.
findings.verify_note: event-detail.ts:5153 and 5167 call api.put('api/splits/{id}'), and ApiService has a put method. The splits router registers /{id} with get().patch().delete() only (router.rs:113-116), so PUT returns 405. update_split (PATCH) accepts event_id as Option<Option<i64>> (models.rs:218-223). Linking and unlinking a split from the event page is broken.

findings.title: Alliance Discord hub cannot create, start, stop, cancel or roster events; thread commands are rejected; alliance events get no auto-stop worker
findings.description: ALLIANCE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS contains only register, balance, balance-request, events, event-join, event-leave, me and player. event-create, event-start, event-stop, event-roster, flash, build and the thread commands (/join /leave /ping /start /stop /reopen /cancel in event-thread-actions.ts) all answer 'only available on a guild Discord'.
