The alliance-operations plan (AC: an officer creates an alliance event) and the comment on the allowlist itself ('event list/join/leave') conflict with this. In an alliance announcement thread the officer cannot run /start, /stop or /cancel, and /join is blocked even though the Join button works because buttons are not gated. The web does allow event create and manage on alliance tenants (nav.ts:123, 'events' is not hiddenForAlliance). On the backend, starts_sync_workers('alliance') is false, so alliance-owned events never get event_sessions auto_stop or battle_linker. Web and Discord therefore behave differently for alliances, and an alliance event started from either client is never auto-stopped.
findings.fix: Decide the alliance model, then make one backend capability list per tenant kind (e.g. add allowed_commands/capabilities to GET /tenants/{id}/status) consumed by both web nav and bot gate. Add event-create/start/stop/roster and the thread commands to the alliance set, and run auto_stop (not battle_linker) for alliance tenants.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed in code. ALLIANCE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS (command-gate.ts:22-31) omits event-create, start, stop and roster. The thread commands go through executeSlashCommand (index.ts:122), so the same gate rejects them. starts_sync_workers('alliance') is false (tenant.rs:84-86), and ensure_sync_workers and the boot loop skip alliance tenants. event_sessions::spawn is the only place that runs auto_stop_expired_sessions and retry_pending_event_completion_xp, so alliance-owned events are never auto-stopped. That backend gap is the strongest part. The Discord allowlist reads as a deliberate product choice (guild-only comment), so I rate this medium. The plan's Slice 3 does say 'Discord event flow' for alliance events.

findings.title: Bot bank commands ignore alliance multi-guild ledgers; /balance-request and alliance accept/reject fail for multi-guild users
findings.description: On an alliance tenant the backend returns an aggregate BalanceSummary with guilds[] and requires guild_tenant_id for withdraw, accept and reject whenever the user has rows in more than one member guild (alliance.rs:205). The web passes guild_tenant_id everywhere. The bot never reads guilds[], so /balance shows only the aggregate; /balance-request and the bank:request_all button always send {all:true} and get a 400 'guild_tenant_id is required...'; the alliance accept/reject buttons send only transaction_ids. 'balance' and 'balance-request' are in the alliance allowlist, so the commands are advertised but break for exactly the users the alliance sync is meant to serve.
findings.fix: Bot: when the tenant is an alliance and guilds.length > 1, show a per-guild breakdown and a guild select before withdrawing, and send guild_tenant_id. Better, make the backend resolve the target per transaction id so no client has to pass it.
findings.verify_note: Partly confirmed. /balance and /balance-request send {all:true} with no guild_tenant_id (balance.ts, balance-request.ts, button.ts:1113-1128). Alliance withdraw uses resolve_target_guild, which returns 400 when the user has rows in more than one member guild (alliance.rs:185-206). That part is real. The accept/reject button claim is weak. The bank:accept and bank:reject buttons are generated by the audit service (audit/service.rs:340-347) and posted for the guild ledger, so they are normally clicked in a guild-tenant Discord and never hit the alliance path. Note also that resolve_target_guild matches on the caller's own bank rows, so an officer clicking in an alliance context would fail for a different reason. Impact is limited to multi-guild users running the bot bank commands on an alliance Discord. Medium.

findings.title: Alliance sync health endpoints (event mirror/fanout status and retry, split distribution status) have no web or Discord surface
findings.description: The owner reports that alliance sync does not work. The backend added GET /events/{id}/fanout-status, GET /events/{id}/mirror-status, POST /events/{id}/mirror-retry and GET /splits/{id}/distribution-status (per-guild recipient state, tx ids, last error), but neither the Angular app nor the bot calls any of them (no literal URL, no 'mirror' or 'distribution' in feature code). Failed mirrors, failed alliance split distributions and retries are therefore invisible and unactionable by officers; the only recourse is DB access. Related: the event page does not warn when a synchronized copy is stale.
findings.fix: Add a sync panel to event-detail and split-detail (status chips per guild, last error, Retry button on mirror-retry), plus a bot button or select on the alliance announcement for officers. Surface the same state in the alliance admin page.
findings.verify_note: The routes exist (events/router.rs:195-197, splits/router.rs:127-129). Grep over apps/frontend/src and apps/discord-bot/src finds no consumer for fanout-status, mirror-status, mirror-retry or distribution-status. The 'distribution' hits are unrelated battle fame charts. The observability gap is real. It is a missing UI for diagnostics, not a sync defect, so I rate it medium.

findings.title: Web re-implements event management authority client-side; bot uses the backend endpoint
findings.description: The backend exposes GET /events/{id}/management-authority returning {is_organizer, can_manage, required_permission}, which the bot calls. The web ignores it and recomputes canEdit/canDelete/canManageParticipants as (events.edit || created_by === userId) plus a source_event_id/is_synchronized_copy check. Any backend rule change (e.g. co-organizer, alliance-owned events, per-guild management for mirrored copies) will silently diverge, giving buttons that 403 or hidden buttons for allowed officers. canDelete also keys off events.delete while the archive endpoint enforces EventsDelete authority but start/cancel enforce EventsEdit.
findings.fix: Fetch management-authority in event-detail (or embed can_manage/can_delete in EventDetailView) and drive all manage buttons from it; remove the duplicated predicates.
findings.verify_note: The web does compute canEdit/canDelete client-side (event-detail.ts:3229-3248, 3464-3466) and never calls management-authority (no frontend hit). The current logic mirrors the backend: a copy gives false, otherwise the organizer or events.edit. The router's is_copy check comes from assert_manageable_source_event rather than the web's is_synchronized_copy flag, and I did not trace whether they always agree. I found no concrete divergence today. The canDelete vs EventsEdit mismatch is not shown to break anything, because delete/archive endpoints enforce EventsDelete (router.rs:1392+). This is a duplication risk, so low.

findings.title: Applications have no list endpoint or web UI; trials are created but can never be listed, ended or expired; role assignment after accept lives in the bot
findings.description: The applications router has only create, active, latest, reopen, accept, decline and close; there is no list or get-by-id route, so the web admin-applications page can only edit settings and cannot show pending applications. Review is Discord-ticket-only. accept with as_trial=true calls TrialService::start_from_accept, but the trials module exposes no HTTP router, nothing lists or ends trials, and no worker removes the trial role at ends_at (grep finds no consumer outside applications/router.rs). The backend only returns trial_role_discord_id and the bot calls applicant.roles.add (button.ts:326-327), so accepting through any non-bot client would not grant roles, and the trial role is never revoked.
findings.fix: Add GET /applications (filters by status) and GET/POST /trials (list, end, extend). Add a trial-expiry worker that ends trials and enqueues role removal through the same backend Discord-role path used by autorole. Move role assignment into the backend accept handler. Then add the web review page.
findings.verify_note: The applications router has no list or get route (router.rs:54-62). The trials module has no router, and its README says listing and manager actions are not implemented. Grep finds no trial worker or expiry consumer. Role add and remove after accept happens in the bot (button.ts:317-327). The web admin page only edits settings. All claims hold. These are missing features and a missing trial-expiry job rather than a broken sync path, so medium.

findings.title: Discord /event-create is a reduced, UTC-ISO form that diverges from the web create form
findings.description: Bot sends only title, comp_id, event_date_utc, description and call_to_arms. It cannot set mass time (backend silently defaults to start minus 30 min), player_cap, regear, ping_alliance, discord_role_ids, vod_forum_post_enabled or create_split with island_tab_id. Events created in Discord therefore cannot enable regear, so they never show up in regear self-service, and cannot ping the alliance Discord. It also requires the officer to type a UTC ISO string and a numeric comp id (no autocomplete), although the tenant stores discord_event_timezone. There is no Discord edit command to fix these afterwards. Same capability, different rules and defaults per client.
findings.fix: Replace the option list with a modal (like /flash) with autocompleted comp, local-time parsing done by the backend using discord_event_timezone, and toggles for regear, alliance ping and split. Even better, expose one POST /events/quick contract shared by both clients.
findings.verify_note: /event-create exposes only title, date (ISO), comp_id, description and call_to_arms (event-create.ts:9-84). The body omits mass_time, player_cap, regear, ping_alliance, roles and split. The web sends all of these (events.ts:911-925). The backend defaults mass to start minus 30 minutes (service.rs:271-274). Parity gap confirmed.

findings.title: Flash mass can only be created from Discord; web only renders it
findings.description: The backend supports event_kind='flash' (no comp, binary participation). The web CreateEventRequest builder never sets event_kind and always requires a comp, so officers on web cannot launch a flash mass, while Discord cannot launch a regular scheduled/regear/split event with all options (parity-8). Each client covers a different half of the event-create contract.
findings.fix: Add an Organized/Flash toggle to the web create dialog sending event_kind; keep flash fields (what, when, notes) consistent with the modal.
findings.verify_note: The web CreateEventRequest builder (events.ts:911-925) never sets event_kind and always requires a comp. The web only renders flash events (events.ts:179, 211). Flash creation exists only in the bot modal. Confirmed, but it is a feature gap in one direction and low impact.

findings.title: Bot resolves Discord user to internal user id with 3 round trips and a username-substring fallback
findings.description: Warn, unwarn and xp commands take a Discord user, but the backend contracts need a numeric user_id (IssueWarnRequest.user_id). The bot impersonates the target (GET users/me with the target's X-Discord-Id), then auth/me, then a username directory search. That is up to three extra requests per command, a rule only the bot has (exact username match, ignore ambiguous), and no equivalent for new clients. Targets who never logged into the web get 401 'no linked account' from the impersonation path and are reported as 'Account Not Found'. expiryFromDays is also computed client-side in the bot while the web sends a date.
findings.fix: Accept discord_id (or user_ref) in warns, progression adjust and similar officer endpoints and resolve it in the backend; take multiplier_days in IssueWarnRequest so both clients send the same thing.
findings.verify_note: resolveInternalUserId makes up to 3 requests (resolve-user.ts:10-48), and IssueWarnRequest needs a numeric user_id (warns/models.rs). The 'username-substring fallback' claim is wrong: the code requires an exact, unique case-insensitive match and comments explicitly against partial hits. The remaining issue is the extra round trips and logic living in the bot. Low.

findings.title: Member self-service gaps: split share donation, giveaway entry on web, VODs on web, regear on Discord
findings.description: POST /splits/{id}/donate is called by neither client (bank only renders a 'donated' status). Giveaway enter and leave exist only as a Discord button; web giveaways are admin-only routes behind giveaways.view, so a member cannot enter from the site. POST /vods is Discord-only and GET /vods/me is used by nobody. The bot has no regear commands at all (death list, request, self-service, officer accept/reject) although regear is a daily workflow, and no officer split commands (create, complete, add participants). Goal 2 (same capabilities in both clients) is not met for these flows.
findings.fix: Prioritise: regear request and approve in Discord (buttons on the audit message), member giveaway page on web, donate button in bank, VOD list on web, /split complete. Use the existing backend routes.
findings.verify_note: Grep finds no client call to splits donate, vods or vods/me. The only giveaway calls are admin-page create, list, draw, cancel and detail (no member enter/leave). The bot has no regear command (commands/ directory listing). Parity gaps confirmed. They are missing features rather than sync bugs, so medium.

findings.title: Officer workflows exist in only one client with no cross-link: roster seating, voice channel, remind, escalation ack, application panel
findings.description: Web-only: roster seats, swaps, auto-fill, roster roles, battle linking, escalation ack (warns.ts), bank deposits, siphoned, comps. Discord-only: remind (/ping), voice channel bind, flash, application review, tickets, application panel publish. The bot lists warn escalations with 'Open Action' but cannot acknowledge them, and the admin-applications page can set the channel but has no 'publish panel' action, so completing setup requires Discord /applications-panel gated by Discord ManageGuild instead of backend RBAC.
findings.fix: Add POST /warns/escalations/{id}/ack button in Discord, 'Remind' and 'Publish panel' actions in web (backend queues the Discord work for the bot), and gate /applications-panel by backend permission instead of ManageGuild.
findings.verify_note: The Discord-only vs web-only split is believable. The bot /applications-panel is gated by Discord ManageGuild (applications-panel.ts:13-17) and the web has no publish-panel action. I did not verify the escalation-ack claim in full. This is a feature gap with no demonstrated breakage, so low.

findings.title: Permissions differ by client: bot uses live Discord role ids, web uses stored roles
findings.description: Bot requests carry X-Discord-Role-Ids and permissions are derived by resolve_bot_role_ids from the claim, falling back to users.role; the web uses DB roles. When Discord roles and the DB drift (member_roles sync lag), the same officer can be allowed in Discord and denied on web or vice versa. Separately, any bot call without X-Discord-Id is treated as Admin 'bot_system', so poller-style calls and any command that forgets discordId (e.g. applications-panel api.put admin/settings) skip RBAC entirely.
findings.fix: Pick one source of truth: sync Discord roles into role assignments on a short schedule and on member update events, then ignore the header for authorisation. Require X-Discord-Id on all user-triggered bot calls and restrict bot_system to a route allowlist.
findings.verify_note: Real mechanics: bot role claims go through resolve_bot_role_ids, and a request with no X-Discord-Id becomes an Admin 'bot_system' (rbac.rs:290-304). applications-panel does call api.put('api/admin/settings') without a discordId (applications-panel.ts:31), so it uses bot_system. The bot_system path is intentional for poller calls and the secret is trusted. The drift scenario is hypothetical. This is a design observation, not a traced defect, so low.

findings.title: About 45 backend routes are used by neither client
findings.description: No literal client URL exists for: albionbb/* (5), albiondata/* (2), economy/* (3), fingerprints/* (4), fight-analytics, attention/findings, combat dataset, mastery-groups, calibration, item-power, member item-power and simulate, openalbion weapons, weapons stats, categories and items, albion/guilds/{id}, comps/builds/{id}/roster-fit, intel scouts/{id}/counters and scouts/backfill, regear/events/{id}/deaths, regear/admin/run-extraction, bank/guild/summary, vods/me, progression users/{id}/ledger, platform admins/reload, alliances GET members and decline, events PUT participants/{u}, retry-after-verification, and hard DELETE for events, comps, builds, splits and bank transactions. Some of these may be used by internal services or reached through utoipa docs; they still cost OpenAPI size, tests and maintenance, and some (economy, fight-analytics, bank guild summary, ledger) look like features meant for the UI that never got wired.
findings.fix: For each: wire it into a UI or bot command if it is part of the roadmap, otherwise delete the route and keep the service function. Start with economy, fight-analytics and attention, which look like finished analytics with no consumer.
findings.verify_note: Spot checks confirm no frontend or bot references for api/economy, api/fingerprints, fight-analytics, api/albionbb, api/albiondata, mastery-groups, item-power, roster-fit and vods/me. The '~45' count and the full list are not verified, and openalbion does have some use. Dead-code hygiene only, low.

findings.title: Alliance invite cannot be declined from the web or Discord
findings.description: The admin-alliance page calls accept, invite, leave and patch but never decline, and GET /alliances/{id}/members is not used either (membership comes from /alliances/me). An invited guild can only accept or ignore the invite, so stale 'invited' memberships pile up on the alliance side.
findings.fix: Add a Decline button next to Accept for invited guild tenants, using POST decline.
findings.verify_note: The backend has POST /alliances/{id}/members/{guild_id}/decline (platform/public.rs:58-61). admin-alliance.ts has no decline call. Confirmed low-impact UI gap.

findings.title: link_player and register_by_ign are copy-pasted handlers with the same side-effect sequence
findings.description: Both handlers repeat assert_register_allowed, create_link, sync_guild_nickname, load_albion_scope, assign_guild_role and after_successful_link. Web uses /link (by player id) and the bot uses /register (by IGN); any fix to link side effects (e.g. alliance fan-out) must be made twice, which already risks the web and Discord paths drifting.
findings.fix: Extract a single LinkOrchestrator::link(user, player) used by both handlers; keep /register as a thin resolver that finds the player id.
findings.verify_note: link_player (router.rs:295) has the shape described: assert_register_allowed, create_link, sync_guild_nickname, load_albion_scope, assign_guild_role, after_successful_link. I read only the first handler closely and did not diff register_by_ign. It is a duplication nit, not a defect. Low.

findings.title: Web: no unlink-by-bot and no alliance-aware tenant hints in Discord; unguarded giveaway detail route
findings.description: admin/giveaways has guildOnlyGuard but admin/giveaways/:giveawayId only has the permission guard, so an alliance tenant can deep-link into a guild-only page. The bot can link a character but not unlink while the web can, which forces users to open the site to fix a wrong link.
findings.fix: Add guildOnlyGuard to giveaway detail; add /unlink to the bot using DELETE /albion/link; centralise 'guild-only' route and nav lists from one tenant-kind capabilities map (see parity-3).
findings.verify_note: app.routes.ts:288-299 shows admin/giveaways has guildOnlyGuard and admin/giveaways/:giveawayId does not. The bot has no unlink command (no link-removal file in commands/). Both are minor. Low.

logic_questions: Alliance Discord hub: should alliance officers be able to create, start, stop and cancel alliance-owned events and run /join, /ping and /cancel inside event threads (as plans/alliance-operations.md says), or is the alliance Discord intentionally join-only with management on web? Options: (a) full management on both, (b) web-only management with join-only Discord, (c) management only on the owner guild Discord and alliance mirrors read-only.

Alliance bank: when a user has balances in several member guilds, should /balance-request send everything (all guilds in one step), prompt for a guild, or should the alliance hub not offer withdrawals at all (withdrawals only on the guild Discord, as plans/alliance-management.md Slice 10 says: no bank for alliance)? Currently the alliance allowlist exposes /balance and /balance-request while the plan says the alliance has no bank.

Applications and trials: is web review of applications wanted (needs a list endpoint), or is the Discord ticket the only intended surface? Who ends a trial (officer manually, automatic expiry with role removal, or both), and should expiry notify the officer?

Permissions source of truth: should an officer's rights in Discord come from live Discord roles (current bot behavior) or from backend-stored roles (current web behavior)? Which wins if they disagree?

Flash masses and regear: should events created from Discord (reduced form, no regear toggle) be editable only from the web, or should the Discord command reach feature parity with the web create form? Do alliance events need regear/split options at all?

Dead routes: for economy, fight-analytics, attention/findings, fingerprints, albionbb, albiondata, combat simulate/calibration/item-power and bank guild summary, which are planned UI features (keep and wire) and which can be removed?
Split donation (POST /splits/{id}/donate) and 'donated' bank status: is member self-donation a wanted feature? If yes, which client(s) should expose it?

Alliance sync visibility: should failed event mirrors and split distributions notify alliance officers automatically (Discord DM or channel post) or only show in a status panel on web with a manual retry?

summary:
The backend is a single Axum process. Each tenant (Discord server) gets its own SeaORM pool pinned to a `tenant_<id>` schema via `SET search_path` on connect (postgres.rs:109-117). `TenantRegistry` (tenant.rs) holds a DashMap of `TenantContext` entries (pool, role-permission cache, feature flags, kind). The context is loaded lazily on the first request for a tenant (running `Migrator::up` on load) and is dropped only by an explicit `evict()`. The `resolve_tenant` middleware picks the tenant from the session cookie, or from `X-Guild-Id` when `X-Bot-Secret` is valid, and injects pool/permissions/features as request extensions. There is no per-request schema switching: each tenant has its own pool, so the switching cost is paid as pool count instead. Nothing sets pool size or timeouts.

Background work:
- Per guild tenant, `event_sessions::spawn` (30s tick) and `battle_sync::spawn` (120s tick) run as detached `tokio::spawn` tasks.
- A global fanout loop (15s tick, alliance to guild event copies) plus a mirror retry loop (guild to alliance) run in `fanout_worker`.
- Workers poll AlbionBB (battle lists, battle detail, kills) and Albion Data (market prices) with no shared limiter. Only battle detail and guild info are cached (24h, 500 entries). Battle lists, kills and prices are uncached.
- Battle sync persists a huge JSON snapshot per battle (`guild_battle_snapshots.*_json`), then runs best-effort persistence for evidence, enemy identity, fingerprints, loss estimates and fight analytics. This also runs inline when a user opens a battle.

Per request, auth does a lot (rbac.rs:116-155):
- It decrypts the cookie and does a tenant DB lookup for the user id.
- It runs a control-plane `get_tenant` join to check ownership.
- It calls the Discord REST API for guild member roles, cached for 60 seconds only on success.
- It reloads all `roles` rows and may write `users.role`.

Combat and OpenAlbion JSON are `include_str!` plus `OnceLock`, so they are parsed once (fine). There is no `spawn_blocking` anywhere, no compression, timeout or concurrency layer, and no body limit. Many list endpoints load whole tables and paginate in memory (fights, alliance bank, battles, guild report). Alliance synchronization is a set of serial control-plane workers that deep-copy comp graphs row by row.

The largest costs are:
- A cache that never hits (`BattlesService::for_scope`).
- Page walks against AlbionBB.
- Per-request Discord and DB round trips in the auth extractor.
- Pool and migration churn on `evict`.
- Fights, reports and alliance bank loading whole tables.

Several services are large (events/service.rs has about 5000 lines of production code in one `impl`), with helpers duplicated across modules.

findings.title: BattlesService::for_scope builds a fresh empty catalog cache per request, so the 60s battle-list cache never hits
findings.description: Every `/api/battles` handler calls `scoped_battles`, which calls `service.for_scope(&scope)`. That calls `Self::new(...)`, which allocates a brand-new `catalog_cache: Arc<RwLock<HashMap>>` (line 93). The `catalog_cache` read in `guild_catalog` (line 127) therefore always misses. Each list request walks up to `GUILD_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES = 20` AlbionBB pages serially and uncached (the loop at line 151; `AlbionBbService::get_battles` is explicitly uncached), then `hydrate_page` does a serial `get_battle` for each item on the page. `battle_sync::spawn` does the same with `BattlesService::new` every 120s tick per guild tenant, via `list_guild_battles(page 1, limit 50)`. Result: up to 20 serial HTTP calls (60s timeout each) per page view and per tenant per tick. This is likely a main source of 'the app is slow', and it stacks across tenants with no limiter. The doc comment at lines 98-99 shows the cache was meant to be tenant-scoped, but it is never persisted anywhere.
findings.fix: Hold the catalog cache in the shared `AlbionBbService`, or in a process-wide cache keyed by (server, guild_id, min_players), with a TTL, singleflight (an in-flight map of futures) and a bound. Make `for_scope` clone the shared handle instead of creating a new cache. Add an upstream concurrency limiter (a Semaphore in `AlbionBbApiClient`). Fetch pages concurrently (bounded), and stop paging early when the oldest battle on a page falls outside the window the caller needs. Have battle_sync read only page 1.
findings.verify_note: for_scope calls Self::new, which allocates a fresh catalog_cache (battles/service.rs:93,100-108). guild_catalog's cache read therefore always misses. It loops up to GUILD_CATALOG_MAX_PAGES=20 uncached get_battles pages (service.rs:151; albionbb/service.rs:43-50 is explicitly uncached), then hydrate_page does a serial get_battle per item. get_battle is cached for 24h, so only cold battles cost an upstream call. battle_sync.rs:56-62 builds a new BattlesService each tick and run_cycle calls list_guild_battles, so each tenant pays the 20-page walk every 120s. Real and traced. Severity is high rather than critical: it is slow rather than broken.

findings.title: Event battle linker walks up to 100 AlbionBB pages per pending event every 30s tick
findings.description: `link_battles_for_event` pages `get_battles` (uncached) from page 1 until an empty page or a page with no new ids, capped at `MAX_BATTLE_PAGES = 100`. The listing is filtered only by guild, not by time, so the loop never stops early on the event window. It effectively scans the guild's whole recent history, then discards battles outside `[started_at, window_end]` (lines 4311-4318). `refresh_pending_links` runs this for every event whose `link_status` is pending or in_progress, on a 30s ticker per guild tenant, for up to the post-stop grace period (~30+ minutes). N pending events x up to 100 serial calls per tick, repeated each tick. The upstream rate limit (429) is not handled, so this feeds spurious `UpstreamService` errors and 'linking never completes'.
findings.fix: Stop paging once a page's oldest `start_time` is before `started_at_utc` (the AlbionBB list is newest-first). Fetch the guild's recent battle list once per tick per tenant (shared via the cache from backend-perf-1) and reuse it for every pending event instead of re-fetching per event. Add a minimum interval per event (use `link_attempts` for backoff) instead of a flat 30s.
findings.verify_note: link_battles_for_event (events/service.rs:4277-4302) pages get_battles with only guild_id and no time bound, stopping at an empty page, a page with no new ids, or 100 pages. It then filters by window at 4311-4318. refresh_pending_links (battle_linker.rs:35-46) runs it for every pending or in_progress event on a 30s tick (event_sessions/mod.rs:30) until the grace period elapses. There is no per-event backoff, and the 429 claim holds: errors are just logged at debug (battle_linker.rs:~130). How often the 100-page cap is reached depends on upstream behaviour, but the unbounded scan and its repetition are real. Not critical.

findings.title: GET /api/fights loads every fight, every segment and every full snapshot JSON, parses in memory, then paginates
findings.description: `list_fights` does `fight::Entity::find().all()` (line 490, no limit), all `fight_battle` rows, then `GuildBattleSnapshotEntity::find().filter(BattleId.is_in(all ids)).all()` (line 518). This selects every snapshot column including `players_json`, `kills_json` and `losses_json`, which can be hundreds of KB per battle, and only `guilds_json` + 3 counters are used. `resolve_fight_outcome` then `serde_json`-parses `guilds_json` for every segment of every fight on each request. All of this runs on the async runtime worker (no `spawn_blocking`). Only then do `filter_sort_fights` and `paginate_vec` cut to the page (limit up to 1000). Cost grows linearly with total fights ever recorded and is paid on every page, filter or sort change. The same load-all-then-slice pattern is used by `paginate_vec` in bank/alliance.rs:375, battles/service.rs:601 and siphoned/router.rs:370. The other snapshot loads at fights.rs:1295, 1449 and 1772 also pull whole JSON rows.
findings.fix: Persist the derived list fields (outcome, total_players/kills/fame, segment_count) on `fights`/`fight_stats` when a fight changes (the writer `fight_analytics::writer` already recomputes it), and page/sort/filter in SQL with LIMIT/OFFSET. Select only the needed snapshot columns (`select_only` of id, battle_id, total_*, guilds_json) or denormalise the verdict. Drop `paginate_vec` for DB-backed lists.
findings.verify_note: list_fights (fights.rs:485-577) does find().all() on fights, all fight_battle rows and all matching snapshots with the full model, including players_json, kills_json and losses_json (battles/entities.rs:12-24). resolve_fight_outcome parses guilds_json per segment. It filters, sorts and paginates in memory (paginate_vec) on every request. Cost grows linearly with total fights.

findings.title: Auth extractor does 3-4 DB queries and a Discord REST call per request; failures are never cached and there is no per-call timeout
findings.description: Every cookie-session `UserContext` extraction runs `user_id_for_discord_id` (tenant DB). It then calls `PlatformService::is_guild_owner`, which runs the full `TENANT_SELECT ... LEFT JOIN tenant_ranks` control-plane query. Then `apply_live_guild_roles` calls `fetch_guild_member_role_ids`, with a 60s cache keyed by (guild, user) in a global `std::sync::Mutex<HashMap>` that never evicts. On a hit, or after a successful fetch, `roles::Entity::find().all(db)` runs on every request, and possibly an UPDATE of `users.role`. `GuildMemberLookup::Unavailable` (any Discord 429/5xx/network error) is deliberately not cached (`remember_member_lookup` returns early), so during a Discord outage or rate-limit every request retries Discord using the shared client's 30s default timeout (http_client.rs:24). That makes each page load of the SPA, which fans out many parallel `/api` calls, block for up to 30s each and keeps hammering a rate-limited endpoint. There is no singleflight: N concurrent requests after cache expiry each call Discord. The same extractor also runs for bot requests (`resolve_bot_role_ids` reloads `roles` each time, rbac.rs:496).
findings.fix: Cache the tenant owner and kind in `TenantContext` (kind is already there). Cache roles in memory (the `Permissions` cache already loads `roles`) instead of `roles.find().all()` per request. Cache `Unavailable` results for a short negative TTL (5-10s), add singleflight per (guild,user), set a 2-3s per-request timeout on this call, and prune the cache map. Better: do the live-role refresh as a background/session-refresh step instead of in every extractor.
findings.verify_note: Per cookie-session request, rbac.rs:140-176 runs user_id_for_discord_id, then is_guild_owner on the control DB, then fetch_guild_member_role_ids (60s cache), then roles::find().all(db) on every request, plus a possible UPDATE. remember_member_lookup skips Unavailable (auth/service.rs:~610), so there is no negative cache. The cache map never evicts. The shared client has a 30s default timeout (http_client.rs:24). The steady-state cost is 3-4 small queries per request, which is moderate. The 30s stalls only occur during a Discord outage or rate limit. Downgraded from high.

findings.title: AuditService::log is synchronous in the request path: re-parses env, builds a fresh reqwest Client with no timeout, and awaits Discord with retries
findings.description: Each `AuditService::log` call (44 call sites outside tests) does `Config::try_from_env()` (env deserialization every call, ignoring the injected `Config` extension) and `AdminService::get_guild_settings`. It then runs INSERT, `users` lookup, optional second `users` lookup, and finally `send_discord_payload`, which does `reqwest::Client::new()` (a brand-new connection pool and TLS handshake per audit entry, and the crate's own `http_client::shared` docs say not to). That client has no timeout, so a hung Discord connection blocks the originating HTTP handler (for example a bank withdrawal) indefinitely. On 429 it sleeps for `retry_after` up to 3 times inside the request. Loops such as bank/service.rs:866-890 and 971-1146 call it once per transaction, serially.
findings.fix: Make the Discord notification fire-and-forget (push to a bounded mpsc/outbox consumed by one worker task) and keep only the DB insert inline. Use `http_client::shared()` plus a per-request timeout (~5s), use the injected `Config`, and cache guild_settings channel ids per tenant (invalidate on settings update).
findings.verify_note: AuditService::log calls Config::try_from_env() each time (audit/service.rs:~139), then get_guild_settings, the INSERT, 1-2 user lookups, and awaits send_discord_payload inline. That function uses reqwest::Client::new() (service.rs:372) with no timeout and sleeps for retry_after up to 3 times. There are 44 non-test call sites. A hung Discord connection can block the originating handler. Real, but it only bites when an audit channel is configured and Discord misbehaves. Medium.

findings.title: Alliance bank transaction list pulls every page of every member guild serially, sorts in memory, then paginates
findings.description: `list_transactions` for an alliance iterates `active_member_guilds` sequentially and for each calls `list_guild_pages`, which loops `list_transactions` with `limit = MAX_PAGE_LIMIT (1000)` until `total_pages` is exhausted (each page = 3 queries: count, num_pages count, fetch, plus view hydration). All views from all guilds are concatenated, stamped, sorted, and only then `paginate_vec` slices one page (line 375). Cost is O(total transactions across the alliance) per request, and calls per guild are serial. `can_view_others` and `resolve_target_guild` additionally do per-guild `user_by_discord` queries, repeated per request. This is the alliance 'sync everything' read path and it will degrade as guild bank history grows.
findings.fix: Add a global-sort cursor merge: query each guild with the same sort and LIMIT page*size (k-way merge of the first `offset+limit` rows from each guild), run guild queries concurrently with `try_join_all`, and compute totals with SQL COUNT/SUM. Or materialise alliance-level aggregates in the alliance schema (projection already exists for splits: alliance_split_distribution) so alliance reads are single-schema.
findings.verify_note: Alliance bank list_transactions (bank/alliance.rs:292-380) iterates member guilds serially. list_guild_pages loops at limit=1000 until total_pages (171-196). It then sorts everything and slices with paginate_vec. can_view_others and user_by_discord are per guild per request. Correct but O(total history) per request. Medium.

findings.title: Per-tenant SeaORM pools have default sizing; registry evict() leaks pools and re-runs all migrations without singleflight
findings.description: 1) `connect_with_search_path` builds `ConnectOptions` with only the schema search path, so pool size is the sqlx default (max 10, min 1, 30s acquire) per tenant. With the control pool that is roughly 10 x (tenants + 1) possible connections against a Postgres default `max_connections` of 100, so about 10 active tenants under concurrent load can exhaust the server. 2) `evict()` just removes the DashMap entry. It is called on every feature-flag change (platform/service.rs:1558), rank change (1404, 1917) and default-rank assignment (167). The next request calls `load` -> `open_context` -> new pool + `Migrator::up` (the full migration check against ~100 migrations) + permission reload + 2 control queries. The old pool is NOT closed: `event_sessions` and `battle_sync` tasks hold `ctx.db.clone()` forever (`running_sync` already contains the tenant, so workers are never restarted). Each eviction therefore leaks a pool and leaves workers on a different pool than request handlers. 3) `get_or_load` has no singleflight: concurrent first requests after eviction each run `load()` and `Migrator::up` in parallel, and the loser's context is discarded. 4) `warmup()` loads tenants strictly serially, running migrations for each at boot, so startup time scales linearly with tenants.
findings.fix: Set `max_connections`/`min_connections`/`acquire_timeout`/`idle_timeout` explicitly per tenant (e.g. max 3-5), or use one shared pool with `SET LOCAL search_path` per transaction or schema-qualified queries. Make feature/permission/rank changes refresh the existing `TenantContext` (mutable `RwLock<HashSet>`/ArcSwap for `features`, `Permissions::reload`) instead of `evict`. Never drop a context that workers still use. Add a per-tenant `tokio::sync::OnceCell`/mutex in `get_or_load`, run migrations in a dedicated startup/provision step instead of each load, and warm tenants with bounded concurrency.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed: connect_with_search_path sets only the schema search path (postgres.rs:109-117), so pool sizing is the default. evict() just removes the DashMap entry (tenant.rs:280) and is called from platform/service.rs:167,1404,1441,1452,1558,1917. The next load runs open_context, which runs Migrator::up plus a permission reload and 2 control queries (tenant.rs:360-381). get_or_load (270-277) has no singleflight, and warmup (246-256) is serial. The leak claim is overstated: the evicted context's pool is dropped once in-flight requests release it. Only the worker-held pool persists, so you get at most one extra pool per tenant, not a pool per eviction. The 'exhausts at about 10 tenants' figure is speculative, since connections open lazily. The per-evict migrations and the missing singleflight are the real costs.

findings.title: battle_sync tick loads full-JSON snapshot rows (50 existence checks + intel scouting scan) every 120s per guild
findings.description: For each of the 50 battles on page 1, `run_cycle` executes `SnapshotEntity::find().filter(BattleId.eq(..)).one(db)` just to test `.is_some()`, which selects `guilds_json/players_json/kills_json/losses_json` for each saved battle (50 round trips, large rows, every 120s per tenant). Then `scout_recent_snapshots` loads the 50 newest snapshots in full (`.limit(50).all(db)`) only to read `battle_id` from them. `group_orphan_fights` follows with another pass. This produces megabytes of DB traffic per tenant per tick, for nothing.
findings.fix: Replace the loop with one query: `SELECT battle_id FROM guild_battle_snapshots WHERE battle_id = ANY($1)` (or `select_only().column(BattleId)`) and diff against the page. In `scout_recent_snapshots` select only `battle_id` (the `scout_battle` call re-reads what it needs). Skip the whole cycle when page-1 battle ids are unchanged since the last tick (keep the last seen max battle id in memory).
findings.verify_note: battle_sync.rs:132-145 runs a SnapshotEntity find().one() per battle, a full-row select that includes the JSON columns, only to test is_some(). That is 50 serial queries per tick. scout_recent_snapshots (auto_scout.rs:44-54) loads the 50 newest full snapshots. Real waste every 120s per tenant, but a background job. Medium.

findings.title: Background workers: all tenants tick at the same instant, no upstream limiter, no panic supervision
findings.description: Each guild tenant spawns two detached tasks with `tokio::time::interval`. The first tick fires immediately, so all tenants hit AlbionBB (list pages, battle details, kills) and Albion Data (prices) simultaneously at boot and then in lockstep every 30s and 120s. `AlbionBbApiClient` has no semaphore, no retry or Retry-After handling for 429, and a 60s timeout, so a burst turns into upstream rate limiting. The tick also issues two control-plane queries (`SELECT status, kind` then `load_albion_scope`, both reading the same `tenants` row; `prepare_cycle` is duplicated verbatim in both workers). Tasks are fire-and-forget: a panic inside `run_cycle` (the code base has `expect`s) silently kills the worker while `running_sync` still contains the tenant, so `ensure_sync_workers` never restarts it. `interval` defaults to `MissedTickBehavior::Burst`, so a slow cycle is followed by back-to-back catch-up ticks. The fanout worker is a single serial loop (12 targets per 15s tick).
findings.fix: Add a global bounded upstream queue (semaphore plus per-host rate limiter with 429 backoff) shared by workers and request handlers. Stagger starts with jitter. Set `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`. Wrap each cycle in `catch_unwind`/a supervised respawn that clears `running_sync` on exit. Merge the two per-tenant loops into one scheduler with one `tenants` query per tick (or one query for all tenants), and de-duplicate `prepare_cycle`.
findings.verify_note: Both workers use tokio::time::interval with the immediate first tick and default Burst behaviour (battle_sync.rs:41-45; event_sessions/mod.rs:51-55). Tenants are started back to back in lib.rs:114-130. There is no Semaphore, rate limiter or catch_unwind anywhere in src. AlbionBbApiClient returns an error on any non-success status with no 429 handling (client.rs:482). prepare_cycle is duplicated verbatim and queries the tenants row twice per tick. Fanout is serial at 12 targets per 15s (fanout_worker.rs:33-48). The panic-kills-worker risk is theoretical, since no concrete panic path was traced.

findings.title: Guild report loads full snapshot JSON for the window and computes on the async runtime; no singleflight, player report recomputes everything
findings.description: `load()` fetches every snapshot in range with all four JSON columns, plus entire `users`, `albion_links`, `comps`, `comp_builds`, `builds`, `scouted_comp_battle` tables, and all transactions, regears and siphoned rows in the window. `decode_fights` then parses every snapshot's JSON. `matchups(db, &[])` loads its own full tables (scouted_comp_battle, fight_battle, event_battle). All CPU work (JSON decode + `compute_*`) runs inline on a Tokio worker with no `spawn_blocking`, stalling unrelated requests on that thread. `ReportCache` is a plain RwLock map with 5-minute TTL and no singleflight, so concurrent first views (officers opening the page) each run the whole pipeline. `build_player_report` explicitly redoes the entire load for one member.
findings.fix: Select only the columns reports need (store `players_json` aggregates in `battle_player_stats`, which already exists from the evidence tables, and compute reports from SQL aggregates). Move the compute step to `spawn_blocking`. Add singleflight on the cache key and stale-while-revalidate (pre-compute in battle_sync). Let the player report reuse the cached `GuildReport` intermediates.
findings.verify_note: load() (intel/report.rs:622+) loads whole tables or windows, including full snapshots with every JSON column. build_guild_report decodes and computes inline. There is no spawn_blocking anywhere in src. ReportCache (intel/cache.rs) has a 5-minute TTL and no singleflight. build_player_report redoes the full load. The guild report is cached per hour window, which limits the impact. Medium.

findings.title: Event roster/participant hydration is an N+1 of about 5 queries per participant (and per comp_build row)
findings.description: In `get_event_roster`, each participation does `users::find_by_id`, up to two `build::find_by_id` (primary/secondary), `resolve_assigned_build_name` (more build lookups) and `display_name::resolve` (one `albion_links` query). That is about 4-5 queries x up to 100+ participants. `canonical_roster_seats` queries `build::find_by_id` once per `comp_build` row. Roster changes broadcast over a websocket to all connected clients, and each client then refetches this endpoint, so one seat assignment triggers (clients x participants x 5) queries (thundering herd). Bulk helpers already exist (`display_name::resolve_by_ids`, `to_event_views`) and are not used here.
findings.fix: Batch-load users, builds and albion_links with `is_in` (3 queries total), build maps, then assemble. Have the websocket notification carry the changed seat deltas (it already has `changed_seat_keys`) so clients patch locally instead of refetching, and debounce refetches.
findings.verify_note: get_event_roster (events/service.rs:1580-1635) runs per participant: users find_by_id, up to 2 build find_by_id, resolve_assigned_build_name, and display_name::resolve (an albion_links query, display_name.rs:44-54). canonical_roster_seats does one build find per comp_build row (1672-1690). The N+1 is real. The websocket thundering-herd claim is plausible given roster_hub.rs, but it was not traced to the client refetch.

findings.title: Market prices (Albion Data) are uncached and fetched twice per battle; comp/regear pricing and loss estimates all hit the public API
findings.description: `AlbionDataService::prices` has no cache. `get_battle_detail_with_losses` calls `estimate_losses` (prices call, battles/service.rs:991) and then `persist_battle_loss_estimate` (economy/writer.rs:175, plus a second fallback call without a location at line 183) for the same kills, so each synced battle costs 2-4 AODP requests. Regear extraction and comp/build pricing add more. The only cache is `PriceCache` (5 min, per tenant+build id, plain RwLock without singleflight), which does not help worker paths. AODP is heavily rate limited, so 2N tenants x battles will trigger throttling, after which loss estimates silently degrade (`unwrap_or_default`).
findings.fix: Add a shared (server, item_id, location, quality) price cache with TTL (10-30 min), prune and singleflight inside `AlbionDataService`, used by all four call sites. Pass the already-fetched price index from `estimate_losses` to `persist_battle_loss_estimate` instead of fetching twice.
findings.verify_note: AlbionDataService::prices has no cache (albiondata/service.rs:62-85). battles/service.rs:991 and economy/writer.rs:157-190 each call prices for the same kills, and the fallback call only runs when the strategy is CheapestAny. The calls are batched per battle rather than per kill, so the 2-4 requests per battle is about right. Failures fall back to empty via unwrap_or_default. A real inefficiency with limited blast radius.

findings.title: AlbionApiClient (and its reqwest Client) is rebuilt on every call; Albion roster/guild lookups are uncached
findings.description: `AlbionApiClient::new` calls `reqwest::Client::builder().build()` (new pool, new TLS config) and every call site constructs it per call: `AlbionService::new` per request, `albion_guild_alliance_id` (twice per `player_in_discord_albion_alliance`, which runs for each tenant in the alliance fan-out when a member links), `guild_belongs_to_alliance` per member. That defeats keep-alive and contradicts the crate's `http_client` module docs. `get_configured_guild_roster` downloads the full guild roster from the public API on each `create_linked_member`/roster search with no cache. `albion_guild_alliance_id` result for the same guild is re-fetched for every fan-out target.
findings.fix: Hold one `AlbionApiClient` per region built from `http_client::shared()`, inject it as an Extension, and add a short-TTL cache (5-15 min) for `get_guild`, `get_guild_members` and `get_alliance` with singleflight.
findings.verify_note: AlbionApiClient::new builds a fresh reqwest client (albion/client.rs:200-209). It is constructed per call in albion/service.rs:31, alliance_fanout.rs:395 and platform/service.rs:2090. There is no keep-alive reuse and no caching of roster or guild lookups. Real but minor.

findings.title: list_my_battles does serial get_battle for up to 5 pages x N battles, then loads detail JSON per request
findings.description: `list_my_battles` pages up to `MY_BATTLES_MAX_UPSTREAM_PAGES = 5` AlbionBB list calls (uncached), then for every raw battle serially awaits `get_battle` and scans the players vector for a lowercased name match. With 5 pages of ~10-20 battles each, a cold cache means up to ~100 serial upstream calls (60s timeout each) behind one HTTP request. After the first load the 24h detail cache helps, but the result set is still recomputed and paginated in memory on every request, and not cached per user.
findings.fix: Answer from persisted data: `battle_player_stats` (already written by evidence persistence) joined to `albion_links` lets this be a SQL query with LIMIT/OFFSET and no upstream calls. If upstream is kept, fetch details with bounded concurrency and cache the per-user result for a minute.
findings.verify_note: list_my_battles (battles/service.rs:444-505) walks up to 5 uncached list pages. For each raw battle it does a serial get_battle (cached for 24h) and a name scan, then paginates in memory. A cold cache means many serial upstream calls behind one request, and the `?` aborts the whole list on any single failure.

findings.title: Opening a battle runs the entire persistence pipeline inline; per-kill inserts in evidence writer
findings.description: `get_battle_detail_with_losses` is also the HTTP handler path. After fetching battle + kills it runs, in order and awaited inline: loss estimate (AODP), snapshot persist, `RoleClassifier::load`, evidence normalize + persist (a loop with one `insert` per kill plus `insert_many` per kill's items, lines 173-222, inside a transaction), enemy aggregates, fingerprints, loss-estimate persistence and `recompute_fight_analytics`. A 100+ player battle means hundreds of sequential round trips before the user gets a response. Persistence is documented as best-effort and independent of the return value, yet it delays it.
findings.fix: Return the response after the core fetch, and push persistence to a background task or the battle_sync worker (idempotent). Batch kill inserts (`insert_many` with a returning id mapping, or a `COPY`-style multi-row insert) and cache `RoleClassifier` per tenant.
findings.verify_note: get_battle_detail_with_losses (battles/service.rs:253-433) awaits loss estimation, snapshot persistence, classifier load, evidence persistence and the rest inline before returning, and the HTTP handler calls the same function. Persistence is best-effort, so the response is delayed for nothing. The evidence writer's per-kill inserts were not verified line by line. Severity is reduced because this is per battle-open and is idempotent.

findings.title: No response compression, request timeout, concurrency limit or body limit on the router; 800KB catalog is cloned and served raw
findings.description: `tower-http` is built with only `cors` and `trace` features; there is no `CompressionLayer`, `TimeoutLayer`, `ConcurrencyLimitLayer` or explicit `DefaultBodyLimit` in lib.rs. `GET /api/openalbion/catalog` returns ~2,700 items from an 807KB JSON as an uncompressed array, and `list_catalog` does `catalog_items().to_vec()` (a deep clone of every `String`) on each call. `comps::service::hydrate_icons` also calls `list_catalog().await` (a full clone) then runs a nested loop over (types x catalog). `catalog_item_by_id` is an O(n) linear scan over the catalog (used per build item, regear and comp pricing); an id-indexed HashMap exists for other lookups but not this one. A slow handler (e.g. perf-1/2) has no upper time bound.
findings.fix: Enable `CompressionLayer` (gzip/br), a global `TimeoutLayer` (e.g. 30s), a `ConcurrencyLimitLayer`, and serve the catalog as a pre-serialised `&'static [u8]` / `Bytes` with ETag + Cache-Control. Use a `HashMap<i64,&'static OpenAlbionItem>` for `catalog_item_by_id` and iterate the static slice instead of cloning.
findings.verify_note: Cargo.toml:17 enables only the cors and trace features of tower-http, and lib.rs:150-205 has no compression, timeout, concurrency or body-limit layers. list_catalog does catalog_items().to_vec() (openalbion/service.rs:93-96), and catalog_item_by_id is a linear find (140-143). Compression may already be applied by the frontend proxy or reverse proxy, which was not checked. This is hardening and micro-optimisation rather than a defect, so low.

findings.title: Alliance->guild event fanout deep-copies the whole comp graph row by row for every target on every operation
findings.description: `process_target` calls `copy_alliance_comp_to_tenant` for every publish/update/archive retry, even when the comp is unchanged. That function does `build::find_by_id` + `resolve_created_by` + `copy_build_graph` per build; `copy_build_graph` deletes and re-inserts all `build_items` and spells with one INSERT each, then `save_asset_map` per build runs against the control DB. Targets are processed serially at most 12 per 15s tick, so publishing one event to 10+ guilds takes multiple ticks, and every event edit re-runs the full copy per guild (and rewrites item ids). `retry_delay_seconds` is duplicated between fanout_worker.rs:105 and mirror_retry.rs:223, and the two outboxes (alliance->guild and guild->alliance) are separate mechanisms with separate retry tables.
findings.fix: Compare a content hash/updated_at/version of the source comp with the last copied one stored in the asset map and skip the copy when unchanged. Use `insert_many` for items/spells. Process targets with bounded concurrency (per-target tenant DB is independent). Unify the two outbox/retry mechanisms behind one worker and one `retry_delay` helper.
findings.verify_note: process_target always calls copy_alliance_comp_to_tenant when a comp exists (fanout_worker.rs:163-190). That runs per-build copy_build_graph, which deletes and re-inserts build_items and spells with one INSERT each (alliance_share/service.rs:640-710), plus save_asset_map per build. There is no change detection. Targets are processed serially at 12 per tick. retry_delay_seconds is duplicated (fanout_worker.rs:105, mirror_retry.rs:223). This is background work, so severity is low.

findings.title: More N+1 patterns in list/read endpoints: VOD forum polling, islands, combat roster fit, readiness
findings.description: `pending_vod_forum_posts` and `archived_vod_forum_posts` (polled by the Discord bot) call `to_event_view` per event instead of the batched `to_event_views` (3-4 queries each). `list_islands` runs `load_island_view` (a `tabs` query) per island. `build_roster_fit` does `users::find_by_id` + `display_name::resolve` (an `albion_links` query) for every member with specializations (up to hundreds), the same shape at combat/service.rs:349 and 912. `retry_pending_event_completion_xp` runs every 30s per tenant and aborts the whole batch on the first DB error via `?`. Split sync/credit logic updates and inserts per row (splits/service.rs:132-165, 259-340).
findings.fix: Use `to_event_views` for batches, one `IN` query for island tabs, `resolve_by_ids` + a single `users is_in` query in combat, and `insert_many`/batch updates in splits.
findings.verify_note: pending_vod_forum_posts and archived_vod_forum_posts call to_event_view per event (events/service.rs:1407-1445). list_islands does a tabs query per island (splits/service.rs:1689-1706). build_roster_fit does user find plus display_name::resolve per member (combat/service.rs:142-200). retry_pending_event_completion_xp aborts the batch via `?` on the first error (events/service.rs:4230). All are real but small-N or rare.

findings.title: Pagination issues three count queries per list and lower(...) LIKE '%q%' search without index support
findings.description: 19 call sites do `paginator.num_items()` then `paginator.num_pages()`. In SeaORM `num_pages` internally calls `num_items` again, so each list issues two `COUNT(*)` plus the page query. Search is `lower(col) LIKE '%term%'` (leading wildcard, function on column), which cannot use a btree index and seq-scans (events.title, splits.note, users.username subquery).
findings.fix: Use `paginator.num_items_and_pages()` (one count) at each site via a small shared helper in pagination.rs. For hot searches add a `pg_trgm` GIN index on lower(title/note/username) or use ILIKE with trigram indexes.
findings.verify_note: There are 19 num_pages() call sites (e.g. events/service.rs:2699-2706). In SeaORM 1.x, num_pages internally recomputes num_items, so two COUNTs run per list. Leading-wildcard lower() LIKE search cannot use a btree index. Minor.

findings.title: Missing standalone index for event_battles.albionbb_battle_id lookups
findings.description: The only index covering `albionbb_battle_id` is the unique composite `(event_id, albionbb_battle_id)`, which a filter on `albionbb_battle_id` alone cannot use. `find_linked_event` (run on every battle detail open and sync) and the intel/matchups joins filter by battle id only, so they seq-scan `event_battles`. Other hot FK columns (transactions, splits, snapshots, evidence) are indexed.
findings.fix: Add a migration creating `CREATE INDEX idx_event_battles_albionbb_battle_id ON event_battles(albionbb_battle_id)` (and consider storing the id as BIGINT).
findings.verify_note: The only index on event_battles.albionbb_battle_id is the composite unique (event_id, albionbb_battle_id) (m20260713_000002_create_event_battles.rs:63-70). find_linked_event filters by battle id alone (battles/service.rs:1214-1226). The table is small per tenant, so a seq scan is cheap. Negligible practical impact.

findings.title: Fights module classifies sides from global env Config instead of the tenant's Albion scope
findings.description: `friendly_side(config)` builds the friendly side from `config.albion_guild_id` and the allied ids/names read from env at boot (fights.rs:719-725; same at 1594 and 1853). The battles module correctly resolves the per-tenant scope via `load_albion_scope`, but fights does not, so in a multi-tenant deployment fight outcomes/win-loss for any tenant other than the env guild are classified against the wrong guild, and alliance tenants have no scope at all. `lib.rs` also constructs a global `BattlesService` and `RegearGuildContext` from env purely as templates.
findings.fix: Resolve the scope per request (cache `AlbionScope` in `TenantContext` and refresh it on tenant settings change) and have fights, regear and battles all take `&AlbionScope`. Delete the env-derived singletons.
findings.verify_note: fights.rs:719-725 builds friendly_side from the env Config, and the same pattern is at 1594 and 1853. No per-tenant override of the Config extension exists (tenant.rs only reads it for the bot check), and fights.rs never calls load_albion_scope. Outcome and win-loss classification are therefore wrong for any tenant whose Albion guild differs from the env guild. Alliance tenants have no scope at all. This is a correctness bug, not a perf nit, and it is the most important finding in this list.

findings.title: God files and duplicated helpers; request-time tenant data fetched ad hoc instead of from the registry
findings.description: events/service.rs has ~5,000 production lines and 131 async fns in one `impl EventService` (plus 4,300 lines of inline tests); comps (2,300), platform (2,100), fights.rs (2,200 prod, router+service+analytics in one file), bank, splits and alliance_share are similar. `pagination.rs` has ~800 lines of near-identical `Paginated*` wrapper structs and `From` impls that could be a generic with `utoipa` aliases. Duplicates: `prepare_cycle` (identical in battle_sync.rs and event_sessions/mod.rs), `retry_delay_seconds` (fanout_worker.rs / mirror_retry.rs), `SELECT kind FROM tenants` (tenant.rs, attribution.rs), `SELECT status, kind` + `load_albion_scope` both reading the `tenants` row, `user_by_discord`-style helpers per module, two separate paginate-in-memory implementations (`paginate_vec`, openalbion `paginate`). Tenant metadata (kind, owner, status, Albion scope, allied ids) is re-queried from the control DB ad hoc in the extractor (rbac.rs:164), workers (every tick) and handlers (`load_albion_scope` at 15 call sites) instead of living in `TenantContext` with a single invalidation path.
findings.fix: Split big services by use case (events: crud, roster, linking, completion/xp, calendar; platform: tenants, ranks, alliances, features). Put tenant metadata + scope in a refreshable `TenantContext` snapshot and give workers/handlers one accessor. Extract `workers::{scheduler, retry}` and a generic `Paginated<T>` type.
findings.verify_note: Maintainability observations that hold up. events/service.rs is 9320 lines (production code ends around 4990, then the tests), with 149 async fns. comps is 5089 lines, platform 3652 and fights 3313. prepare_cycle is duplicated in battle_sync.rs and event_sessions/mod.rs, and retry_delay_seconds in the two outbox workers. load_albion_scope has 13 non-test call sites. Not a defect. Low.

logic_questions: How many guild tenants (and member guilds per alliance) do you expect in production over the next 6-12 months? This decides whether to keep one pool per tenant (needs explicit small max_connections per pool plus PgBouncer) or move to a single shared pool with transaction-scoped search_path.

Is horizontal scaling (more than one backend replica) in scope? RosterHub, ReportCache/PriceCache, the AlbionBB cache, the Discord member-lookup cache and the per-tenant worker tasks are all in-process; with N replicas every tenant would run its workers N times and caches would diverge. Options: (a) stay single replica and document it, (b) move workers to a leader-elected/advisory-lock singleton and caches to Redis/Postgres.

Should /api/battles and /api/fights keep reading live from AlbionBB (what the code does today: 20 pages per list view), or should the list views be served only from persisted `guild_battle_snapshots`/evidence populated by the sync worker? The second is much faster but means a battle shows up in the UI only after the next sync tick (up to 2 min plus AlbionBB ingest lag).

For alliance tenants: should alliance-level reads (bank, splits, events, comps) be served from a projection written into the alliance schema at write time (like `alliance_split_distribution`), or aggregated live across member-guild schemas at request time (like alliance bank today)? A projection is faster and simpler to paginate, but needs a reliable fanout/outbox for every write path.

Permission and role freshness: is a 60s staleness window acceptable for Discord role changes (so the live role fetch can move out of the request path into a periodic or event-driven refresh), or must a role removal take effect on the very next request?

Audit/notification delivery: can Discord audit-log and announcement posts be asynchronous best-effort (queued, possibly delayed or lost on crash), or must the originating action fail or wait when Discord is unreachable?

Fights/reports currently classify 'our side' from env-configured `ALBION_GUILD_ID` in some places and from per-tenant `AlbionScope` in others. Is the env config meant to be removed entirely in favour of tenant settings (and what should an alliance tenant's 'friendly side' be: all active member guild ids, as `EventReadScope` already does)?

Retention: is there any intended pruning of `guild_battle_snapshots` (full players/kills/losses JSON per battle), `battle_kills`, audit logs and fanout/outbox rows? Without it the load-all queries in fights/reports, and table sizes generally, grow forever.

summary:
The frontend is Angular 21 (standalone, signals, Analog/Vite, SSR enabled) with a hand-rolled data layer. All 99 components are OnPush, all routes are lazy (app.routes.ts), ECharts is dynamically imported, and the shared primitives are reasonably adopted (PageHeader/PageStack in 55 files, DataTable in 27, Dialog in 26, Loading/ErrorState widely). Gaps in the ordinary hygiene checks are small. The real problems are architectural.

Data flow today:
- ApiService (core/services/api.service.ts) is a thin HttpClient wrapper. There are no interceptors, no HTTP cache, no shared store, and no resource()/httpResource.
- Each of the roughly 57 feature files calls `firstValueFrom(api.get(...))` in its own constructor or `load()`. There are about 374 such calls and 389 api.* call sites.
- Each component hand-rolls its own loading, failed and race-guard signals. Only 5 files have a request-sequence guard.
- The same session-scoped resources are refetched everywhere: `api/albion/link/me` in 5 places, `api/alliances/me` in 3, and bank balance, metrics and progression in several.
- AuthService holds the profile in a signal and the profile is fetched once. TranslateService statically imports all 5 dictionaries (a 760KB chunk). Realtime exists only for the event roster (a WebSocket through a Nitro proxy). Notifications poll a badge every 30s.
- Nothing else refreshes after a Discord-side action, because there is no invalidation channel.

Where the owner's complaints show up in the frontend:
- Alliance sync is invisible. The backend exposes `/events/{id}/mirror-status`, `/events/{id}/mirror-retry` and `/splits/{id}/distribution-status`, and none of the three is called from the frontend.
- Alliance tenants get the guild personal dashboard, and the tenant rail is a flat list.
- Business logic is computed in the browser: withdrawal selection and split payout shares (bank, splits), and counts and attention items via list endpoints (events, dashboard, admin hub). Anything computed in the browser cannot be shared with Discord.
- Event time entry uses browser timezone while Discord uses the guild timezone.

Performance causes:
- The i18n bundle is eager.
- SSR renders only the login shell for every auth-gated route, then re-renders after hydration.
- Pages issue many parallel list requests where one aggregate endpoint would do.
- The event-detail component is 6,230 lines, with a 1-second ticker re-checking its whole template.

UI against DESIGN.md and the Zed redesign plan: about 5 out of 10.
- Positives: tokenised CSS variables, hairline borders, a compact shell, light and dark themes, tenant branding with contrast-aware ink, and a native `<dialog>`-based Dialog.
- DESIGN.md and plans/zed-compact-frontend-redesign.md (status Active, acceptance boxes unchecked) call for the Zed system: light default, IBM Plex Serif headings, 2px radii, near-zero shadows.
- styles.css still carries the full Discord token set (Nunito, 8–24px radii, indigo-black). A second Zed override block is appended from line 1722 and kills shadows with `!important`. The result is two stacked, partly contradictory systems.
- IBM Plex is never loaded; index.html only requests Inter, Nunito and Geist Mono.
- ThemeService defaults to dark while the CSS `:root` default is light, so there is a theme flash.
- There are 76 `rounded-xl/2xl/3xl` uses, 161 text sizes under 12px, 45 raw `<select>` elements, 24 raw `<table>` elements, native `confirm()` dialogs, hardcoded Italian and English strings, no route titles, and low-contrast disabled text.

Proposed refactor:
1. Add a `core/data` layer: a tenant-keyed query/resource store with dedupe, stale-while-revalidate, per-tenant clearing on switch, and invalidation driven by one generalized WebSocket or SSE channel. Replace the per-component `firstValueFrom` boilerplate.
2. Add backend aggregate endpoints so the frontend renders instead of computes:
   - `/api/me/overview` (dashboard, including attention items and next mass)
   - `/api/admin/overview`
   - `/api/events/summary`
   - `/api/bank/withdrawable` and a server-side `withdraw {amount|ids}`
   - split preview shares from the existing `participant_shares`
   - tenant-timezone-aware event create
3. Add shared primitives: a `ListPage` template (PageHeader + FilterBar + server-mode DataTable), a `DetailPage` template (header + child-route tabs + `@defer`), `MoneyPipe`/`DateTimePipe`, a `ConfirmDialog` service, a `FormField`, and an `AllianceScopeBar` (guild filter and sync badge) used by events, splits, bank and users.
4. Split event-detail, comp-detail, battle-detail and admin-finance into routed child components.
5. Lazy-load i18n per language.
6. Pick one design system (finish Zed), delete the other token block, load its real fonts, and add a pre-boot theme script.
7. Generate api.models.ts from the backend OpenAPI schema; the Discord bot's types.ts could use the same schema.

findings.title: Alliance sync state is invisible in the web UI: mirror-status, mirror-retry and distribution-status endpoints are never called
findings.description: The backend added an event mirror retry system and an alliance split distribution status (GET /splits/{id}/distribution-status, GET /events/{id}/mirror-status, POST /events/{id}/mirror-retry). A grep of apps/frontend/src finds zero references to `mirror-status`, `mirror-retry` or `distribution-status`. The only alliance awareness in event/split pages is a boolean `is_synchronized_copy` badge and a fetch of `api/alliances/me` (just to decide whether the 'ping alliance' checkbox is enabled). When a mirror to a member guild fails or an alliance split has not distributed, the officer sees nothing in the web UI and cannot retry. This matches the owner's report that synchronizations 'do not work at all': they may run, but the user has no feedback and no repair action.
findings.fix: Add an `AllianceSyncBadge` component, used on event-detail, events list, split-detail and splits list. It reads mirror-status and distribution-status per guild (or a batched `sync_status` field on the list endpoints) and shows ok / pending / failed / inactive with a Retry button wired to mirror-retry. Add an alliance panel on admin-alliance listing recent failed mirror requests across member guilds. Surface the same states in the bot so both channels show one backend-computed status.
findings.verify_note: Grep of apps/frontend/src finds no reference to mirror-status, mirror-retry or distribution-status. The backend routes exist at events/router.rs:196-197. The UI has no way to see mirror state or retry it. This is a missing feature, not breakage, so I lowered it from high to medium.

findings.title: Bank withdrawal eligibility and selection is computed in the browser by downloading every pending and rejected transaction
findings.description: openWithdrawal() calls loadRequestableCredits(), which loops `GET api/bank/transactions?status=pending` and `status=rejected` at limit=1000 per page until total_pages is exhausted (loadTransactionsByStatus). It then filters client-side (`amount > 0 || split_id != null`, `transaction.guild_tenant_id === guildTenantId`). The `guildTenantId` is never sent to the API, so in an alliance tenant it downloads every member guild's ledger and discards other guilds in the browser. toSilverCents/canSelectWithdrawalGroup/toggleSelectAllWithdrawalCredits then run a greedy subset-selection against pending_total, using float arithmetic. This is money logic and a rule Discord cannot reuse. It also scales with ledger size and can drift from what POST /withdraw validates.
findings.fix: Add a backend endpoint (e.g. GET /api/bank/withdrawable?guild_tenant_id=) returning grouped requestable credits and the max withdrawable amount, and make POST /api/bank/transactions/withdraw accept either `transaction_ids` or `amount` (server picks FIFO and enforces the rules). The frontend renders the list and a single amount input. The Discord bot calls the same endpoint.
findings.verify_note: bank.ts:909-941 pages through every pending and rejected transaction at limit=1000 and filters by guild_tenant_id in the browser. The query params are only page, limit and status. toSilverCents selection runs client-side. The backend withdraw already accepts transaction_ids or all, so the money rules are still enforced server-side. The cost is performance and no reuse from Discord, not a money bug.

findings.title: Switching tenant while on /dashboard keeps showing the previous tenant's data; notifications and caches are not reset
findings.description: TenantRail.select() calls `auth.switchTenant()` (which only sets the profile signal) and then `router.navigateByUrl('/dashboard')`. The router is configured without `onSameUrlNavigation: 'reload'`, so when the user is already on /dashboard (the most common case) the navigation is ignored and the Dashboard component, which loads its six requests once in its constructor, keeps the old tenant's balance, events and attention items. Only branding repaints, via an effect. NotificationService is a root singleton: its unread count and inbox items are not reset or refetched on switch and stay stale until the next 30s poll. Every page that holds data in component signals has the same exposure whenever the profile changes without a route change (e.g. switching from an alliance hub to a member guild).
findings.fix: Introduce a `TenantContext` signal (tenant_id) and make the data layer key on it. Until then, after switchTenant call `window.location.assign('/dashboard')` (hard reset) or `router.navigateByUrl('/dashboard', {onSameUrlNavigation:'reload'})` plus an explicit NotificationService.reset(). Use `shellKey = tenant_id` on the `<router-outlet>` wrapper (`@for` with track) to destroy and recreate the page.
findings.verify_note: tenant-rail.ts:239-240 calls switchTenant, which only sets the profile, then navigateByUrl('/dashboard'). No onSameUrlNavigation is configured anywhere. The Dashboard loads once in its constructor and has no profile effect, so on /dashboard it keeps the old tenant's data. NotificationService has no reset on switch. The stale view only occurs when the user is already on /dashboard, so I rated it medium.

findings.title: Web event creation interprets wall-clock times in the browser timezone, Discord uses the guild's discord_event_timezone
findings.description: events.ts builds mass/start with `new Date(`${date}T${time}`)` (combineLocalDateTime), i.e. the browser's local zone, and sends `toISOString()`. Defaults are hardcoded 19:30 and 20:00. The bot resolves the same kind of input in the guild's configured IANA timezone (`guildSettings.discord_event_timezone ?? 'Europe/Rome'`). The web never reads `discord_event_timezone` outside the admin form. An officer in another timezone entering '20:00' on the web creates an event at a different instant than '20:00' typed in Discord, and the pre-filled defaults are wrong for non-Italian browsers. Edit forms and the countdown have the same problem.
findings.fix: Expose the tenant timezone on the profile or settings payload, and parse/format event wall-clock times with that zone (Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone). Better, accept `{date, mass_time, start_time, timezone}` on POST /api/events and let the backend do the conversion so web and bot share one code path. Show the zone next to every time input.
findings.verify_note: The web events.ts combineLocalDateTime uses the browser zone. discord_event_timezone is only used in admin-discord.ts. The bot uses the guild zone only in the /flash modal (modal.ts:119), which is a free-text flash-mass flow. The web form uses explicit pickers in the user's own zone. That is a defensible difference rather than a clear defect, and the two flows are not the same input. The remaining gap is that the defaults (19:30, 20:00) and the zone are not tied to the guild.

findings.title: Split fee, net value and per-participant shares are recomputed in the browser with different rounding than the backend
findings.description: The backend computes net with round_dp(2) and distributes with participant_shares(), where the last participant receives the rounding remainder so shares sum exactly to net. The frontend re-implements this: netOf() with a hardcoded `DEFAULT_SPLIT_FEE = 20` (declared separately in splits.ts and split-detail.ts) used when `fee` is null, a template expression computing the fee amount inline (line 559), and estimatedShare() using `Math.round(net*(w/total)*100)/100` for every participant including the last. The previewed shares can differ by a cent from credited amounts and may not add up to net. If the backend default fee ever changes, the UI silently lies. Discord has no access to this logic.
findings.fix: Return `fee_amount`, `net_value` and `participants[].estimated_share` in SplitDetail and expose a POST /api/splits/preview endpoint for the edit form (weights, values). Delete netOf/estimatedShare/DEFAULT_SPLIT_FEE from the frontend.
findings.verify_note: The duplication is real: DEFAULT_SPLIT_FEE in two files, netOf and estimatedShare using Math.round with no last-participant remainder. But the backend SplitDetail.fee is a non-optional Decimal, so the `fee ?? DEFAULT` fallback is effectively dead. The create form takes its default from kpi.default_split_fee (splits.ts:1902). Templates prefer row.share_amount when it is present. estimatedShare is only a pre-completion preview, so it is cosmetic and can be off by a cent. Credited amounts are computed by the backend. Not high.

findings.title: No data layer: 374 hand-written fetches, no caching, duplicated session-level requests and almost no race protection
findings.description: ApiService has no cache, no interceptor and no request dedupe. A grep finds 374 `firstValueFrom(` calls in 57 feature files, 0 uses of resource()/httpResource/rxResource, and only 5 files with a request-sequence guard (events.ts:load() at line 945 has none, so a slow earlier page can overwrite a newer filter). Concrete duplication: `api/albion/link/me` is fetched by the shell's AlbionLinkGate on every shell mount and again by dashboard.ts:712, settings.ts:1061, albion-settings.ts:285 and battles.ts:833; `api/alliances/me` by events.ts, event-detail.ts and admin-alliance.ts; bank balance/metrics/progression by dashboard and settings. On login the dashboard fires 6 parallel requests plus the shell's link-gate and tenant-rail requests. Each component re-implements loading/failed/empty signals and error toasts (`error instanceof Error ? error.message : ...` appears 216 times).
