This is a main cause of 'the app is slow' and of stale or desynced views.
findings.fix: Add core/data with a `createResource(key, fetcher)` helper (on Angular resource()/rxResource) backed by a tenant-keyed cache with TTL/SWR, in-flight dedupe and invalidation tags. Move session-level resources (albion link, alliance context, balance, tenants, permissions) into root services (`AllianceContextService`, `AlbionLinkService`). Add an HttpInterceptor for error normalization, 401 handling and abort-on-navigate. Convert list pages to server-mode DataTable plus resource().
findings.verify_note: No interceptor, no resource()/rxResource, and ApiService has no cache or dedupe. api/albion/link/me is fetched in 5 places (albion-link-gate, dashboard, settings, albion-settings, battles). api/alliances/me is fetched in 3 places. The counts are slightly off (394 firstValueFrom calls in 62 files, not 374 in 57). The architecture problem is real, but it is not a defect with a traced failure path, so I rated it medium.

findings.title: All five 150-200KB i18n dictionaries are statically bundled into the shared chunk (760KB minified)
findings.description: TranslateService (providedIn root, injected by shell, topbar, login and nearly every page; the built chunk is imported by 68 other chunks) does `import { en } ... { es } ... { fr } ... { it } ... { uk }` and builds `DICTIONARIES` eagerly. Source sizes are en 145KB, es 155KB, fr 159KB, it 153KB, uk 203KB. The built `translate.service-*.js` is 759,615 bytes, the largest JS asset in the build and bigger than the ECharts runtime. Every user downloads, parses and keeps in memory four languages they will never use before the first authenticated paint.
findings.fix: Keep `en` static (or also lazy) and `await import('../../i18n/<lang>')` for the selected language. Hydrate the signal when the chunk resolves, and block bootstrap with an APP_INITIALIZER only for the detected language. Optionally split dictionaries by route group (admin.*, platform.*, intel.*) so admin strings load with the admin routes. Expect the first-load JS to drop by roughly 600KB.
findings.verify_note: translate.service.ts:3-7 statically imports all five dictionaries (about 815KB source). dist/client/assets/translate.service-B87Vssh0.js is 759,615 bytes. Gzip transfer is much smaller than the minified size, so medium.

findings.title: SSR is net-negative: every auth-gated route server-renders the login page, then the client re-renders it (hydration mismatch), and all API traffic goes through a Node proxy hop
findings.description: AuthService.fetchProfile() deliberately returns null on the server (the cookie is never forwarded to the render), so authGuard on the server always redirects to /login?next=...; the HTML for /events/12 is the login screen. The client then boots, probes /api/auth/me, and navigates to the real page, so the user gets a login flash followed by a destroy-and-recreate (hydration with event replay cannot match, since the Shell reads localStorage in its constructor, and TranslateService/ThemeService choose language and theme from localStorage/navigator that do not exist server-side, so even the matching parts mismatch). Nothing is prerendered (prerender.routes=[]). Meanwhile the production runtime is a Node/Nitro server that also proxies every /api call and the roster WebSocket, adding a hop, no compression tuning and no caching to each of the 389 request sites. SSR here costs CPU and complexity for zero benefit on an app whose every route needs a session.
findings.fix: Set `analog({ ssr: false })` (SPA build served statically, `/api` and `/api/events/*/roster/live` proxied by the edge/ingress instead of Nitro), or forward the cookie to the render and run auth.load() server-side with TransferState. SPA is simpler and removes the hydration class of bugs. Keep the Nitro proxy only if the container must stay single-process.
findings.verify_note: auth.service.ts:160-172 confirms the server render is always signed out. Because of this the auth guard redirects every protected route to /login on the server, and prerender routes is []. The nitro proxy hop is real. But this is documented as deliberate, and the claim of a hydration mismatch is speculative and not traced. The cost is a login flash and wasted SSR, not a functional break.

findings.title: No global HTTP error handling: expired session or tenant removal mid-use only produces repeated failing toasts
findings.description: provideHttpClient(withFetch(), withInterceptorsFromDi()) is configured but no interceptor exists (grep for HttpInterceptorFn/HTTP_INTERCEPTORS finds nothing). A 401/403 after the initial `auth.load()` is only handled by the notification poller (which sets the badge to 0). Each page just toasts the ApiError message, so a signed-out user keeps clicking on a shell that looks alive. Error toasts are `truncate`d single lines that auto-dismiss after 3.5s, so a long backend detail (e.g. a 409 explanation) is cut off and gone before it can be read (WCAG 2.2.1).
findings.fix: Add a functional interceptor in app.config: on 401 call `auth.setProfile(null)` and navigate to /login?next=; on 403 'tenant removed' re-run auth.load(). Make error toasts persistent until dismissed (or 8s+ with pause on hover) and allow wrapping; add role='alert' for kind==='error'.
findings.verify_note: No HttpInterceptor exists. 401/403 is handled only in auth.service load and the notification poller. Correction to the finding: toast.error uses 6000ms, not 3500ms (toast.service.ts:29). The toast text is still `truncate`d single-line (topbar.ts:206). The toast region has role=region aria-live=polite, not role=alert.

findings.title: Counts, 'attention' items and 'next mass' are derived client-side from list endpoints (up to 7 requests per page, silently capped at 100 rows)
findings.description: events.ts loadStats() fetches `api/events?limit=100` and counts `status==='live'`, `'scheduled'` and `call_to_arms` in the browser; with more than 100 events the live/scheduled/CTA tiles are wrong (total_items is correct, the rest are not). admin-hub.ts loadOverview() issues up to 7 parallel list calls with `limit: 1` only to read `total_items` (users, splits, events, withdrawals, regears), plus summary, permission matrix and audit. dashboard.ts decides what needs the user's attention (withdraw pending, regears, link Albion, a mass starting in under 6 hours) and which event is 'next mass' (selectNextMass, formatMassEta) in the browser from 20+10 events. admin-finance.ts calls the expensive `api/intel/report` twice (current and previous window) and computes deltas and averages (avgLoot, regearCoverageRatio) client-side. The same attention logic would have to be duplicated in the bot for the same 'what do I need to do' view.
findings.fix: Add `GET /api/me/overview` (balance, pending actions with typed `kind` + deep link, next mass, attendance), `GET /api/admin/overview` (queue counts), `GET /api/events/summary` (counts per status) and a `compare=previous` parameter on `intel/report`. The frontend only renders; the bot's `/me` view uses the same payloads.
findings.verify_note: events.ts:808-818 counts live, scheduled and CTA events from only the first 100 events, so the tiles are wrong above 100 events. This is a real concrete bug. admin-hub makes up to 7 limit=1 count calls. The dashboard attention logic is derived client-side. Mostly an architecture and parity concern, so low overall.

findings.title: Two design systems stacked in styles.css; the Zed redesign is half applied and its fonts are never loaded
findings.description: DESIGN.md and plans/zed-compact-frontend-redesign.md (status Active, all acceptance boxes unchecked) specify the Zed system: light default, IBM Plex Serif headings, 2px radii, shadowless, hairline. styles.css still opens with 'Style reference: DESIGN.md — Discord', defines the Discord palette/radius scale (4/8/12/16/24px, Nunito display, indigo-black) at lines 1–1700, and then appends a second `:root, html.light` / `html.dark` token block at 1722–1800 that overrides colors and fonts, plus `.shadow-lg/xl/2xl{box-shadow:none !important}` (line 1803). Components still hardcode the old geometry: 76 uses of `rounded-xl/2xl/3xl` (e.g. bank.ts:232 `rounded-xl`), vs 1 of `rounded-sm/none`. index.html's comment still describes Nunito/Ginto Nord and loads only Inter, Nunito and Geist Mono, while `--font-display` is now 'IBM Plex Serif' and `--font-mono` 'IBM Plex Mono', neither of which is ever fetched, so headings fall back to Georgia and the mono to ui-monospace. The result looks inconsistent (serif headings from fallback fonts next to Discord-sized rounded cards) and cannot be maintained: any token change must be made in two places.
findings.fix: Pick one system (per the plan: Zed). Delete the Discord token block and merge the Zed values into the single `:root`/`.dark` definitions. Load IBM Plex Serif/Sans/Mono (self-hosted woff2 with `font-display: swap` and `preload`, not Google Fonts). Replace `rounded-xl/2xl` with `--radius-*` tokens through a lint rule (ban arbitrary radius utilities) and remove the `!important` shadow hack. Tick off the acceptance list in the plan as screens are converted.
findings.verify_note: styles.css header still says 'Style reference: DESIGN.md — Discord', and a second Zed token block sits at about 1722 with a `.shadow-*{box-shadow:none !important}` override. --font-display is 'IBM Plex Serif' and --font-mono is 'IBM Plex Mono' (styles.css:1772-1774), but nothing loads them: grep finds no Plex font files or links, and index.html loads only Inter, Nunito and Geist Mono. 77 rounded-xl/2xl/3xl uses. Cosmetic inconsistency.

findings.title: Theme flash on every load: CSS defaults to light, ThemeService defaults to dark and applies the class only after Angular boots; fonts are render-blocking third-party CSS
findings.description: The Zed block makes `:root` light, but ThemeService.loadPreference() returns 'dark' when nothing is stored, and the `dark` class is toggled inside a constructor effect, i.e. after bundle load, bootstrap and the auth probe. index.html has no inline script that sets `<html class>` from localStorage/prefers-color-scheme, so every new or dark-preference user sees a white page that flips to dark (and light-preference users see a dark first paint depending on stored value). The Google Fonts stylesheet is a render-blocking cross-origin request (preconnect to googleapis/gstatic) that also leaks every visitor to a third party.
findings.fix: Add a tiny synchronous inline script in index.html that reads `alm.theme` (default 'system' to match the plan's light default) and sets `document.documentElement.classList` and `color-scheme` before first paint. Self-host the fonts. Make the default preference 'system' or 'light' to match plans/zed-compact-frontend-redesign.md.
findings.verify_note: index.html has no inline theme script. ThemeService.loadPreference defaults to 'dark' (theme.service.ts:79). The html class is set in a constructor effect after bootstrap, while :root is light in the Zed block. That gives a light-to-dark flash for new or dark-preference users. The Google Fonts stylesheet is render-blocking. Cosmetic.

findings.title: event-detail.ts is a 6,230-line single component (2,990-line template, 101 signals, 36 API calls) with a 1s ticker that re-checks the whole view
findings.description: All event tabs (roster, builds, splits, battles, regear, VOD, Discord, members) live in one class: 101 `signal`s and 50 `computed`s, tab state in a `tab` signal, a 6,000-line file that nobody can safely change. `currentTime` is set every second by setInterval (line 4143) and read by the large-template `countdownText` computed, so the OnPush view of the entire 3k-line template is marked dirty every second for as long as the page is open, including while the tab is hidden. `loadAllBuilds` pulls 500 builds on demand; each tab's data is requested from the same component. The same pattern repeats in comp-detail (2,656), battle-detail (2,740), admin-finance (2,859), fight-detail (2,083) and splits (2,012). There is no `@defer` anywhere, so heavy panels such as equipment grids and charts are instantiated eagerly once their tab opens.
findings.fix: Turn event detail into a routed shell (`events/:id` with child routes roster | splits | battles | settings), each a small component with its own resource. Move the countdown into a leaf `<app-countdown [target]>` component that owns the timer (pause on `document.hidden`). Use `@defer (on viewport)` for equipment grids and charts. Apply the same split to the other >2k-line pages.
findings.verify_note: event-detail.ts has 6230 lines. A 1s setInterval (4143) writes currentTime, which is read by countdownText with no document.hidden check. There is no @defer anywhere. Counts are inflated: about 50 `signal(` calls, not 101. The 1s tick only re-evaluates the template diff and is cheap. This is a maintainability issue more than a defect.

findings.title: Untranslated hardcoded strings in Italian and English bypass the 5-language i18n system
findings.description: Examples: 'Seleziona una build o uno slot primario.', 'Ruolo extra aggiunto al roster.', 'Mass deve essere uguale o precedente all'orario di Start.', 'Incantesimi Selezionati', 'Nessun incantesimo salvato', 'Nessuna abilità configurabile per questo set.', 'Nessun equipaggiamento' (Italian), and 'Member added to the event.', 'Starting now', 'Failed to copy link.', 'Item saved', 'Flash Mass', `Battle ${id}` / `${n} players · ${n} kills` (English), plus the mobile drawer's `aria-label="Navigation menu"` / `"Close menu"` and the toast region's `aria-label="Notifications"`. French, Spanish and Ukrainian users get mixed-language UI and screen readers read English labels.
findings.fix: Replace with TranslationKeys. Add an ESLint rule (or a vitest check) that fails on string literals passed to toasts.*(...), `aria-label="..."` and `.set('...')` of error signals in features/**.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked and confirmed: 'Seleziona una build o uno slot primario.', 'Ruolo extra aggiunto al roster.', 'Member added to the event.', 'Starting now', 'Failed to copy link.', 'Item saved', 'Incantesimi Selezionati', 'Nessun equipaggiamento', and the English aria-labels in shell.ts:93/98. Cosmetic i18n gap.

findings.title: Accessibility gaps against the AGENTS.md 'must pass AXE / WCAG AA' rule: no per-route titles, low-contrast tertiary text, sub-12px text, modal drawer without focus management
findings.description: 1) app.routes.ts defines no `title` on any route and no code uses the Title service, so every page is 'Weaklings' (WCAG 2.4.2; also useless browser history/tabs). 2) `--color-text-disabled` is #707985 on #1d2026 in dark (3.7:1) and #6a7282 on #f5f4f0 in light (4.4:1), but it is used 82 times for real information (priority badges, labels, '—' placeholders) at 9–10px, e.g. admin-permissions.ts:284 and :378; the legacy token block (muted #7c8195 on #2b2c36 = 3.6:1) still applies wherever the Zed override does not redefine a token. 3) 161 occurrences of `text-[9px|10px|11px]` produce unreadable densities on small screens, despite DESIGN.md allowing micro copy only for tags. 4) The mobile nav drawer is `role=dialog aria-modal` but built from a plain div: no focus trap, no focus restore to the menu button, Esc handled only at document level. 5) The login language toast (login.ts:140) is invisible because the toast region lives in Topbar, which does not exist on public routes.
findings.fix: Add `title: () => translate.t(...)` to each route (and a TitleStrategy that appends the tenant name). Raise disabled/tertiary tokens to ≥4.5:1 and stop using disabled for information. Add a minimum `--text-micro: 0.75rem` and lint arbitrary px font sizes. Reuse the native-dialog Dialog (or `inert` + focus restore) for the drawer. Move the toast region to the root App component.
findings.verify_note: No `title` in app.routes.ts and no Title or TitleStrategy use. 170 text-[9|10|11px] occurrences. The mobile drawer is role=dialog aria-modal with no focus code in shell.ts. The contrast figures are close to my own estimate (about 3.6:1 in dark). I did not verify the login toast point.

findings.title: Alliance tenants have no dedicated experience: guild-style dashboard, flat tenant rail, no per-guild scope
findings.description: Alliance awareness is scattered: `tenant_kind === 'alliance'` is checked only in guards, nav.ts filtering (hiddenForAlliance on a few items), bank.ts, split-detail and admin-alliance. dashboard.ts never branches on tenant kind, so an alliance hub shows the personal guild dashboard and fires progression/me, users/me/metrics and the guild event queries (the 'season' page is hidden for alliances but the dashboard still asks for progression, producing the 'failed' state). TenantRail renders a flat `TenantChoice[]` (auth/tenants) with no grouping of an alliance and its member guilds, and reloads the list on each mount (including each mobile-drawer open and collapse toggle). Events, splits, users and comps lists have no per-guild filter or column on alliance tenants; only the bank has one. Given goal (3) that alliances sync everything with member guilds, the UI offers no way to see what is shared, from which guild, or its sync status.
findings.fix: Create an alliance landing page backed by `GET /api/alliances/me/overview` (member guilds with last sync, pending mirrors, aggregate bank, upcoming mass per guild). Group the tenant rail as alliance → guilds. Add a reusable `GuildScopeFilter` and a `guild_name` column to alliance-mode DataTables, driven by one `isAlliance` signal in a shared `TenantContext` service instead of ad-hoc profile reads.
findings.verify_note: The dashboard does not branch on alliance (no alliance or tenant_kind reference in dashboard.ts), and the tenant rail is a flat list. But the finding undercounts how many places check tenant_kind: events, splits, comps, admin pages and the sidebar do. The claim that an alliance dashboard hits a failed progression state is unverified. It is a UX gap against goal 3, not a traced defect.

findings.title: Realtime exists only for the event roster; every other page goes stale after changes made from Discord or another officer
findings.description: The only push channel is the per-event roster WebSocket, which already carries invalidation-only messages. Everything else loads once on enter: events list, splits, regears, bank, admin queues. The only polling is the unread badge (30s). battles.ts runs a 1-second interval for a 5-minute countdown even when the tab is hidden (no visibilityState check, unlike the other timers). When a Discord command signs up, approves a regear or completes a split, the web UI stays wrong until the user reloads, which reads as 'sync doesn't work' even when the data is right.
findings.fix: Generalize the roster socket into one tenant-scoped invalidation channel (`/api/live` emitting `{topic, id, version}`), and let the data layer from frontend-6 invalidate keys on message. Gate timers on `document.visibilityState`.
findings.verify_note: The only WebSocket user is realtime-roster.service. The only polling is notification unread (30s, with a visibility check). Correction: battles.ts:723-735 is an auto-refresh countdown that reloads the list every 5 minutes, so battles are not stale; it just has no visibility gate. Low.

findings.title: Hand-copied API types and duplicated helpers: 3,191-line api.models.ts, three AllianceShareStatus copies, ~40 formatAmount/formatDate variants
findings.description: Backend DTOs are re-typed by hand in the frontend (3,191 lines) and again in the bot (types.ts), with no OpenAPI codegen even though the backend publishes openapi.rs; field drift is silent (e.g. `fee`, `net_value` optional guesses). The share/unshare/status flow is copied into split-detail, comp-detail and comp-build-detail with a private `AllianceShareStatus` interface in each. Number/date/compact-silver formatters are redefined in ~30 components with different locale and rounding behavior (`formatCompactSilver` in dashboard.ts vs formatCompact in bank/admin/fights; fight-trends uses `undefined` locale), 61 raw `toLocale*String` calls, and `Intl.NumberFormat` is constructed per call.
findings.fix: Generate api.models.ts (and the bot types) from the backend OpenAPI document in CI. Extract `ShareWithAllianceButton`, a `MoneyPipe`/`CompactNumberPipe`/`DateTimePipe` (locale from TranslateService, cached Intl formatters) and delete the per-component copies.
findings.verify_note: api.models.ts is 3191 lines. There are three private AllianceShareStatus interfaces (split-detail, comp-detail, comp-build-detail). 61 raw toLocale*String calls. backend/src/openapi.rs exists, so codegen is possible. Maintainability only.

findings.title: Inconsistent primitives: raw selects/tables/confirm() next to shared components; no NgOptimizedImage; silent failures
findings.description: 45 raw `
findings.fix: Ship `FormField`, `ConfirmDialog` (service), `DataTable` simple mode and `Avatar/ItemIcon` (NgOptimizedImage with width/height) as the only allowed controls; add an eslint-plugin-angular-template rule banning raw `<select>`, `<table>` and `confirm(`. Replace caps with server-side search in SearchableSelect.
findings.verify_note: 54 raw <select> and 27 raw <table> exist. admin-alliance.ts:347 and :444 use globalThis.confirm. NgOptimizedImage has 0 non-spec uses despite AGENTS.md requiring it. events.ts:821 is an empty catch that leaves the stats at 0. event-detail.ts:5097 only console.errors. Style and consistency nits.

logic_questions: Event time entry: should event Mass/Start times be entered and displayed in the guild's configured `discord_event_timezone` (what Discord already does), in the viewer's browser timezone (what the web does now), or always UTC? Options: (a) tenant timezone everywhere with the zone label shown next to every input, (b) browser timezone everywhere including the bot via Discord's own timestamp tokens, (c) UTC with explicit conversion hints.

Alliance landing: what should an alliance-tenant member see on /dashboard and in the lists? Options: (a) aggregated view across all member guilds with a guild filter and a per-row guild column, (b) only alliance-owned records plus explicit shared/mirrored items, (c) a hub page of per-guild cards with sync health that links into each guild tenant.

Alliance mirror failures: who is allowed to retry a failed event mirror or alliance split distribution from the web (alliance officers only, source-guild officers, or member-guild officers), and should retries and statuses also be offered as Discord buttons for parity?

Bank withdrawals: should members cherry-pick individual credit rows to withdraw (current web behavior, requires client-side subset logic) or request an amount that the backend fulfils FIFO? The Discord flow almost certainly cannot do row-picking, so this decides whether the two surfaces can share one endpoint.

SSR: is there any requirement for server rendering (SEO, link previews, first paint) given that every route is auth-gated? If not, should the app be shipped as a static SPA behind the reverse proxy, which removes the login-flash/hydration bugs and the Nitro API proxy hop?

Design direction: should the Zed light-first theme in DESIGN.md/the redesign plan be the final target (light default, serif headings, 2px radii), or is the Discord-style dark theme the real brand? The code currently ships both and defaults to dark; the team needs one before more screens are touched.

Language: should the UI language be a server-side profile preference shared by web and bot (so one choice applies in Discord messages and the web), or stay a per-browser localStorage setting? This also decides whether non-English dictionaries can be lazy-loaded from the profile.

Freshness model: is it acceptable for web list pages to update only on navigation/refresh (current), or must events, splits, regears and bank queues update live when something changes from Discord? If live, should it be one WebSocket invalidation channel (extending the roster socket) or periodic polling?
